author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.1 Dhritarashtra said What did my people and the sons of Pandu do when they had assembled
together eager for battle on the holy plain of Kurukshetra, O Sanjaya.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.2. Sanjaya said Having seen the army of the Pandavas drawn up in battle-array,
King Duryodhana then approached his teacher (Drona) and spoke these words.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.3. "Behold, O Teacher! this mighty army of the sons of Pandu,
arrayed by the son of Drupada, thy wise disciple.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.4. Here are heroes, mighty archers, eal in battle to Bhima
and Arjuna, Yoyudhana (Satyaki), Virata and Drupada, of the great car (mighty
warriors).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.5. "Dhrishtaketu, chekitana and the valiant king of Kasi, Purujit
and Kuntibhoja and Saibya, the best men.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.6. "The strong Yodhamanyu and the brave Uttamaujas, the son
of Subhadra (Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadra and Arjuna), and the sons of
Draupadi, all of great chariots (great heroes).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.8. "Thyself and Bhishma, and Karna and also Kripa, the victorious
in war, Asvatthama, Vikarna, and also Bhurisrava, the son of Somadatta.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.9. "And also many other heroes who are ready to give up their
lives for my sake, armed with various weapons and missiles, all well-skilled
in battle.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.10. "This army of ours marshalled by Bhishma is insufficient,
whereas that army of theirs marshelled by Bhima is sufficient.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.11. "Therefore do ye all, stationed in your respective positions,
in the several divisions of the army, protect Bhishma alone."

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.12. His glorious grandsire (Bhishma), the oldest of the Kauravas,
in order to cheer Duryodhana, now roared like a lion, and blew his conch.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.13. Then (following Bhishma), conches and kettledrums, tabors,
drums and cow horns blared forth ite suddenly (from the Kaurava side)
and the sound was tremendous.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.14. Then, also, Madhava (Krishna) and the son of Pandu (Arjuna),
seated in the magnificent chariot, yoked with white horses, blew divine
conches.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.15. Hrishikesha blew the Panchajanya and Arjuna blew the Devadatta
and Bhima (the wolf-bellied), the doer of terrible deeds, blew the great
conch Paundra.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.16. The king Yodhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya;
Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and the Manipushpaka.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.17. The king of Kasi, an exellent archer, Sikhandi, the mighty
car-warrior, Dhrishtadyumna and Virata and Satyaki, the unconered.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.18. Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O Lord of the earth, and
the son of Subhadra, the mighty-armed, blew their conches separately.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.19. That tumultuous sound rent the hearts of (the members of)
Dhritarashtra's party, making both the heaven and the earth resound.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.20. Then, seeing the people of Dhritarashtra’s party standing
arrayed and the discharge of weapons about to begin, Arjuna, the son of
Pandu, whose ensign was a monkey, took up his bow and said the following
to Krishna, O Lord of the earth.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.21 Arjuna said In the middle between the two armies, place my chariot,
O krishna, so that I may behold those who stand here desirous to fight,
and know with whom I must fight, when the battle is about to commence.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.22. Arjuna said In the middle between the two armies, place my chariot,
O krishna, so that I may behold those who stand here desirous to fight,
and know with whom I must fight, when the battle is about to commence.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.23. For I desire to observe those who are assembled here to fight,
wishing to please in battle the evil-minded Duryodhana (the son of Dhritarashtra).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.24. Sanjaya said Thus addressed by Arjuna, Krishna, having stationed that
best of chariots, O Dhritarashtra, in the midst of the two armies.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.25. In front of Bhishma and Drona, and all the rulers of the
earth, said: "O Arjuna (son of Pritha), behold these Kurus gathered together."

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.26. Then, Arjuna (son of Pritha) saw there (in the armies) stationed,
fathers and grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons
and friends too.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.27. (He saw) fathers-in-law and friends also in both the armies.
The son of Kunti, Arjuna, seeing all those kinsmen thus standing arrayed,
spoke this, sorrowfully filled with deep pity.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.28. Arjuna said Seeing these, my kinsmen, O krishna, arrayed, eager to fight.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.29. My limbs fail and my mouth is parched, my body ivers and
my hair stands on end.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.30. The (bow) Gandiva slips from my hand, and also my skins burns
all over; I am unable even to stand and my mind is reeling, as it were.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.31. And I see adverse omens, O Kesava. I do not see any good
in killing my kinsmen in battle.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.32. I desire not victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures.
Of what avail is dominion to us, O Krishna, or pleasures or even life?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.33. Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures,
stand here in battle, having renounced life and wealth.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.34. Teachers, fathers, sons and also grandfathers, maternal uncles,
fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives,-

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.35. These I do not wish to kill, though they kill me, O Krishna,
even for the sake of dominion over the three worlds; leave alone killing
them for the sake of the earth.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.36. By killing these sons of Dhritarashtra, what pleasure can
be ours, O Janardana? Only sin will accrue to us from killing these felons.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.37. Therefore, we should not kill the sons of Dhritarashtra,
our relatives; for how can we be happy by killing our own people, O Madhava
(Krishna)?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.38. Though they, with intelligence overpowered by greed, see
no evil in the destruction of families, and no sin in hostility to friends,

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.39. Why should not we who clearly see evil in the destruction
of families, learn to turn away from this sin, O Janardana (Krishna)?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.40. In the destruction of a family, the immemorial religious
rites of that family perish; on the destruction of spirituality, impiety,
indeed, overcomes the whole family.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.41. By the prevalence of impiety, O Krishna, the women of
the family become corrupt; and , women being corrupted, O Varshenya (descendant
of Vrishni), there arises intermingling of castes.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.42. Confusion of castes leads to hell the slayers of the family,
for their forefathers fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-ball and
water (libations).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.43. By these evil deeds of the destroyers of the family, which
cause confusion of castes, the eternal religious rites of the caste and
the family are destroyed.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.44. We have heard, O Janardana, that inevitable is the dwelling
for an unknown period in hell for those men in whose families the religious
practices have been destroyed.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.45. Alas! We are involved in a great sin, in that we are
prepared to kill our kinsmen, through greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.46. If the sons of Dhritarashtra with weapons in hand should
slay me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that would be better for me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.47. Sanjaya said Having thus spoken in the midst of the battlefield, Arjuna,
casting away his bow and arrow, sat down on the seat of the chariot with
his mind overwhelmed with sorrow.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.1 Sanjaya said To him who was thus overcome with pity and who was despondent, with eyes full of tears and agitated, Madhusudana (the destroyer of Madhu) or Krishna spoke these words.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.2 The Blessed Lord said Whence is this perilous strait come upon thee, this dejection which is unworthy of you, disgraceful, and which will close the gates of heaven upon you, O Arjuna?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.3 Yield not to impotence, O Arjuna, son of Pritha. It does not befit thee. Cast off this mean weakness of the heart! Stand up, O scorcher of the foes!

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.4 Arjuna said How, O Madhusudana, shall I fight in battle with arrows against Bhishma and Drona, who are fit to be worshipped, O destroyer of enemies?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.5 Better it is, indeed, in this world to accept alms than to slay the most noble teachers. But if I kill them, even in this world all my enjoyments of wealth and fulfilled desires will be stained with (their) blood.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.6 I can hardly tell which will be better, that we should coner them or that they should coner us. Even the sons of Dhritarashtra, after slaying whom we do not wish to live, stand facing us.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.7 My heart is overpowered by the taint of pity; my mind is confused as to duty. I ask Thee: Tell me decisively what is good for me. I am Thy disciple. Instruct me who has taken refuge in Thee.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.8 I do not see that it would remove this sorrow that burns up my senses, even if I should attain prosperous and unrivalled dominion on earth or lordship over the gods.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.9 Sanjaya said Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha (the Lord of the senses), Arjuna (the coneror of sleep), the destroyer of foes, said to Krishna, "I will not fight" and became silent.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.10 To him who was despondent in the midst of the two armies, Krishna, as if smiling, O Bharata, spoke these words.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.11 The Blessed Lord said Thou hast grieved for those that should not be grieved for, yet thou speakest words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the living nor for the dead.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.12 Nor at any time indeed was I not, nor thou, nor these rulers of men, nor verily shall we ever cease to be hereafter.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.13 Just as in this body the embodied (soul) passes into childhood, youth and old age, so also does it pass into another body; the firm man does not grieve thereat.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.14 The contacts of the senses with the objects, O son of Kunti, which cause heat and cold, pleasure and pain, have a beginning and an end; they are impermanent; endure them bravely, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.15 That firm man whom, surely, these afflict not, O chief among men, to whom pleasure and pain are the same, is fit for attaining immortality.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.16 The unreal hath no being; there is non-being of the real; the truth about both has been seen by the knowers of the Truth (or the seers of the Essence).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.17 Know that to be indestructible, by Which all this is pervaded. None can cause the destruction of That, the Imperishable.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.18 These bodies of the embodied Self, Which is eternal, indestructible and immeasurable, are said to have an end. Therefore fight, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.19 He who takes the Self to be the slayer and he who thinks It is slain, neither of them ï1knowsï1. It slays not, nor is It slain.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.20 It is not born, nor does It ever die; after having been, It again ceases not to be; unborn, eternal, changeless and ancient, It is not killed when the body is killed.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.21 Whosoever knows It to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and inexhaustible, how can that man slay, O Arjuna, or cause to be slain?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.22 Just as a man casts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so also the embodied Self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others which are new.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.23 Weapons cut It not, fire burns It not, water wets It not, wind dries It not.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.24 This Self cannot be cut, burnt, wetted, nor dried up. It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable and ancient.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.25 This (Self) is said to be unmanifested, unthinkable and unchangeable. Therefore, knowing This to be such, thou shouldst not grieve.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.26 But even if thou thinkest of It as being constantly born and constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed, thou shouldst not grieve.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.27 For certain is death for the born, and certain is birth for the dead; therefore, over the inevitable thou shouldst not grieve.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.28 Beings are unmanifested in their beginning, manifested in their middle state, O Arjuna, and unmanifested again in their end. What is there to grieve about?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.29 One sees This (the Self) as a wonder; another speaks of It as a wonder; another hears of It as a wonder; yet having heard, none understands It at all.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.30 This, the Indweller in the body of everyone, is ever indestructible, O Arjuna; therefore, thou shouldst not grieve for any creature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.31 Further, having regard to thy duty, shouldst not waver, for there is nothing higher for a Kshatriya than a righteous war.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.32 Happy are the Kshatriyas, O Arjuna! who are called upon to fight in such a battle that comes of itself as an open door to heaven.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.33 But if thou wilt not fight this righteous war, then having abandoned thine own duty and fame, thou shalt incur sin.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.34 People, too, will recount thy everlasting dishonour; and to one who has been honoured, dishonour is worse than death.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.35 The great car-warriors will think that thou hast withdrawn from the battle through fear; and thou wilt be lightly held by them who have thought much of thee.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.36 Thy enemies also, cavilling at thy power, will speak many abusive words. What is more painful than this?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.37 Slain, thou wilt obtain heaven; victorious, thou wilt enjoy the earth; therefore, stand up, O son of Kunti, resolved to fight.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.38 Having made pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat the same, engage thou in battle for the sake of battle; thus thou shalt not incur sin.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.39 This, which has been taught to thee, is wisdon concerning Sankhya. Now listen to wisdom concerning Yoga, endowed with which, O Arjuna, thou shalt cast off the bonds of action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.40 In this there is no loss of effort, nor is there any harm (production of contrary results or transgression). Even a little of this knowledge (even a little practice of this Yoga) protects one from great fear.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.41 Here, O joy of the Kurus, there is but a single one-pointed determination; many-branched and endless are the thoughts of the irresolute.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.42 Flowery speech is uttered by the unwise, taking pleasure in the eulogising words of the Vedas, O Arjuna, saying, "There is nothing else."

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.43 Full of desires, having heaven as their goal, (they utter speech which is directed to ends) leading to new births as the result of their works, and prescribe various methods abounding in specific actions, for the attainment of pleasure and power.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.44 For those who are attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are drawn away by such teaching, ï1thatï1 determinate reason is not formed which is steadily bent on meditation and Samadhi (superconscious state).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.45 The Vedas deal with the three attributes (of Nature); be thou above these three attributes. O Arjuna, free yourself from the pairs of opposites, and ever remain in the ality of Sattva (goodness), freed from (the thought of) acisition and preservation, and be established in the Self.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.46 To the Brahmana who has known the Self, all the Vedas are of as much use as is a reservoir of water in a place where there is a flood.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.47 Thy right is to work only, but never with its fruits; let not the fruits of action be thy motive, nor let thy attachment be to inaction.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.48 Perform action, O Arjuna, being steadfast in Yoga, abandoning attachment and balanced in success and failure. Evenness of mind is called Yoga.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.49 Far lower than the Yoga of wisdon is action, O Arjuna. Seek thou refuge in wisdom; wretched are they whose motive is the fruit.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.50 Endowed with wisdom (evenness of mind), one casts off in this life both good and evil deeds; therefore, devote thyself to Yoga; Yoga is skill in action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.51 The wise, possessed of knowledge, having abandoned the fruits of their actions, and being freed from the fetters of birth, go to the place which is beyond all evil.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.52 When thy intellect crosses beyond the mire of delusion, then thou shalt attain to indifference as to what has been heard and what has yet to be heard.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.53 When thy intellect, which is perplexed by the Veda text, which thou hast read, shall stand immovable and steady in the Self, then thou shalt attain Self-realisation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.54 Arjuna said What, O Krishna, is the description of him who has steady wisdom, and is merged in the superconscious state? How does one of steady wisdom speak, how does he sit, how does he walk?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.55 The Blessed Lord said When a man completely casts off, O Arjuna, all the desires of the mind and is satisfied in the Self by the Self, then is he said to be one of steady wisdom.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.56 He whose mind is not shaken by adversity, who does not hanker after pleasures, and is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.57 He who is everywhere without attachment, on meeting with anything good or bad, who neither rejoices not hastes, his wisdom is fixed.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.58 When, like the tortoise which withdraws on all sides its limbs, he withdraws his senses from the sense-objects, then his wisdom becomes steady.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.59 The objects of the senses turn away from the abstinent man leaving the longing (behind); but his longing also turns away on seeing the Supreme.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.60 The turbulent senses, O Arjuna, do violently carry away the mind of a wise man though he be striving (to control them).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.61 Having restrained them all he should sit steadfast, intent on Me; his wisdom is steady whose senses are under control.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.62 When a man thinks of the objects, attachment for them arises; from attachment desire is born; from desire anger arises.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.63 From anger comes delusion; from delusion loss of memory; from loss of memory the destruction of discrimination; from the destruction of discrimination he perishes.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.64 But the self-controlled man, moving among the objects with the senses under restraint and free from attraction and repulsion, attains to peace.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.65 In that peace all pains are destroyed; for the intellect of the tranil-minded soon becomes steady.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.66 There is no knowledge of the Self to the unsteady and to the unsteady no meditation is possible, and to the unmeditative there can be no peace, and to the man who has no peace, how can there be happiness?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.67 For the mind, which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, carries away his discrimination, as the wind (carries away) a boat on the waters.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.68 Therefore, O mighty-armed Arjuna, his knowledge is steady whose senses are completely restrained from sense-objects.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.69 That which is night to all beings, in that the self-controlled man is awake; when all beings are awake, that is night for the Muni (sage) who sees.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.70 He attains peace into whom all desires enter as waters enter the ocean which, filled from all sides, remains unmoved; but not the man who is full of desires.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.71 That man attains peace who, abandoning all desires, moves about without longing, without the sense of mine and without egoism.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.72 This is the Brahmic seat (eternal state), O son of Pritha. Attaining to this, none is deluded. Being established therein, even at the end of life, one attains to oneness with Brahman.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.1 Arjuna said If Thou thinkest that knowledge is superior to action, O Krishna, why then, O Kesava, dost Thou ask me to engage in this terrible action?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.2 With this apparently perplexing speech, Thou confusest, as it were, my understanding; therefore tell me that one way for certain by which I may attain bliss.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.3 The Blessed Lord said In this world there is a twofold path, as I said before, O sinless one; the path of knowledge of the Sankhyas and the path of action of the Yogins.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.4 Not by non-performance of actions does man reach actionlessness; nor by mere renunciation does he attain to perfection.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.5 Verily none can ever remain for even a moment without performing action; for everyone is made to act helplessly indeed by the alities born of Nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.6 He who, restraining the organs of action, sits thinking of the sense-objects in mind, he of deluded understanding is called a hypocrite.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.7 But whosoever, controlling the senses by the mind, O Arjuna, engages himself in Karma Yoga with the organs of action, without attachment, he excels.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.8 Do thou perform (thy) bounden duty, for action is superior to inaction and even the maintenance of the body would not be possible for thee by inaction.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.9 The world is bound by actions other than those performed for the sake of sacrifice; do thou, therefore, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), perform action for that sake (for sacrifice alone), free from attachment.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.10 The Creator, having in the beginning (of creation) created mankind together with sacrifice, said, "By this shall ye propagate; let this be the milch cow of your desires (the cow which yields all the desired objects)."

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.11 With this do ye nourish the gods and may those gods nourish you; thus nourishing one another, ye shall attain to the highest good.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.12 The gods, nourished by the sacrifice, will give you the desired objects. So, he who enjoys the objects given by the gods without offering (in return) to them, is verily a thief.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.13 The righteous who eat the remnants of the sacrifice are freed from all sins; but those sinful ones who cook food (only) for their own sake verily eat sin.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.14 From food come forth beings; from rain food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain and sacrifice is born of action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.15 Know thou that action comes from Brahma and Brahma comes from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading (Brahma) ever rests in sacrifice.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.16 He who does not follow here the wheel thus set revolving, who is of sinful life, rejoicing in the senses, he lives in vain, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.17 But for that man who rejoices only in the Self, who is satisfied with the Self and who is content in the Self alone, verily there is nothing to do.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.18 For him there is no interest whatever in what is done or what is not done; nor does he depend on any being for any object.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.19 Therefore without attachment, do thou always perform action which should be done; for by performing action without attachment man reaches the Supreme.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.20 Janaka and others attained perfection verily by action only; even with a view to the protection of the masses thou shouldst perform action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.21 Whatsoever a great man does, that the other men also do; whatever he sets up as the standard, that the world (mankind) follows.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.22 There is nothing in the three worlds, O Arjuna, that should be done by Me, nor is there anything unattained that should be attained; yet I engage Myself in action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.23 For, should I not ever engage Myself in action, unwearied, men would in every way follow My path, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.24 These worlds would perish if I did not perform action; I should be the author of confusion of castes and destruction of these beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.25 As the ignorant men act from attachment to action, O Bharata (Arjuna), so should the wise act without attachment, wishing the welfare of the world.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.26 Let no wise man unsettle the mind of ignorant people who are attached to action; he should engage them in all actions, himself fulfilling them with devotion.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.27 All actions are wrought in all cases by the alities of Nature only. He whose mind is deluded by egoism thinks, "I am the doer."

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.28 But he who knows the Truth, O mighty-armed (Arjuna), about the divisions of the alities and (their) functions, knowing that the Gunas as senses move amidst the Gunas as the sense-objects, is not attached.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.29 Those deluded by the alities of Nature are attached to the functions of the alities. The man of perfect knowledge should not unsettle the foolish one who is of imperfect knowledge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.30 Renouncing all actions in Me, with the mind centred in the Self, free from hope and egoism, and from (mental) fever, do thou fight.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.31 Those men who constantly practise this teaching of Mine with faith and without cavilling, they too are freed from actions.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.32 But those who carp at My teaching and do not practise it, deluded of all knowledge, and devoid of discrimination, know them to be doomed to destruction.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
3.33 Even a wise man acts in accordance with his own nature; beings will follow Nature; what can
restraint do?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.34 Attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses; let none come under their sway; for, they are his foes.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.35 Better is one's own duty, though devoid of merit than the duty of another well discharged. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with fear (is productive of danger).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.36 Arjuna said But impelled by what does man commit sin, though against his wishes, O Varshneya (Krishna), constrained as it were, by force?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.37 The Blessed Lord said It is desire, it is anger both of the ality of Rajas, all-devouring, all-sinful; know this as the foe here (in this world).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.38 As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dust, and as an embryo by the amnion, so is this enveloped by that.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.39 O Arjuna, wisdom is enveloped by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is unappeasable as fire.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.40 The senses, the mind and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these it deludes the embodied by veiling his wisdom.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.41 Therefore, O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna), controlling the senses first, do thou kill this sinful thing, the destroyer of knowledge and realisation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.42 They say that the senses are superior (to the body); superior to the senses is the mind; superior to the mind is the intellect; one who is superior even to the intellect is He (the Self).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.43 Thus knowing Him Who is superior to the intellect and restraining the self by the Self, slay thou, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the enemy in the form of desire, hard to coner.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.1 The Blessed Lord said I taught this imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan; he told it to Manu; Manu proclaimed it to Ikshvaku.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.2 This, handed down thus in regular succession, the royal sages knew. This Yoga, by long lapse of time, has been lost here, O Parantapa (burner of the foes).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.3 That same ancient Yoga has been today taught to thee by Me, for thou art My devotee and My friend; it is the supreme secret.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.4 Arjuna said Later on was Thy birth, and prior to it was the birth of Vivasvan (the Sun); how am I to understand that Thou taughtest this Yoga in the beginning?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.5 The Blessed Lord said Many births of Mine have passed as well as of thine, O Arjuna; I know them all but thou knowest not, O Parantapa (scorcher of foes).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.6 Though I am unborn, of imperishable nature, and though I am the Lord of all beings, yet, governing My own Nature, I am born by My own Maya.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.7 Whenever there is decline of righteousness, O Arjuna, and rise of unrighteousness, then I manifest Myself.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.8 For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked and for the establishment of righteousness, I am born in every age.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.9 He who thus know, in their true light, My divine birth and action, having abandoned the body, is not born again, he comes to Me, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.10 Freed from attachment, fear and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, purified by the fire of knowledge, many have attained to My Being.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.11 In whatever way men approach Me even so do I reward them; My path do men tread in all ways, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.12 Those who long for success in action in this world sacrifice to the gods; because success is ickly attained by men through action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.13 The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of Guna and Karma; though I am the author thereof know Me as non-doer and immutable.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.14 Actions do not taint Me, nor have I a desire for the fruit of actions. He who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.15 Having known this, the ancient seekers after freedom also performed action; therefore do thou also perform action, as did the ancients in days of yore.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.16 What is action? What is inaction? As to this even the wise are confused. Therefore I shall teach thee such action (the nature of action and inaction) by knowing which thou shalt be liberated from the evil (of Samsara, the wheel of birth and death).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
4.17 For verily (the true nature) of action (enjoined by the scriptures) should be known, also (that)
of forbidden (or unlawful) action, and of inaction; hard to understand is the nature (path) of action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.18 He who seeth inaction in action and action in inaction, he is wise among men; he is a Yogi and performer of all actions.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.19 He whose undertakings are all devoid of desires and (selfish) purposes and whose actions have been burnt by the fire of knowledge, him the wise call a sage.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.20 Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of the action, ever content, depending on nothing, he does not do anything though engaged in activity.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.21 Without hope and with the mind and the self controlled, having abandoned all covetousness, doing mere bodily action, he incurs no sin.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.22 Content with what comes to him without effort, free from the pairs of opposites and envy, even-minded in success and failure, though acting, he is not bound.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.23 To one who is devoid of attchment, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, who works for the sake of sacrifice (for the sake of God), the whole action is dissolved.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.24 Brahman is the oblation; Brahman is the melted butter (ghee); by Brahman is the oblation poured into the fire of Brahman; Brahman verily shall be reached by him who always sees Brahman in action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.25 Some Yogies perform sacrifice to the gods alone; while others (who have realised the Self) offer the self as sacrifice by the Self in the fire of Brahman alone.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.26 Some again offer the organ of hearing and other senses as sacrifice in the fire of restraint; others offer sound and other objects of the senses as sacrifice in the fire of the senses.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.27 Others again sacrifice all the functions of the senses and those of the breath (vital energy or Prana) in the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint kindled by knowledge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.28 Others again offer wealth, austerity and Yoga as sacrifice, while the ascetics of self-restraint and rigid vows offer study of scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.29 Others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming, and the incoming in the outgoing, restraining the course of the outgoing and the incoming breaths, solely absorbed in the restraint of the breath.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.30 Others who regulate their diet offer life-breaths in life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins are destroyed by sacrifice.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.31 Those who eat the remnants of the sacrifice, which are like nectar, go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for the man who does not perform sacrifice; how then can he have the other, O Arjuna?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.32 Thus, manifold sacrifices are spread out before Brahman (literally) at the mouth or face of Brahman). Know them all as born of action and thus knowing, thou shalt be liberated.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.34 Know That by long prostration, by estion and by service; the wise who have realised the Truth will instruct thee in (that) knowledge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.35 Knowing ï1thatï1 thou shalt not, O Arjuna, again get deluded like this; and by that thou shalt see all beings in thy Self and also in Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.36 Even if thou art the most sinful of all sinners, yet thou shalt verily cross all sins by the raft of knowledge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.37 As the blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ashes.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.38 Verily, there is no purifier in this world like knowledge. He who is perfected in Yoga finds it in the Self in time.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.39 The man who is full of faith, who is devoted to it, and who has subdued the senses obtains (this) knowledge; and having obtained the knowledge he attains at once to the supreme peace.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.40 The ignorant the faithless, the doubting self goes to destruction; there is neither this world nor the other, nor happiness for the doubting.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.41 He who has renounced actions by Yoga, whose doubts are rent asunder by knowledge, and who is self-possessed actions do not bind him, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.42 Therefore with the sword of the knowledge (of the Self) cut asunder the doubt of the self born of ignorance, residing in thy heart, and take refuge in Yoga. Arise, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.1 Arjuna said Renunciation of actions, O Krishna, Thou praisest, and again Yoga. Tell me conclusively that which is the better of the two.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.2 The Blessed Lord said Renunciation and the Yoga of action both lead to the highest bliss; but of the two, the Yoga of action is superior to the renunciation of action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.3 He should be known as a perpertual Sannyasi who neither hates nor desires; for, free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he is easily set free from bondage.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.4 Children, not the wise, speak of knowledge and the Yoga of action or the performance of action as though they are distinct and different; he who is truly established in one obtains the fruits of both.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.5 That place which is reached by the Sankhyas or the Jnanis is reached by the Yogis (Karma Yogis). He sees, who sees knowledge and the performance of action (Karma Yoga) as one.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.6 But renunciation, O mighty-armed Arjuna, is hard to attain without Yoga; the Yoga-harmonised sage ickly goes to Brahman.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.7 He who is devoted to the path of action, whose mind is ite pure, who has conered the self, who has subdued his senses and who realises his Self as the Self in all beings, though acting, is not tainted.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.8 "I do nothing at all," thus would the harmonised knower of Truth think seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, breathing.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.9 Speaking, letting go, seizing, opening and closing the eyes convinced that the senses move among the sense-objects.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending

alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.12 Having closed all the gates, confined the mind in the heart and fixed the life-breath in the head, engaged in the practice of concentration.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.13 Uttering the one-syllabled Om the Brahman and remembering Me, he who departs, leaving the body, attains to the Supreme Goal.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.14 I am easily attainable by that ever-steadfast Yogi who constantly and daily remembers Me (for a long time), not thinking of anything else (with a single mind or one-pointed mind), O Partha (Arjuna).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
8.15 Having attained Me these great souls do not again take birth (here) which is the place of pain
and is non-eternal: they have reached the highest perfection (liberation).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.16 (All) the worlds including the world of Brahma are subject to return again, O Arjuna; but he who reaches Me, O son of Kunti, has no rirth.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.17 Those people who know the day of Brahma which is of a duration of a thousand Yugas (ages) and the night which is also of a thousand Yugas duration, they know day and night.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.18 From the Unmanifested all the manifested (worlds) proceed at the coming of the 'day'; at the coming of the 'night' they dissolve verily into ï1thatï1 alone which is called the Unmanifested.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.19 This same multitude of beings, being born again and again, is dissolved, helplessly, O Arjuna (into the Unmanifested) at the coming of the night and comes forth at the coming of the day.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.20 But verily there exists, higher than this Unmanifested, another unmanifested Eternal, which is not destroyed when all beings are destroyed.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.21 What is called the Unmanifested and the Imperishable, That they say is the highest goal. They who reach It do not return (to this Samsara). That is My highest abode (place or state).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.22 That highest Purusha, O Arjuna, is attainable by unswerving devotion to Him alone within Whom all beings dwell and by Whom all this is pervaded.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.23 Now I will tell thee, O chief of Bharatas, the times departing at which the Yogis will return or not return.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.24 Fire, light daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path of the sun (the northern solstice) departing then (by these) men who know Brahman go to Brahman.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.25 Attaining to the lunar light by smoke, night time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path of the sun (the southern solstice), the Yogi returns.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.26 The bright and the dark paths of the world are verily thought to be eternal; by the one (the bright path) a man goes not to return and by the other (the dark path) he returns.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.27 Knowing these paths, O Arjuna, no Yogi is deluded; therefore at all times be steadfast in Yoga.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.28 Whatever fruit of merit is declared (in the scriptures) to accrue from (the study of) the Vedas, (the performance of) sacrifices, (the practice of) austerities, and gifts beyond all this goes the Yogi, having known this; and he attains to the Supreme Primeval (first or ancient) Abode.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.1 The Blessed Lord said I shall now declare to thee who does not cavil, the greatest secret, the knowledge combined with experience (Self-realisation). Having known this thou shalt be free evil.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.2 This is the kingl science, the kingly secret, the supreme purifier, realisable by direct intuitional knowledge, according to righteousness, very easy to perform and imperishable.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.3 Those who have no faith in this Dharma (knowledge of the Self), O Parantapa (Arjuna), return to the path of this world of death without attaining Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.4 All this world is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest aspect; all beings exist in Me, but I do not dwell in them.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.5 Nor do beings exist in Me (in reality); behold My divine Yoga, supporting all beings, but not dwelling in them, is My Self, the efficient cause of beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.6 As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, rests always in the ether, even so, know thou that all beings rest in Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.7 All beings, O Arjuna, go into My Nature at the end of a Kalpa; I send them forth again at the beginning of (the next) Kalpa.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.8 Animating My Nature, I again and again send forth all this multitude of beings, helpless by the force of the Nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.9 These acts do not bind Me, O Arjuna, sitting like one indifferent, unattached to those acts.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.10 Under Me as supervisor, Nature produces the moving and the unmoving; because of this, O Arjuna, the world revolves.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.11 Fools disregard Me, clad in human form, not knowing My higher Being as the great Lord of (all) beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.12 Of vain hopes, of vain actions, of vain knowledge and senseless, they verily are possessed of the deceitful nature of demons and undivine beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.13 But the great souls, O Arjuna, partaking of My divine nature, worship Me with a single mind (with the mind devoted to nothing else), knowing Me as the imperishable source of beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.14 Always glorifying Me, striving,firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion always steadfast.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.15 Others also sacrificing with the wisdom-sacrifice worship Me, the All-faced, as one, as distinct, and as manifold.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.16 I am the Kratu; I am the Yajna; I am the offering (food) to the manes; I am the medicinal herbs and all the plants; I am the Mantra; I am also the Ghee or the melted butter; I am the fire; I am the oblation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
9.17 I am the father of this world, the mother, the dispenser of the fruits of actions and the
grandfather; the (one) thing to be known, the purifier, the sacred monosyllable (Om), and also the Rik-, the Sama-and the Yajur-Vedas.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.18 I am the goal, the supporter, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the shelter, the friend, the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the treasure-house and the seed which is imperishable.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.19 (As the sun) I give heat; I withhold and send forth the rain; I am immortality and also death, existence and non-existence, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.20 The knowers of the three Vedas, the drinkers of Soma, purified of all sins, worshipping Me by sacrifices, pray for the way to heaven; they reach the holy world of the Lord of the gods and enjoy in heavn the divine pleasures of the gods.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.21 They, having enjoyed the vast heaven, enter the world of mortals when their merit is exhausted; thus abiding by the injunctions of the ï1threeï1 (Vedas) and desiring (objects of) desires, they attain to the state of going and returning.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.22 For those men who worship Me alone, thinking of no other, for those ever-united, I secure what is not already possessed and preserve what they already possess.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.23 Even those devotees who, endowed with faith, worship other gods, worship Me alone, O Arjuna, b the wrong method.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.24 (For) I alone am the enjoyer and also the Lord of all sacrifices; but they do not know Me in essence (in reality), and hence they fall (return to this mortal world).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.25 The worshippers of the gods go to them; to the manes go the ancestor-worshippers; to the deities who preside over the elements go their worshippers; but My devotees come to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.26 Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water that, so offered devotedly by the pure-minded, I accept.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.27 Whatever thou doest, whatever thou eatest, whatever thou offerest in sacrifice, whatever thou givest, whatever thou practisest as austerity, O Arjuna, do it as an offering unto Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.28 Thus shalt thou be freed from the bonds of actions yielding good and evil fruits; with the mind steadfast in the Yoga of renunciation, and liberated, thou shalt come unto Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.29 The same am I to all beings; to Me there is none hateful or dear; but those who worship Me with devotion are in Me and I am also in them.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.30 Even if the most sinful worships Me, with devotion to none else, he too should indeed by regarded as righteous for he has rightly resolved.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.31 Soon he becomes righteous and attains to eternal peace; O Arjuna, proclaim thou for certain that My devotee never perishes.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.32 For, taking refuge in Me, they also who, O Arjuna, may be of a sinful birth women, Vaisyas as well as Sudras attain the Supreme Goal.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.33 How much more (easily) then the hold Brahmins and devoted royal saints (attain the goal); having come to this impermanent and unhappy world, do thou worship Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.34 Fix thy mind on Me; by devoted to Me; sacrifice unto Me; bow down to Me; having thus united thy whole self to Me, taking Me as the supreme goal, thou shalt come unto Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.1 The Blessed Lord said Again, O mighty-armed Arjuna, listen to my supreme word which I will declare to thee who who art beloved, for thy welfare.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.2 Neither the hosts of the gods nor the great sages know My origin; for in every way I am the source of all the gods and the great sages.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.3 He who knows Me as unborn and beginningless, as the great Lord of the worlds, he, among mortals, is undeluded and he is liberated from all sins.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.4 Intellect, wisdom, non-delusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, happiness, pain, existence or birth, non-existence or death, fear and also fearlessness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.5 Non-injury, eanimity, contentment, austerity, beneficence, fame, ill-fame (these) different kinds of alities of beings arise from Me alone.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.6 The seven great sages, the ancient four and also the Manus, possessed of powers like Me (on account of their minds being fixed on Me), were born of (My) mind; from them are these creatures born in this world.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.7 He who in truth knows these manifold manifestations of My Being and (this) Yoga-power of Mine becomes established in the unshakable Yoga; there is no doubt about it.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.8 I am the source of all; from Me everything evolves; understanding thus, the wise, endowed with meditation, worship Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.9 With their mind and their life wholly absorbed in Me, enlightening each other and ever speaking of Me, they are satisfied and delighted.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.10 To them who are ever steadfast, worshipping Me with love, I give the Yoga of discrimination by which they come to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.11 Out of mere compassion for them, I, dwelling within their Self, destroy the darkness born of ignorance by the luminous lamp of knowledge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.12 Arjuna said Thou art the Supreme Brahman, the supreme abode (or the supreme light), the supreme purifier, eternal, divine Person, the primeval God, unborn andn omnipresent.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.13 All the sages have thus declared Thee, as also the divine sage Narada; so also Asita, Devala and Vyasa; and now Thou Thyself sayest so to me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.14 I believe all this that Thou sayest to me to be true, O Krishna; verily, O blessed Lord! neither the gods nor the demons know Thy manifestation (origin).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.16 Thou shouldst indeed tell, without reserve, of Thy divine glories by which Thou existest, pervading all these worlds. (None else can do so.)

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
10.17 How shall I, ever meditating, know Thee, O Yogin? In what aspects or things, O blessed
Lord, art Thou to be thought of by me?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.18 Tell me again in detail, O Krishna, of Thy Yogic power and glory; for I am not satiated with what I have heard of Thy life-giving and nectar-like speech.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.19 The Blessed Lord said Very well! Now I will declare to thee My divine glories in their prominence, O Arjuna; there is no end to their detailed description.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.20 I am the Self, O Gudakesa, seated in the hearts of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and also the end of all beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.21 Among the (twelve) Adityas, I am Vishnu; among luminaries, the radiant sun; I am Marichi among the (seven or forty-nine) Maruts; among stars the moon am I.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.22 Among the Vedas I am the Sama-Veda; I am Vasava among the gods; among the senses I am the mind; and I am intelligence among living beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.23 And, among the Rudras I am Sankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, the Lord of wealth (Kubera); among the Vasus I am Pavaka (fire); and among the (seven) mountains I am the Meru.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
10.24 And, among the household priests (of kings), O Arjuna, know Me to be the chief, Brihaspati; among the army generals I am Skana; among lakes I am the ocean.
'

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
