content: 10.25 Among the great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one syllable (Om); among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the immovable things I am the Himalayas.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.26 Among all the trees ( I am) the Peepul; among the divine sages, I am Narada; among Gandharvas, Chitraratha; among the perfected, the sage Kapila.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.27 Know Me as Ucchaisravas born of nectar, among horses; among lordly elephants (I am) the Airavata; and, among men, the king.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.28 Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am the wish-fulfilling cow called Kamadhenu; I am the progenitor, the god of love; among serpents I am Vasuki.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.29 I am Ananta among the Nagas; I am Varuna among water-deities; Aryaman among the Manes I am; I am Yama among the governors.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.30 And, I am Prahlada among the demons, among the reckoners I am time; among beasts I am the lion, and Vainateya (Garuda) among birds.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.31 Among the purifiers (or the speeders) I am the wind; Rama among the warriors am I; among the fishes I am the shark; among the streams I am the Ganga.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.32 Among creations I am the beginning, the middle and also the end, O Arjuna; among the sciences I am the science of the Self; and I am the logic among controversialists.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
10.33 Among the letters of the alphabets, the letter 'A' I am and the dual among the compounds. I am verily the inexhaustible or everlasting time; I am the dispenser (of the fruits of actions) having
faces in all directions.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.34 And I am the all-devouring Death, and the prosperity of those who are to be prosperous; among the feminine alities (I am) fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness and forgiveness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.35 Among the hymns also I am the Brihatsaman; among metres Gayatri am I; among the montsh I am the Margasirsha; among the seasons (I am) the flowery season.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.36 I am the gambling of the fraudulent; I am the splendour of the splendid; I am victory; I am determination (of those who are determined); I am the goodness of the good.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.37 Among the Vrishnis I am Vaasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Arjuna; among the sages I am Vyasa; among the Poets I am Usanas, the poet.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.38 Of those who punish, I am the sceptre; among those who seek victory, I am statesmanship; and also among secrets, I am silence; knowledge among knowers I am.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.39 And whatever is the seed of all beings, that also am I, O Arjuna; there is no being, whether moving or unmoving, that can exist without Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.40 There is no end to My divine gloreis, O Arjuna, but this is a brief statement by Me of the particulars of My divine glories.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.41 Whatever being there is glorious, prosperous or powerful, that know thou to be a manifestation of a part of My splendour.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 10.42 But, of what avail to thee is the knowledge of all these details, O Arjuna? I exist, supporting this whole world by one part of Myself.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.1 Arjuna said By this word (explanation) of the highest secret concerning the Self which Thou hast spoken, for the sake of blessing me, my delusion is gone.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.2 The origin and the destruction of beings verily have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O lotus-eyed Lord, and also Thy inexhaustible greatness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.3 (Now) O Supreme Lord, as Thou hast thus described Thyself, O Supreme Person, I wish to see Thy divine form.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.4 If Thou, O Lord, thinkest it possible for me to see it, do Thou, then, O Lord of the Yogins, show me Thy imperishable Self.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.5 The Blessed Lord said Behold, O Arjuna, forms of Mine, by the hundreds and thousands, of different sorts, divine, and of various colours and shapes.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.6 Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Asvins and also the Maruts; behold many wonders never seen before, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.7 Now behold, O Arjuna, in this, My body, the whole universe centred in one including the moving and the unmoving and whatever else thou desirest to see.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.8 But thou art not able to behold Me with these thine own eyes; I give thee the divine eye; behold My lordly Yoga.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.9 Sanjaya said Having thus spoken, O king, the great Lord of Yoga, hari (Krishna), showed to Arjuna His supreme form as the Lord.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.10 With numerous mouths and eyes, with numerous wonderful sights, with numerous divine ornaments, with numerous divine weapons uplifted (such a form He showed).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.11 Wearing divine garlands (necklaces) and apparel, anointed with divine unguents, the all-wonderful, resplendent (Being) endless with faces on all sides.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.12 If the splendour of a thousand suns were to blaze out at once (simultaneously) in the sky, that would be the splendour of that mighty Being (great Soul).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.13 There, in the body of the God of gods, Arjuna then saw the whole universe resting in one, with its many groups.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.14 Then, Arjuna, filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, bowed down his head to the God and spoke with joined palms.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.15 Arjuna said I see all the gods, O God, in Thy body, and (also) hosts of various classes of beings, Brahma, the Lord, seated on the lotus, all the sages and the celestial serpents.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.16 I see Thee of boundless form on every side with many arms, stomachs, mouths and eyes: neither the end nor the middle nor also the beginning do I see, O Lord of the universe, O Cosmic Form.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
11.17 I see Thee with the diadem, the club and the discus, a mass of radiance shining
everywhere, very hard to look at, blazing all round like burning fire and the sun, and immeasurable.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.18 Thou art the Imperishable, the Supreme Being, worthy to be known. Thou art the great treasure-house of this universe; Thou art the imperishable protector of the eternal Dhrama; Thou art the Primal Person, I deem.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.19 I see Thee without beginning, middle or end, infinite in power, of endless arms, the sun and the moon being Thy eyes, the burning fire Thy mouth, heating the whole universe with Thy radiance.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.20 This space between the earth and the heaven and all the arters are filled by Thee alone; having seen this, Thy wonderful and teriible form, the three worlds are trembling with fear, O great-souled Being.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.21 Verily, into Thee enter these hosts of gods; some extol Thee in fear with joined palms; saying 'may it be well', bands of great sages and perfected ones praise Thee with hymns complete.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.22 The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Visvedevas, the two Asvins, Maruts, the manes and the hosts of celestial singers, Yakshas, demons and the perfected ones, are all looking at Thee, in great amazement.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.23 Having seen Thy immeasurable form with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs and feet, with many stomachs and fearful with many teeth the worlds are terrified and so am I.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.24 On seeing Thee (the Cosmic Form) touching the sky, shining in many colours, with mouths wide open, with large fiery eyes, I am terrified at heart and find neither courage nor peace, O Vishnu.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.25 Having seen Thy mouths fearful with teeth (blazing) like the fires of cosmic dissolution, I know not the four arters, nor do I find peace. Have mercy, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.26 All the sons of Dhritarashtra, with the hosts of kings of the earth, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, with the chief among our warriors.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.27 Some hurriedly enter Thy mouths with their terrible teeth, fearful to behold. Some are found sticking in the gaps between the teeth with their heads crushed to powder.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.28 Verily, just as many torrents of rivers flow towards the ocean, even so these heroes in the world of men enter Thy flaming mouths.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.29 As moths hurriedly rush into a blazing fire for (their own) destruction, so also these creatures hurriedly rush into Thy mouths for (their own) destruction.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.30 Thou lickest up, devouring all the worlds on every side with Thy flaming mouths. Thy fierce rays, filling the whole world with radiance, are burning, O Vishnu!

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.31 Tell me, who Thou art, so fierce of form. Salutations to Thee, O God Supreme: have mercy. I desire to know Thee, the original Being. I know not indeed Thy working.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.32 The Blessed Lord said I am the full-grown world-destroying Time, now engaged in destroying the worlds. Even without thee, none of the warriors arrayed in the hostile armies shall live.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.33 Therefore, stand up and obtain fame. Coner the enemies and enjoy the unrivalled kingdom. Verily by Me have they been already slain; be thou a mere instrument, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.34 Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and other brave warriors these are already slain by Me: do thou kill; be not distressed with fear; fight and thou shalt coner thy enemies in battle.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.35 Sanjaya said Having heard that speech of Lord Krishna, Arjuna, with joined palms, trembling, prostrating himself, again addressed Krishna, in a choked voice, bowing down, overwhelmed with fear.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.36 Arjuna said It is meet, O Krishna, that the world delights and rejoices in Thy praise; demons fly in fear to all arters and the hosts of the perfected ones bow to Thee.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.37 And why should they not, O great Soul, bow to Thee Who art greater (than all else), the primal cause even of the Creator (Brahma), O Infinite Being, O Lord of the gods, O Abode of the universe; Thou art the imperishable, the Being, the non-being and That which is the supreme (that which is beyond the Being and the non-being).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.38 Thou art the primal God, the ancient Purusha, the supreme refuge of this universe, the knower, the knowable and the supreme Abode. By Thee is the universe pervaded, O Being of infinite forms.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.39 Thou art Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, the Creator, and the great-grandfather. Salutations, salutations unto Thee, a thousand times, and again salutations, salutations unto Thee.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.40 Salutations to Thee, in front and behind! Salutations to Thee on every side! O All!! Thou infinite in power and prowess, pervadest all; wherefore Thou art all.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.41 Whatever I have presumptuously said from carelessness or love, addressing Thee as O Krishna! O Yadava! O Friend! regarding Thee merely as a friend, unknowing of this, Thy greatness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.42 In whatever way I may have insulted Thee for the sake of fun, while at play, reposing, sitting or at meals, when alone (with Thee), O Krishna, or in company that I implore Thee, immeasurable one, to forgive.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.43 Thou art the Father of this world, moving and unmoving. Thou art to be adored by this world, Thou, the greatest Guru; (for) none there exists who is eal to Thee; how then could there be another superior to Thee in the three worlds, O Being of unealled power?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
11.44 Therefore, bowing down, prostrating my body, I crave Thy forgiveness, O adorable Lord. As a father forgives his son, a friend his (dear) friend, a lover his beloved, even so shouldst Thou
forgive me, O God.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.45 I am delighted, having seen what has never been seen before; and yet my mind is distressed with fear. Show me that (previous) form only, O God; have mercy, O God of gods, O Abode of the universe.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.46 I desire to see Thee as before, crowned, bearing a mace, with the discus in hand, in Thy former form only, having four arms, O thousand-armed, Cosmic Form (Being).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.47 The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, this Cosmic Form has graciously been shown to thee by Me by My own Yogic power; full of splendour, primeval, and infinite, this Cosmic Form of Mine has never been seen before by anyone other than thyself.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.48 Neither by the study of the Vedas and sacrifices, nor by gifts nor by rituals nor by severe austerities can I be seen in this form in the world of men by any other than thyself, O great hero of the Kurus (Arjuna).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.49 Be not afraid, nor bewildered on seeing such a teriible form of Mine as this; with thy fear dispelled and with a gladdened heart, now behold again this former form of Mine.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.50 Sanjaya said Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Krishna again showed His own form and the great Soul (Krishna), assuming His gentle form, consoled him (Arjuna) who was terrified.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.51 Arjuna said Having seen this Thy gentle human form, O Krishna, now I am composed and am restored to my own nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.52 The Blessed Lord said Very hard indeed it is to see this form of Mine which thou hast seen. Even the gods are ever longing to behold it.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.53 Neither by the Vedas nor by austerity, nor by gift, nor by sacrifice can I be seen in this form as thou hast seen Me (so easily).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.54 But by single-minded devotion can I, of this Form, be known and seen in reality and also entered into, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.55 He who does all actions for Me, who looks upon Me as the Supreme, who is devoted to Me, who is free from attachment, who bears enmity towards no creature, he comes to Me, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.1 Arjuna said Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship Thee and those also who worship the imperishable and the unmanifested which of them are better versed in Yoga?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.2 The Blessed Lord said Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever steadfast and endowed with supreme faith, are the best in Yoga in My opinion.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.4 Having restrained all the senses, even-minded everywhere, intent on the welfare of all beings verily they also come unto Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.5 Greater is their trouble whose minds are set on the unmanifested; for the goal; the unmanifested, is very hard for the embodied to reach.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.6 But to those who worship Me, renouncing all actions in Me, regarding Me as the supreme gaol, meditating on Me with single-minded Yoga.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.7 To those whose minds are set on Me, O Arjuna, verily I become ere long the saviour out of the ocean of Samsara.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.8 Fix thy mind in Me only, thy intellect in Me, (then) thou shalt no doubt live in Me alone hereafter.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.9 If thou art unable to fix thy mind steadily on Me, then by the Yoga of constant practice do thou seek to reach Me, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.10 If thou art unable to practise even this Abhyasa Yoga, be thou intent on doing actions for My sake; even by doing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.11 If thou art unable to do even this, then, resorting to union with Me, renounce the fruits of all actions with the self controlled.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.12 Better indeed is knowledge than practice; than knowledge meditation is better; than meditation the renunciation of the fruits of actions: peace immediately follows renunciation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.13 He who hates no creature, who is friendly and compassionate to all, who is free from attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.14 Ever content, steady in meditation, self-controlled, possessed of firm conviction, with the mind and intellect dedicated to Me, he, My devtoee, is dear to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.15 He by whom the world is not agitated and who cannot be agitated by the world, and who is freed from joy, anger, fear and anxiety he is dear to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.16 He who is free from wants, pure, expert, unconcerned, and free from pain, renouncing all undertakings or commencements he who is (thus) devoted to Me, is dear to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.17 He who neither rejoices, nor hates, nor grieves, nor desires, renouncing good and evil, and who is full of devotion, is dear to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.19 He to whom censure and praise are eal, who is silent, content with anything, homeless, of a steady mind, and full of devotion that man is dear to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.20 They verily who follow this immortal Dharma (law or doctrine) as described above, endowed with faith, regarding Me as their supreme goal, they, the devotees, are exceedingly dear to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.2 The Blessed Lord said This body, O Arjuna, is called the field; he who knows it is called the knower of the field, by those who know of them.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.3 Do thou also know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, O Arjuna. Knowledge of both the field and the knower of the field is considered by Me to be ï1the ï1 knowledge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.4 What the field is and of what nature, what are its modifications and whence it is and also who He is and what His powers are hear all that from Me in brief.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.5 Sages have sung in many ways, in various distinctive chants and also in the suggestive words indicative of the Absolute, full of reasoning and decisive.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.6 The great elements, egoism, intellect, and also the Unmanifested Nature, the ten senses and one (mind), and the five objects of the senses.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.7 Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the aggregate (the body), intelligence, fortitude the field has thus been briefly described with its modifications.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.8 Humility, unpretentiousness, non-injury, forgiveness, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.9 Indifference to the objects of the senses and also absence of egoism; perception of (or reflection on) the evil in birth, death, old age, sickness and pain.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.10 Non-attachment, non-identification of the Self with son, wife, home and the rest, and constant even-mindedness on the attainment of the desirable and the undesirable.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.11 Unswerving devotion unto Me by the Yoga of non-separation, resort to solitary places, distaste for the society of men.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.12 Constancy in Self-knowledge, perception of the end of true knowledge this is declared to be knowledge, and what is opposed to it is ignorance.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.13 I will declare that which has to be known, knowing which one attains to immortality, the beginningless supreme Brahman, called neither being nor non-being.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.14 With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, with ears everywhere, He exists in the worlds enveloping all.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.15 Shining by the functions of all the senses, yet without the senses; unattached, yet supporting all; devoid of alities, yet their experiencer.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.16 Without and within (all) beings the unmoving and also the moving; because of Its subtlety, unknowable; and near and far away is That.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.17 And undivided, yet It exists as if divided in beings; It is to be known as the supporter of being; It devours and It generates.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.18 That, the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness: knowledge, the knowable and the goal of knowledge, seated in the hearts of all.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.19 Thus the field, as well as knowledge and the knowable have been briefly stated. My devotee, knowing this, enters into My Being.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.20 Know thou that Nature (matter) and the Spirit are both beginningless; and know also that all modifications and alities are born of Nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.21 In the production of the effect and the cause, Nature (matter) is said to be the cause; in the experience of pleasure and pain, the soul is said to be the cause.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.22 The soul seated in Nature experiences the alities born of Nature; attachment to the alities is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.23 The Supreme Soul in this body is also called the spectator, the permitter, the supporter, the enjoyer, the great Lord and the Supreme Self.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.24 He who thus knows the Spirit and Matter together with the alities, in whatever condition he may be, he is not born again.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.25 Some by meditation behold the Self in the self by the self, others by the Yoga of knowledge, and still others by the Yoga of action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.26 Others also, not knowing thus, worship, having heard of It from others; they, too, cross beyond death, regarding what they have heard as the Supreme refuge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.27 Wherever a being is born, whether unmoving or moving, know thou, O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna), that it is from the union between the field and its knower.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.28 He sees, who sees the Supreme Lord, existing eally in all beings, the unperishing within the perishing.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.29 Because he who sees the same Lord eally dwelling everywhere does not destroy the Self by the self; he goes to the highest goal.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.30 He sees, who sees that all actions are performed by Nature alone and that the Self is actionless.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.31 When a man sees the whole variety of beings as resting in the One, and spreading forth from That alone, he then becomes Brahman.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.32 Being without beginning and being devoid of (any) alities, the Supreme Self, imperishable, though dwelling in the body, O Arjuna, neither acts nor is tainted.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.33 As the all-pervading ether is not tainted, because of its subtlety, so the Self seated everywhere in the body is not tainted.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
13.34 Just as the one sun illumines the whole world, so also the Lord of the field (Supreme Self)
illumines the whole field, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.35 They who, by the eye of knowledge, perceive the distinction between the field and its knower and also the liberation from the Nature of being, go to the Supreme.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.1 The Blessed Lord said I will again declare (to thee) that supreme knowledge, the best of all knowledge, having known which all the sages have gone to the supreme perfection after this life.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.2 They who, having taken refuge in this knowledge, have attained to unity with Me, are neither born at the time of creation nor are they disturbed at the time of dissolution.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.3 My womb is the great Brahma; in that I place the germ; thence, O Arjuna, is the birth of all beings.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.4 Whatever forms are produced, O Arjuna, in any womb whatsoever, the great Brahma is their womb and I am the seed-giving father.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.5 Purity, passion and inertia these alities, O Arjuna, born of Nature, bind fast in the body, the embodied, the indestructible.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.6 Of these, Sattva, which from its stainlessness is luminous and healthy, binds by attachment to happiness and by attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.7 Know thou Rajas to be of the nature of passion, the source of thirst (for sensual enjoyment) and attachment; it binds fast, O Arjuna, the embodied one by attachment to action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.8 But know thou Tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds fast, O Arjuna, by heedlessness, indolence and sleep.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.9 Sattva attaches to happiness, Rajas to action, O Arjuna, while Tamas verily shrouding knowledge attaches to heedlessness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.10 Now Sattva arises (prevails), O Arjuna, having overpowered Rajas and Tamas; nor Rajas, having overpowered Sattva and Tamas; and now Tamas, having overpowered Sattva and Rajas.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.11 When through every gate (sense) in this body, the wisdom-light shines, then it may be known that Sattva is predominant.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.12 Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness, longing these arise when Rajas is predominant, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.13 Darkness, inertness, heedlessness and delusion these arise when Tamas is predominant, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.14 If the embodied one meets with death when Sattva is predominant, then he attains to the spotless worlds of the knowers of the Highest.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.15 Meeting death in Rajas, he is born among those who are attached to action; and dying in Tamas, he is born in the womb of the senseless.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.16 The fruit of good action, they say, is Sattvic and pure, verily the fruit of Rajas is pain, and ignorance is the fruit of Tamas.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.17 From Sattva arises knowledge, and greed from Rajas; heedlessness and delusion arise from Tamas, and also ignorance.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.18 Those who are seated in Sattva go upwards; the Rajasic dwell in the middle; and the Tamasic, abiding in the function of the lowest Guna, go downwards.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.19 When the seer beholds no agent other than the Gunas and knows That which is higher than they, he attains to My Being.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.20 The embodied one having crossed beyond these three Gunas out of which the body is evolved, is freed from birth, death, decay and pain, and attains to immortality.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.21 Arjuna said What are the marks of him who has transcended the three alities, O Lord? What is his conduct and how does he go beyond these three alities?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.22 The Blessed Lord said When light, activity and delusion are present, he hates them not, nor does he long for them when they are absent.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.23 He who, seated like one unconcerned, is not moved by the alities, and who, knowing that the alities are active, is self-centred and moves not.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.24 Who is the same in pleasure and pain, who dwells in the Self, to whom a clod of earth, stone and gold are alike, who is the same to the dear and the unfriendly, who is firm, and to whom censure and praise are as one.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.25 Who is the same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings he is said to have transcended the alities.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.26 And he who serves Me with unswerving devotion, he, crossing beyond the alities, is fit for becoming Brahman.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.27 For I am the abode of Brahman, the immortal and the immutable, of everlasting Dharma and of absolute bliss.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.1 The Blessed Lord said They (the wise) speak of the indestructible peepul tree having its root above and branches below, whose leaves are the metres or hymns: he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.2 Below and above spread its branches, nourished by the Gunas; sense-objects are its buds; and below, in the world of men, stretch forth the roots, originating action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.3 Its form is not perceived here as such, neither its end nor its origin, nor its foundation nor resting place: having cut asunder this firmly rooted peepul tree with the strong axe of non-attachment.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.4 Then That goal should be sought for, whither having gone none returns again. I seek refuge in that Primeval Purusha Whence streamed forth the ancient activity or energy.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.5 Free from pride and delusion, victorious over the evil of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, their desires having completely turned away, freed from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach the eternal goal.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.6 Neither doth the sun illumine there nor the moon, nor the fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.7 An eternal portion of Myself having become a living soul in the world of life, draws to (itself) the (five) senses with the mind for the sixth, abiding in Nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.8 When the Lord (as the individual soul) obtains a body and when He leaves it, He takes these and goes (with them) as the wind takes the scents from their seats (flowers, etc.).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.9 Presiding over the ear, the eye, touch, taste and smell, as well as the mind, it enjoys the objects of the senses.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.10 The deluded do not see Him Who departs, stays and enjoys; but they who possess the eye of knowledge behold Him.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.11 The Yogins striving (for perfection) behold Him dwelling in the Self; but, the unrefined and unintelligent, even though striving, see Him not.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.12 That light which residing in the sun illumines the whole world, that which is in the moon and in the fire know that light to be Mine.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.13 Permeating the earth I support all beings by (My) energy; and having become the watery moon I nourish all herbs.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.14 Having become the fire Vaisvanara, I abide in the body of living beings and, associated with the Prana and the Apana, digest the fourfold food.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.15 And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me are memory and knowledge, as well as their absence. I am verily That which has to be known by all the Vedas; I am indeed the author of the Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas am I.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
15.16 Two Purushas there are in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are
the perishable and the Kutastha the unchanging is called the imperishable.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.17 But distinct is the Supreme Purusha called the highest Self, the indestructible Lord Who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.18 As I transcend the perishable and am even higher than the imperishable, I am declared to be the highest Purusha in the world and in the Vedas.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.19 He who, undeluded, knows Me thus as the highest Purusha, he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being (heart), O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.20 Thus, this most secret science has been taught by Me, O sinless one; on knowing this, a man becomes wise, and all his duties are accomplished, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.1 The Blessed Lord said Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and Yoga, almsgiving, control of the senses, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.2 Harmlessness, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion towards beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.3 Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of hatred, absence of pride these belong to the one born for a divine state, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.4 Hypocrisy, arrogance and self-conceit, anger and also harshness and ignorance, belong to one who is born for a demoniacal state, O Partha (Arjuna).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.5 The divine nature is deemed conducive to liberation, and the demoniacal to bondage. Grieve not, O Arjuna, thou art born with divine endowments.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.6 There are two types of beings in this world, the divine and the demoniacal; the divine has been described at length; hear from Me, O Arjuna, of the demoniacal.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.7 The demoniacal know not what to do and what to refrain from; neither purity, nor right conduct nor truth is found in them.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.8 They say, "This universe is without truth, without (moral) basis, without a God, brought about by mutual union, with lust for its cause; what else?"

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.9 Holding this view, these ruined souls of small intellect and fierce deeds, come forth as the enemies of the world for its destruction.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.10 Filled with insatiable desires, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they work with impure resolves.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.11 Giving themselves over to immeasurable cares ending only with death, regarding gratification of lust as their highest aim, and feeling sure that that is all.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.12 Bound by a hundred ties of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards to wealth for sensual enjoyments.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.13 "This has been gained by me today; this desire of mine I shall fuffil; this is mine and this wealth also shall be mine in future."

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.14 "That enemy has been slain by me; and others also I shall slay. I am the lord. I enjoy. I am perfect, powerful and happy."

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.15 "I am rich and born in a noble family. Who else is equal to me? I shall perform sacrifices. I shall give (charity). I shall rejoice," thus deluded by ignorance.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.16 Bewildered by many a fancy, entangled in the snare of delusion, addicted to the gratification of lust, they fall into a foul hell.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.17 Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name out of ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.18 Given over to egoism, power, haughtiness, lust and anger, these malicious people hate Me in their own bodies and in those of others.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.19 Those cruel haters, worst among men in the world, I hurl those evil-doers into the wombs of demons only.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.20 Entering into demoniacal wombs and deluded, birth after birth, not attaining Me, they thus fall, O Arjuna, into a condition still lower than that.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.21 Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self lust, anger and greed; therefore one should abandon these three.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.22 A man who is liberated from these three gates to darkness, O Arjuna, practises what is good for him and thus goes to the Supreme Goal.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.23 He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the scriptures, acts under the impulse of desire, attains not perfection, nor happiness nor the Supreme Goal.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.24 Therefore, let the scripture be thy authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known what is said in the ordinance of the scriptures, thou shouldst act here in this world.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.1 Arjuna said Those who, setting aside the ordinances of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith, what is their condition, O Krishna? Is is Sattva, Rajas or Tamas?

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.2 The Blessed Lord said Threefold is the faith of the embodied, which is inherent in their nature the Sattvic (pure), the Rajasic (passionate) and the Tamasic (dark). Do thou hear of it.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.3 The faith of each is in accordance with his nature, O Arjuna. The man consists of his faith; as a man's faith is, so is he.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.4 The Sattvic or the pure men worship the gods; the Rajasic or the passionate worship the Yakshas and the Rakshasas; the others (the Tamasic or the deluded people) worship the ghosts and the hosts of the nature-spirits.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.5 Those men who practise terrific austerities not enjoined by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, impelled by the force of lust and attachment.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.6 Senseless, torturing all the elements in the body and Me also, Who dwell in the body, know thou these to be of demonical resolves.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.7 The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.8 The foods which increase life, purity, strength, health, joy and cheerfulness (good appetite), which are savoury and oleaginous, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic (pure) people.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.9 The foods that are bitter, sour, saline, excessively hot, pungent, dry and burning, are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief and disease.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.10 That which is state, tasteless, putrid, rotten, refuse and impure, is the food liked by the Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.11 That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for reward as enjoined by the ordinance (scripture), with a firm faith that to do so is a duty, is Sattvic or pure.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.12 The sacrifice which is offered, O Arjuna, seeking a reward and for ostentation, know thou that to be a Rajasic Yajna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.13 They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, which is devoid of Mantras, gifts and faith.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.14 Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers and the wise, purity, straightforwardness, celibacy and non-injury are called the austerities of the body.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.15 Speech which causes no excitement, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Vedas, are called austerity of speech.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.16 Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, self-control, purity of nature this is called mental austerity.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.17 This threefold austerity, practised by steadfast men, with the utmost faith, desiring no reward, they call Sattvic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.18 The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining good reception, honour and worship, and with hypocrisy, is here said to be Rajasic, unstable and transitory.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.19 That austerity which is practised out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.20 That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that gift is held to be Sattvic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.21 And, that gift which is given with a view to receive something in return, or looking for a reward, or reluctantly, is held to be Rajasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.22 The gift that is given at a wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult is declared to be Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.23 "Om Tat Sat": This has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that were created formerly, the Brahmanas, the Vedas and the sacrifices.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.24 Therefore, with the utterance of "Om" are the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as enjoined in the scriptures, always begun by the students of Brahman.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.25 Uttering ï1Tatï1, without aiming at the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice and austerity and the various acts of gifts performed by the seekers of liberation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.26 The word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of reality and of goodness; and so also, O Arjuna, the word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of an auspicious act.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.27 Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift, is also called 'Sat' and also action in connection with these (or for the sake of the Supreme) is called 'Sat'.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.28 Whatever is sacrificed, given or performed, and whatever austerity is practised without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Arjuna; it is naught here or hereafter (after death).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.1 Arjuna said I desire to know severally, O mighty-armed, the essence or truth of renunciation, O Hrishikesa, as also of abandonment, O slayer of Kesi.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.2 The Blessed Lord said The sages understand Sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions as Tyaga.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.3 Some philosophers declare that actions should be abandoned as an evil; while others (declare) that acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinished.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.4 Hear from Me the conclusion or the final truth about this abandonment, O best of the Bharatas; abandonment, verily, O best of men, has been declared to be of three kinds.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.5 Acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the purifiers of the wise.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.6 But even these actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards, O Arjuna; this is My certain and best conviction.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.7 Verily the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper; the abandonment of the same from delusion is declared to be Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.8 He who abandons action on account of the fear of bodily trouble (because it is painful), does not obtain the merit of renunciation by doing such Rajasic renunciation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.9 Whatever obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, merely because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and also the desire for reward, that renunciation is regarded as Sattvic (pure).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.10 The man of renunciation, pervaded by purity, intelligent, and with his doubts cut asunder, does not hate a disagreeable work nor is he attached to an agreeable one.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.11 Verily, it is not possible for an embodied being to abandon actions entirely; but he who relinishes the rewards of actions is verily called a man of renunciation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.12 The threefold fruit of action (evil, good and mixed) accrues after death to the non-abandoners, but never to the abandoners.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.13 Learn from Me, O mighty-armed Arjuna, these five causes as declared in the Sankhya system for the accomplishment of all actions.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.14 The seat (body), the doer, the various senses, the different functions of various sorts, and the presiding deity, also, the fifth.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.15 Whatever action a man performs with his body, speech and mind whether right or the reverse these five are its causes.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.16 Now, such being the case, verily he who owing to untrained understanding looks upon his Self, which is isolated, as the agent, he of perverted intelligence, sees not.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
18.17 He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose intelligence is not tainted (by good or evil),
though he slays these people, he slayeth not, nor is he bound (by the action).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.18 Knowledge, the knowable and the knower form the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action and the agent form the threefold basis of action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.19 Knowledge, action and actor are declared in the science of the Gunas (Sankhya philosophy) to be of three kinds only, according to the distinction of the Gunas. Of these also, hear duly.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.20 That by which one sees the one indestructible Reality in all beings, not separate in all the separate beings know thou that knowledge to be Sattvic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.21 But that knowledge which sees in all beings various entities of distinct kinds as different from one another know thou that knowledge to be Rajasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.22 But that which clings to one single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, without foundation in Truth, and trivial that is declared to be Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.23 An action which is ordained, which is free from attachment, and which is done without love or hatred by one who is not desirous of any reward that action is declared to be Sattvic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.24 But that action which is done by one longing for the fulfilment of desires or gain with egoism or with much effort that is declared to be Rajasic (passionate).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.25 That action which is undertaken from delusion, without a regard for the conseences, loss, injury and (one's own) ability that is declared to be Tamasic (dark).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.26 An agent who is free from attachment, non-egoistic, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is called Sattvic (pure).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.27 Passionate, desiring to obtain the reward of actions, greedy, cruel, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an agent is said to be Rajasic (passionate).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.28 Unsteady, vulgar, unbending, cheating, malicious, lazy, desponding and procrastinating such an agent is called Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.29 Hear thou the threefold division of intellect and firmness according to the Gunas, as I declare them fully and distinctly, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.30 The intellect which knows the path of work and renunciation, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation that intellect is Sattvic (pure), O Arjuna.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.31 That, by which one wrongly understands Dharma and Adharma and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done that intellect, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.32 That, which, enveloped in darkness, sees Adharma as Dharma and all things perverted that intellect, O Arjuna, is Tamasic (dark).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.33 The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, the functions of the mind, the life-force and the senses are restrained that firmness, O Arjuna, is Sattvic (pure).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.34 But that, O Arjuna, by which, on account of attachment and desire for reward, one holds fast to Dharma (duty), enjoyment of pleasures and earning of wealth that firmness, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.35 That, by which a stupid man does not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair and also conceit that firmness, O Arjuna, is Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.36 And now hear from Me, O Arjuna, of the threefold pleasure, in which one rejoices by practice and surely comes to the end of pain.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.37 That which is like poison at first but in the end like nectar that happiness is declared to be Sattvic, born of the purity of one's own mind due to Self-realisation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.38 That happiness which arises from the contact of the sense-organs with the objects, which is at first like nectar, and in the end like poison that is declared to be Rajasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.39 That happiness which at first as well as in the seel deludes the self, and which arises from sleep, indolence and heedlessness that is declared to be Tamasic.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.40 There is no being on earth or again in heaven among the gods, that is liberated from the three alities born of Nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.41 Of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaisyas, as also of Sudras, O Arjuna, the duties are distributed according to the alities born of their own nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.42 Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness and also uprightness, knowledge, realisation and belief in God are the duties of the Brahmanas, born of (their own) nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.43 Prowess, splendour, firmness, dexterity and also not fleeing from battle, generosity and lordliness are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of (their own) nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.44 Agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade are the duties of the Vaisya (merchant), born of (their own) nature; and action consisting of service is the duty of the Sudra (servant-class), born of (their own) nature.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.10 He who does actions, offering them to Brahman, and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus-leaf is not tainted by water.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.46 He from Whom all the beings have evolved and by Whom all this is pervaded worshipping Him with his own duty, man attains perfection.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.47 Better is one's own duty (though) destitute of merits, than the duty of another well performed. He who does the duty ordained by his own nature incurs no sin.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.48 One should not abandon, O Arjuna, the duty to which one is born, though faulty; for, all undertakings are enveloped by evil, as fire by smoke.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.49 He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, from whom desire has fled, he by renunciation, attains the supreme state of freedom from action.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.50 Learn from Me in brief, O Arjuna, how he who has attained perfection reaches Brahman (the Eternal), that supreme state of knowledge.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.51 Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self by firmness, relinishing sound and other objects and abandoning attraction and hatred.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.52 Dwelling in solitude, eating but little, with speech, body and mind subdued, always engaged in meditation and concentration, resorting to dispassion.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.53 Having abandoned egoism, strength, arrogance, desire, anger and covetousness, and free from the notion of 'mine' and peaceful, he is fit for becoming Brahman.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.54 Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, he neither grieves nor desires, the same to all beings, he obtains supreme devotion to Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.55 By devotion he knows Me in truth, what and who I am; then having known Me in truth, he forthwith enters into the Supreme.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.56 Doing all actions always having taken refuge in Me, by My grace he obtains the eternal indestructible state of being.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.57 Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, having Me as the highest goal, resorting to the Yoga of discrimination do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.58 Fixing thy mind on Me, thou shalt by My grace overcome all obstacles; but if from egoism thou wilt not hear Me, thou shalt perish.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.59 If, filled with egoism, thou thinkest: "I will not fight", vain is this, thy resolve; Nature will compel thee.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.60 O Arjuna, bound by thy own Karma (action) born of thy own nature, that which from delusion thou wishest not to do, even that thou shalt do helplessly.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
