content: 18.56 सर्वकर्माणि all actions? अपि also? सदा always? कुर्वाणः doing? मद्व्यपाश्रयः taking refuge in Me? मत्प्रसादात् by My grace? अवाप्नोति obtains? शाश्वतम् the eternal? पदम् state or abode? अव्ययम् indestructible.Commentary Worshipping Me with the flowers of his good actions he reaches the imperishable Brahmic seat of ineffable splendour through My grace. He attains union with Me and enjoys the supreme bliss. If by chance he commits some prohibited actions? still? as in the Ganga (Indias most holy river) the waters of the drains and roads find union? so My devotee? becoming united with Me? is unaffected by these prohibited actions.Worship of the Lord through ones duties purifies the heart of the aspirant and prepares him for the devotion to knowledge which eventually leads him to the attainment of Selfrealisation. The Yoga of Devotion is eulogised here.All actions Good actions and even the prohibited actions. He who takes shelter in Me? Vaasudeva? the Lord? with his whole self centred in Me attains the eternal abode of Vishnu? by the grace of the Lord.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.57 चेतसा mentally? सर्वकर्माणि all actions? मयि in Me? संन्यस्य resigning? मत्परः having Me as the highest goal? बुद्धियोगम् the Yoga of discrimination? उपाश्रित्य resorting to? मच्चित्तः with the mind fixed on Me? सततम् always? भव be.Commentary Do thou? O Arjuna? surrender all thy actions to Me whilst at the same time fixing thy mind on discrimination. Then through that discrimination thou wilt see thy Self as separate from the body and activity and existing in My pure Being. Chetasa Mentally with the discriminative faith that knowledge finally leads to liberation when the heart is purified through selfless works done with the spirit of offering to God.Sarvakarmani All actions producing visible and invisible results.Me The Lord As taught in verse 27 of chapter IX Whatever thou doest? whatever thou eatest? etc.? do thou dedicate all thy actions to Me.Matparah Taking Me? Vaasudeva? as the supreme goal? and his whole self centred in Me.Resorting to Buddhi Yoga As thy sole refuge steadymindedness.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.58 मच्चित्तः fixing thy mind on Me? सर्वदुर्गाणि all obstacles? मत्प्रसादात् by My grace? तरिष्यसि (thou) shalt overcome? अथ now? चेत् if? त्वम् thou? अहङ्कारात् from egoism? न not? श्रोष्यसि (thou) wilt hear? विनङ्क्ष्यसि (thou) shalt perish.Commentary When thy mind? O Arjuna? through onepointed devoion is fixed on Me? thou shalt by My grace cross over all difficulties and obstacles. But shouldst thou not take My teaching to heart and through pride disregard it? thou shalt be ruined.Difficulties Obstacles? snares? pitfalls? temptations on the spiritual path and various sorts of other difficulties of Samsara? diseases? etc.Egosim The idea that thou art a learned man. Thou shouldst not think I am independent. I know everything. I am a wise man. Why should I take the advice of another

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.59 यत् if? अहङ्कारम् egoism? आश्रित्य having taken refuge in? न not? योत्स्ये (I) will fight? इति thus? मन्यसे (thou) thinkest? मिथ्या vain? एषः this? व्यवसायः resolve? ते thy? प्रकृतिः nature? त्वाम् thee? नियोक्ष्यति will compel.Commentary This strong determination of thy mind will be rendered utterly futile by thy inner nature thy nature will constrain thee thy nature as a warrior will compel thee to fight. It is a mere illusion to say that thou art Arjuna? that these are thy relatives and that to kill them will be a sin.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.60 स्वभावजेन born of (thy) own nature? कौन्तेय O son of Kunti? निबद्धः bound? स्वेन (thy) own? कर्मणा by action? कर्तुम् to do? न not? इच्छसि (thou) wishest? यत् which? मोहात् from delusion? करिष्यसि (thou) shalt do? अवशः helpless? अपि also? तत् that.Commentary Thou art endowed? O Arjuna? with martial alities? prowess? valour? skill? etc. Thou art? therefore? bound by these innate alities. Thou wilt be forced to fight by thy own nature. Nature will constrain thee to fight? much against thy will.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.61 ईश्वरः the Lord? सर्वभूतानाम् of all beings? हृद्देशे in the hearts? अर्जुन O Arjuna? तिष्ठति dwells? भ्रामयन् causing to revolve? सर्वभूतानि all beings? यन्त्रारूढानि mounted on a machine? मायया by illusion.Commentary Isvara The Lord the Ruler of the universe Narayana.The Lord abides in the hearts of all beings. It is He Who has given a gift of this marvellous machine to you. It is by His power that all bodies move. The Lord is the real Actor within.By Maya By causing illusion.He causes all beings to revolve like wooden dolls mounted on a machine. (Cf.X.20.XIII.18)

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.62 तम् to Him? एव even? शरणम् गच्छ take refuge? सर्वभावेन with all thy being? भारत O Bharata? तत्प्रसादात् by His grace? पराम् supreme? शान्तिम् peace? स्थानम् the abode? प्राप्स्यसि (thou) shalt obtain? शाश्वतम् eternal.Commentary Do total and perfect surrender to the Lord. Do not keep any secret desires for silent gratification. Desire and egoism are the two chief obstacles that stand in the way of selfsurrender. Kill them ruthlessly.Run to the Lord for shelter with all thy being for freeing thyself from the troubles? afflictions and sorrows of Samsara. Take the Lord as the sole refuge. Then by His grace? thou shalt obtain supreme peace and attain to the supreme? eternal Abode.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.63 इति thus? ते to thee? ज्ञानम् wisdom? आख्यातम् has been declared? गुह्यात् than the secret? गुह्यतरम् more secret? मया by Me? विमृश्य reflecting over? एतत् this? अशेषेण fully? यथा as? इच्छसि (thou) wishest? तथा so? कुरु act.Commentary Thus has wisdom? more profound than all secrets? been declared to thee by Me. This teaching is well known as the Gita? the essence of all the Vedas. If anyone follows it and lives in the spirit of this teaching he will certainly attain supreme peace? highest knowledge and immortality. There is no doubt about this. I have revealed the mystery of this secret treasure to thee as thou art dear to Me? O Arjuna.It The teaching declared above. Reflect fully over everything that has been taught to thee.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.64 सर्वगुह्यतमम् the most secret of all? भूयः again? श्रृणु hear? मे My? परमम् supreme? वचः word? इष्टः beloved? असि (thou) art? मे of Me? दृढम् dearly? इति thus? ततः therefore? वक्ष्यामि (I) will speak? ते thy? हितम् what is good.Commentary Now listen once more with rapt attention to My words. Thou art very dear to Me. Thou art a sincere aspirant. Therefore I am telling thee this most mysterious truth. Hear from Me this mystery of all mysteries. I shall tell it to you again to make a deep impression on your mind? although it has been declared more than once. I do not hope to get any reward from thee. Thou art My most beloved friend and disciple. Therefore I will speak what is good for thee? the means of attaining Selfrealisation. This is the supreme good or the highest of all kinds of good for thee.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.65 मन्मनाः with mind fixed on Me? भव be? मद्भक्तः devoted to Me? मद्याजी sacrifice to Me? माम् to Me? नमस्कुरु bow down? माम् to Me? एव even? एष्यसि (thou) shalt come? सत्यम् truth? ते to thee? प्रतिजाने (I) promise? प्रियः dear? असि (thou) art? मे of Me.Commentary Develop onepointedness of mind. Fix thy thought on Me. If the mind wanders bring it again and again to the centre or point or object of meditation? through constant practice. Offer all thy actions to Me. Let thy tongue utter My name. Let thy hands work for Me. Let thy feet move for Me. Let all thy actions be for Me. Give up hatred towards any living creature. Bow down to Me. Then thou wilt attain Me.The Lord gives Arjuna His definite word of promise or solemn declaration. Having received My grace thou wilt gain complete knowledge of Me and that in itself will indeed lead to thy absorption into My Being.O Arjuna? looking up to Me alone as thy aim and the sole refuge? thou shalt assuredly come to,Me.Have faith in the words of the Lord and make a solemn promise. Take the Lord as your sole refuge. You will attain final emancipation.The secret of devotion is to take the Lord as your sole refuge. In the next verse the Lord proceeds to speak of the gist of selfsurrender. (Cf.IX.34XII.8)

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.66 सर्वधर्मान् all duties? परित्यज्य having abandoned? माम् to Me? एकम् alone? शरणम् refuge? व्रज take? अहम् I? त्वा thee? सर्वपापेभ्यः from all sins? मोक्षयिष्यामि will liberate? मा dont? शुचः grieve.Commentary This is the answer given by the Lord to the estion put by Arjuna in chapter II? verse 7 I ask Thee which may be the better tell me that decidedly. I am Thy disciple? suppliant to Thee teach me.All Dharmas Righteous deeds? including Adharma all actions? righteous or unrighteous? as absolute freedom from all actions is intended to be taught here.Taking refuge in Me alone implies the knowledge of unity without any thought of duality knowing that there is nothing else except Me? the Self of all? dwelling the same in all. If thou art established in this faith? I shall liberate thee from all sins? from all bonds of Dharma and Adharma by manifesting Myself as thy own Self.To behold forms is the Dharma of the eye. The support or substratum of all forms is Brahman. When you look at an object behold Brahman Which is the one essence and abandon the form as it is illusory and unreal. Have the same attitude towards the other objects which pertain to the other senses.Give up the JivaDharma (the notions I am the doer o actions? I enjoy. I am a Brahmana. I am a Brahmachari. I am endowed with a little knowledge and power? etc. and get yourself established in BrahmaBhavana (the understanding or knowledge I am Brahman). This is what is meant by taking refuge in Lord Krishna? according to the Vedantins.Work ceaselessly for the Lord but surrender the fruits of all actions to the Lord. Take the Lord as your sole refuge. Live for Him. Work for Him. Serve Him in all forms. Think of Him only. Meditate on Him alone. See Him in all forms. Think of Him only. Meditate on Him alone. See Him everywhere. Worship Him in your heart. Consecrate your life? all actions? feelings and thoughts to the Lord. You will rest in Him. You will attain union with Him. You will attain immortal supreme peace and eternal bliss. This is the view of another school of thought.Sri Sankara very strongly refutes the idea that knowledge in conjunction with Karma (action) produces or leads to liberation. He says that Karma and knowledge may not go together in the same man? that karma helps the man to get purification of the heart? and that right knowledge of the Self alone will give him absolute freedom from Samsara. He says that work and knowledge are like darkness and light? that action is possible only in this universe of illusory phenomena which is the projection of ignorance and knowledge dispels this ignorance. (Cf.III.30IX.22)

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.67 इदम् this? ते by thee? न not? अतपस्काय to one who is devoid of austerity? न not? अभक्ताय to one who is not devoted? कदाचन never? न not? च and? अशुश्रूषवे to one who does not render service or who does not desire to listen? वाच्यम् to be spoken? न not? च and? माम् Me? यः who? अभ्यसूयति cavils at.Commentary This The scripture which has been taught to you.Service To the Guru.The scripture can be taught to him who does not speak ill of the Lord? who is a man of austerities? who is devoted? who is thirsting to hear and who renders service to his Guru.One who cavils at Me He who disregards Me taking Me for an ordinary man? who does not like to be told that I am the Lord.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.68 यः who? इमम् this? परमम् supreme? गुह्यम् secret? मद्भक्तेषु in My devotees? अभिधास्यति shall declare? भक्तिम् devotion? मयि in Me? पराम् supreme? कृत्वा having done? माम् to Me? एव even? एष्यति shall come? असंशयः doubtless.Commentary This supreme secret The teachings of the Gita as taught above in the form of a dialogue between Lord Krishna and Arjuna. Why is it called a supreme secret Because it helps one to attain immortality or freedom from the whell of birth and death.He alone? who has devotion? is alified to receive the teachings of the Gita.Teach with the faith that he is thus doing service to the Lord? the Supreme Teacher.Doubtless may also mean freedom from doubts.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.69 न not? च and? तस्मात् than he? मनुष्येषु among men? कश्चित् any? मे of Me? प्रियकृत्तमः one who does dearer service? भविता shall be? न not? च and? मे of Me? तस्मात् than he? अन्यः another? प्रियतरः dearer? भुवि on the earth.Commentary He who hands down this Gita to My devotees does immense service to Me. He is very dear to Me. There is none in the present generation who des dearer service to Me? nor shall there be in future also in this world.Bhuvi On earth in this world.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.70 अध्येष्यते shall study? च and? यः who? इमम् this? धर्म्यम् sacred? संवादम् dialogue? आवयोः of ours? ज्ञानयज्ञेन by the sacrifice of wisdom? तेन by him? अहम् I? इष्टः worshipped? स्याम् (I) shall have been? इति thus? मे My? मतिः conviction. Commentary There are four kinds of sacrifice -- Vidhi? Japa? Upamsu and Manasa. Vidhi is ritual. Japa is recitation of a Mantra. Upamsu is Japa done in a whisper. Of the four kinds? JnanaYajna or the wisdomsacrifice comes under Manasa and is? therefore? the highest. The Gita is eulogised as a JnanaYajna. He who studies this scripture with faith and devotion will attain the fruit that is eal to that of performing JnanaYajna or meditation on a deity and the like.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.71 श्रद्धावान् full of faith? अनसूयः free from malice? च and? श्रृणुयात् may hear? अपि also? यः who? नरः man? सः he? अपि also? मुक्तः liberated? शुभान् happy? लोकान् worlds? प्राप्नुयात् shall attain? पुण्यकर्मणाम् of those of righteous deeds.Commentary Liberated from sin.Punyakarmanam Of those who have done Agnihotra and such other sacrifices.He too Much more so who understands the teachings of the Gita? lives in its spirit and who practises the most valuable spiritual instructions contained in it.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.72 कच्चित् whether? एतत् this? श्रुतम् heard? पार्थ O son of Kunti (Arjuna)? त्वया by thee? एकाग्रेण onepointed? चेतसा by mind? कच्चित् whether? अज्ञानसंमोहः the delusion of ignorance? प्रनष्टः has been destroyed? ते thy? धनञ्जय O Dhananjaya.Commentary It is the duty of the spiritual teacher or preceptor to make the aspirant understand the teaching of the scripture and to enable him to attain the goal of life (Moksha). If the student has not grasped the subject he will have to explain it in some other way with similes? analogies and illustrations. That is the reason why Lord Krishna asks Arjuna Has the delusion of thy ignorance been destroyedThis What I have told thee.Have you heard it? O Arjuna? with onepointed mind Have you grasped My teachingDelusion of ignorance The absence of discrimination which is caused by ignorance and which is natural. The destruction of delusion is the aim of all this endeavour on your part to hear the scripture and the exertion on My part as the teacher.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.73 नष्टः is destroyed? मोहः delusion? स्मृतिः memory (knowledge)? लब्धा has been gained? त्वत्प्रसादात् through Thy grace? मया by me? अच्युत O Krishna? स्थितः अस्मि I remain? गतसन्देहः freed from doubts? करिष्ये (I) will do? वचनम् word? तव Thy.Commentary Moha Delusion This is the strongest weapon of Maya to take the Jivas in Her clutch. It is born of ignorance. It is the cause of the whole evil of Samsara. It is as hard to cross as the ocean.Smritih I have attained knowledge of the true nature of the Self. The whole aim of Sadhana or spiritual practice and the study of scriptures is the annihilation of delusion and the attainment of the knowledge of the Self. When one gets it? the three knots or ties of ignorance? viz.? ignorance? delusion (desire) and action are destroyed? all the doubts are cleared? and all the Karmas are destroyed.To him who beholds the Self in all beings? what delusion is there? what grief (Isavasya Upanishad? 7)I shall do Thy word Arjuna means to say? I am firm in Thy ?nd. Through Thy grace I have achieved the end of life. I have nothing more to do.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.74 इति thus? अहम् I? वासुदेवस्य of Krishna? पार्थस्य of Arjuna? च and? महात्मनः highsouled? संवादम् dialogue? इमम् this? अश्रौषम् (I) have heard? अद्भुतम् wonderful? रोमहर्षणम् which causes the hair to stand on end.Commentary Wonderful because it deals with Yoga and transcendental spiritual matters that pertain to the mysterious immortal Self.Whenever good? higher emotions manifest themselves in the heart the hair stands on end. Devotees often experience this horripilation.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.75 व्यासप्रसादात् through the grace of Vyasa? श्रुतवान् have heard? एतत् this? गुह्यम् secret? अहम् I? परम् supreme? योगम् Yoga? योगेश्वरात् from the Lord of Yoga? कृष्णात् from Krishna? साक्षात् directly? कथयतः declaring? स्वयम् Himself.Commentary Through the grace of Vyasa By obtaining the divine eye from him.Yoga This dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna? I have heard it direct from Him. This dialogue is called Yoga because it treats of Yoga and it leads to the attainment of union with the Lord.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.76 राजन् O King? संस्मृत्य having remembered? संस्मृत्य having remembered? संवादम् the dialogue? इमम् this? अद्भुतम् wonderful? केशवार्जुनयोः between Kesava and Arjuna? पुण्यम् holy? हृष्यामि (I) rejoice? च and? मुहुः again? मुहुः again.Commentary Rajan King Dhritarashtra to whom the Gita is narrated by Sanjaya.Punyam Holy because the mere hearing of the dialogue destroys a multitude of sins and makes the hearer pious and Godfearing and turns his mind towards God.

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.77 तत् that? च and? संस्मृत्य having remembered? संस्मृत्य having remembered? रूपम् the form? अत्यद्भुतम् the most wonderful? हरेः of Hari? विस्मयः wonder? मे my? महान् great? राजन् O King? हृष्यामि (I) rejoice? च and? पुनः again? पुनः again.Commentary Form The Cosmic Form. (Cf.XI)

author: Swami Sivananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.78 यत्र wherever? योगेश्वरः the Lord of Yoga? कृष्णः Krishna? यत्र wherever? पार्थः Arjuna? धनुर्धरः the archer? तत्र there? श्रीः prosperity? विजयः victory? भूतिः happiness? ध्रुवा firm? नीतिः policy? मतिः conviction? मम my.Commentary This verse is called the Ekasloki Gita? i.e.? Bhagavad Gita in one verse. Repetition of even this one verse bestows the benefits of reading the whole of the scripture.Wherever On that side on which.Yogesvarah The Lord of Yoga. Krishna is called the Lord of Yogas as the seed of all Yogas comes forth from Him.Dhanurdharah The wielder of the bow called the Gandiva. There On the side of the Pandavas.Thus in the Upanishads of the glorious Bhagavad Gita? the science of the Eternal? the scripture of Yoga? the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna? ends the eighteenth discourse entitledThe Yoga of Liberation by Renunciation.OM SHANTIH SHANTIH SHANTIH ,,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.13 And immediately all the conches and drums, the trumpets and horns, blared forth in tumultuous uproar.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.14 Then seated in their spacious war chariot, yoked with white horses, Lord Shri Krishna and Arjuna sounded their divine shells.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.15 Lord Shri Krishna blew his Panchajanya and Arjuna his Devadatta, brave Bheema his renowned shell, Poundra.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.16 The King Dharmaraja, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya, Nakalu and Sahadeo, the Sugosh and Manipushpaka, respectively.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.17 And the Maharaja of Benares, the great archer, Shikhandi, the great soldier, Dhrishtayumna, Virata and Satyaki, the invincible,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.18 And O King! Drupada, the sons of Droupadi and Soubhadra, the great soldier, blew their conches.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.19 The tumult rent the hearts of the sons of Dhritarashtra, and violently shook heaven and earth with its echo.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.20 Then beholding the sons of Dhritarashtra, drawn up on the battle- field, ready to fight, Arjuna, whose flag bore the Hanuman,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.21 Raising his bow, spoke this to the Lord Shri Krishna: O Infallible! Lord of the earth! Please draw up my chariot betwixt the two armies,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.22 So that I may observe those who must fight on my side, those who must fight against me;

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.23 And gaze over this array of soldiers, eager to please the sinful sons of Dhritarashtra."

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.24 Sanjaya said: "Having listened to the request of Arjuna, Lord Shri Krishna drew up His bright chariot exactly in the midst between the two armies,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.25 Whither Bheeshma and Drona had led all the rulers of the earth, and spoke thus: O Arjuna! Behold these members of the family of Kuru assembled.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.26 There Arjuna noticed fathers, grandfathers, uncles, cousins, sons, grandsons, teachers, friends;

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.27 Fathers-in-law and benefactors, arrayed on both sides. Arjuna then gazed at all those kinsmen before him.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.28 And his heart melted with pity and sadly he spoke: O my Lord! When I see all these, my own people, thirsting for battle,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.29 My limbs fail me and my throat is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.30 The bow Gandeeva slips from my hand, and my skin burns. I cannot keep quiet, for my mind is in tumult.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.31 The omens are adverse; what good can come from the slaughter of my people on this battlefield?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.32 Ah my Lord! I crave not for victory, nor for the kingdom, nor for any pleasure. What were a kingdom or happiness or life to me,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.33 When those for whose sake I desire these things stand here about to sacrifice their property and their lives:

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.34 Teachers, fathers and grandfathers, sons and grandsons, uncles, father-in-law, brothers-in-law and other relatives.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.35 I would not kill them, even for three worlds; why then for this poor earth? It matters not if I myself am killed.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.36 My Lord! What happiness can come from the death of these sons of Dhritarashtra? We shall sin if we kill these desperate men.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.37 We are worthy of a nobler feat than to slaughter our relatives - the sons of Dhritarashtra; for, my Lord, how can we be happy of we kill our kinsmen?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.38 Although these men, blinded by greed, see no guilt in destroying their kin, or fighting against their friends,

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.39 Should not we, whose eyes are open, who consider it to be wrong to annihilate our house, turn away from so great a crime?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.40 The destruction of our kindred means the destruction of the traditions of our ancient lineage, and when these are lost, irreligion will overrun our homes.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.41 When irreligion spreads, the women of the house begin to stray; when they lose their purity, adulteration of the stock follows.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.42 Promiscuity ruins both the family and those who defile it; while the souls of our ancestors droop, through lack of the funeral cakes and ablutions.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.43 By the destruction of our lineage and the pollution of blood, ancient class traditions and family purity alike perish.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.44 The wise say, my Lord, that they are forever lost, whose ancient traditions are lost.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.45 Alas, it is strange that we should be willing to kill our own countrymen and commit a great sin, in order to enjoy the pleasures of a kingdom.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.46 If, on the contrary, the sons of Dhritarashtra, with weapons in their hand, should slay me, unarmed and unresisting, surely that would be better for my welfare!"

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.47 Sanjaya said: "Having spoken thus, in the midst of the armies, Arjuna sank on the seat of the chariot, casting away his bow and arrow; heartbroken with grief."

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.1 Sanjaya then told how the Lord Shri Krishna, seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with compassion, his eyes dimmed with flowing tears and full of despondency, consoled him:

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.2 "The Lord said: My beloved friend! Why yield, just on the eve of battle, to this weakness which does no credit to those who call themselves Aryans, and only brings them infamy and bars against them the gates of heaven?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.3 O Arjuna! Why give way to unmanliness? O thou who art the terror of thine enemies! Shake off such shameful effeminacy, make ready to act!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.4 Arjuna argued: My Lord! How can I, when the battle rages, send an arrow through Bheeshma and Drona, who should receive my reverence?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.5 Rather would I content myself with a beggar's crust that kill these teachers of mine, these precious noble souls! To slay these masters who are my benefactors would be to stain the sweetness of life's pleasures with their blood.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.6 Nor can I say whether it were better that they conquer me or for me to conquer them, since would no longer care to live if I killed these sons of Dhritarashtra, now preparing for fight.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.7 My heart is oppressed with pity; and my mind confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Thy disciple. Please direct me, I pray.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.8 For should I attain the monarchy of the visible world, or over the invisible world, it would not drive away the anguish which is now paralysing my senses."

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.9 Sanjaya continued: "Arjuna, the conqueror of all enemies, then told the Lord of All-Hearts that he would no fight, and became silent, O King!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.10 Thereupon the Lord, with a gracious smile, addressed him who was so much depressed in the midst of the two armies.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.11 Lord Shri Krishna said: Why grieve for those for whom no grief is due, and yet profess wisdom? The wise grieve neither for the dead nor the living.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.12 There was never a time when I was not, nor thou, nor these princes were not; there will never be a time when we shall cease to be.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.13 As the soul experiences in this body infancy, youth and old age, so finally it passes into another. The wise have no delusion about this.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.14 Those external relations which bring cold and heat, pain and happiness, they come and go; they are not permanent. Endure them bravely, O Prince!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.15 The hero whose soul is unmoved by circumstance, who accepts pleasure and pain with equanimity, only he is fit for immortality.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.16 That which is not, shall never be; that which is, shall never cease to be. To the wise, these truths are self-evident.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.17 The Spirit, which pervades all that we see, is imperishable. Nothing can destroy the Spirit.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.18 The material bodies which this Eternal, Indestructible, Immeasurable Spirit inhabits are all finite. Therefore fight, O Valiant Man!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.19 He who thinks that the Spirit kills, and he who thinks of It as killed, are both ignorant. The Spirit kills not, nor is It killed.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.20 It was not born; It will never die, nor once having been, can It cease to be. Unborn, Eternal, Ever-enduring, yet Most Ancient, the Spirit dies not when the body is dead.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.21 He who knows the Spirit as Indestructible, Immortal, Unborn, Always-the-Same, how should he kill or cause to be killed?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.22 As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new, so the Spirit throws off Its worn-out bodies and takes fresh ones.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.23 Weapons cleave It not, fire burns It not, water drenches It not, and wind dries It not.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.24 It is impenetrable; It can be neither drowned nor scorched nor dried. It is Eternal, All-pervading, Unchanging, Immovable and Most Ancient.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.25 It is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, the immutable. Wherefore, knowing the Spirit as such, thou hast no cause to grieve.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.26 Even if thou thinkest of It as constantly being born, constantly dying, even then, O Mighty Man, thou still hast no cause to grieve.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.27 For death is as sure for that which is born, as birth is for that which is dead. Therefore grieve not for what is inevitable.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.28 The end and the beginning of beings are unknown. We see only the intervening formations. Then what cause is there for grief?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.29 One hears of the Spirit with surprise, another thinks It marvellous, the third listens without comprehending. Thus, though many are told about It, scarcely is there one who knows It.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.30 Be not anxious about these armies. The Spirit in man is imperishable.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.31 Thou must look at thy duty. Nothing can be more welcome to a soldier than a righteous war. Therefore to waver in this resolve is unworthy, O Arjuna!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.32 Blessed are the soldiers who find their opportunity. This opportunity has opened for thee the gates of heaven.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.33 Refuse to fight in this righteous cause, and thou wilt be a traitor, lost to fame, incurring only sin.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.34 Men will talk forever of thy disgrace; and to the noble, dishonour is worse than death.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.35 Great generals will think that thou hast fled from the battlefield through cowardice; though once honoured thou wilt seem despicable.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.36 Thine enemies will spread scandal and mock at thy courage. Can anything be more humiliating?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.37 If killed, thou shalt attain Heaven; if victorious, enjoy the kingdom of earth. Therefore arise, O Son of Kunti, and fight!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.38 Look upon pleasure and pain, victory and defeat, with an equal eye. Make ready for the combat, and thou shalt commit no sin.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.39 I have told thee the philosophy of Knowledge. Now listen and I will explain the philosophy of Action, by means of which, O Arjuna, thou shalt break through the bondage of all action.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.40 On this Path, endeavour is never wasted, nor can it ever be repressed. Even a very little of its practice protects one from great danger.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.41 By its means, the straying intellect becomes steadied in the contemplation of one object only; whereas the minds of the irresolute stray into bypaths innumerable.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.42 Only the ignorant speak in figurative language. It is they who extol the letter of the scriptures, saying, There is nothing deeper than this.'

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.43 Consulting only their own desires, they construct their own heaven, devising arduous and complex rites to secure their own pleasure and their own power; and the only result is rebirth.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.44 While their minds are absorbed with ideas of power and personal enjoyment, they cannot concentrate their discrimination on one point.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.45 The Vedic Scriptures tell of the three constituents of life - the Qualities. Rise above all of them, O Arjuna, above all the pairs of opposing sensations; be steady in truth, free from worldly anxieties and centered in the Self.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.46 As a man can drink water from any side of a full tank, so the skilled theologian can wrest from any scripture that which will serve his purpose.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.47 But thou hast only the right to work, but none to the fruit thereof. Let not then the fruit of thy action be thy motive; nor yet be thou enamored of inaction.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.48 Perform all thy actions with mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye. Spirituality implies equanimity.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.49 Physical action is far inferior to an intellect concentrated on the Divine. Have recourse then to Pure Intelligence. It is only the petty-minded who work for reward.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.50 When a man attains to Pure Reason, he renounces in this world the results of good and evil alike. Cling thou to Right Action. Spirituality is the real art of living.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.51 The sages guided by Pure Intellect renounce the fruit of action; and, freed from the chains of rebirth, they reach the highest bliss.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.52 When thy reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, then shalt thou become indifferent both to the philosophies thou hast heard and to those thou mayest yet hear.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.53 When the intellect, bewildered by the multiplicity of holy scripts, stands unperturbed in blissful contemplation of the Infinite, then hast thou attained Spirituality.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.54 Arjuna asked: My Lord! How can we recognise the saint who has attained Pure Intellect, who has reached this state of Bliss, and whose mind is steady? how does he talk, how does he live, and how does he act?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.55 Lord Shri Krishna replied: When a man has given up the desires of his heart and is satisfied with the Self alone, be sure that he has reached the highest state.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.56 The sage, whose mind is unruffled in suffering, whose desire is not roused by enjoyment, who is without attachment, anger or fear - take him to be one who stands at that lofty level.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.57 He who wherever he goes is attached to no person and to no place by ties of flesh; who accepts good and evil alike, neither welcoming the one nor shrinking from the other - take him to be one who is merged in the Infinite.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.58 He who can withdraw his senses from the attraction of their objects, as the tortoise draws his limbs within its shell - take it that such a one has attained Perfection.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.59 The objects of sense turn from him who is abstemious. Even the relish for them is lost in him who has seen the Truth.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.60 O Arjuna! The mind of him, who is trying to conquer it, is forcibly carried away in spite of his efforts, by his tumultuous senses.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.61 Restraining them all, let him meditate steadfastly on Me; for who thus conquers his senses achieves perfection.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.62 When a man dwells on the objects of sense, he creates an attraction for them; attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.63 Anger induces delusion; delusion, loss of memory; through loss of memory, reason is shattered; and loss of reason leads to destruction.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.64 But the self-controlled soul, who moves amongst sense objects, free from either attachment or repulsion, he wins eternal Peace.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.65 Having attained Peace, he becomes free from misery; for when the mind gains peace, right discrimination follows.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.66 Right discrimination is not for him who cannot concentrate. Without concentration, there cannot be meditation; he who cannot meditate must not expect peace; and without peace, how can anyone expect happiness?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.67 As a ship at sea is tossed by the tempest, so the reason is carried away by the mind when preyed upon by straying senses.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.68 Therefore, O Might-in-Arms, he who keeps his senses detached from their objects - take it that his reason is purified.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.69 The saint is awake when the world sleeps, and he ignores that for which the world lives.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.70 He attains Peace, into whom desires flow as rivers into the ocean, which though brimming with water remains ever the same; not he whom desire carries away.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.71 He attains Peace who, giving up desire, moves through the world without aspiration, possessing nothing which he can call his own, and free from pride.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.72 O Arjuna! This is the state of the Self, the Supreme Spirit, to which if a man once attain, it shall never be taken from him. Even at the time of leaving the body, he will remain firmly enthroned there, and will become one with the Eternal."

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.1 "Arjuna questioned: My Lord! If Wisdom is above action, why dost Thou advise me to engage in this terrible fight?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.2 Thy language perplexes me and confuses my reason. Therefore please tell me the only way by which I may, without doubt, secure my spiritual welfare.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.3 Lord Shri Krishna replied: In this world, as I have said, there is a twofold path, O Sinless One! There is the Path of Wisdom for those who meditate, and the Path of Action for those who work.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.4 No man can attain freedom from activity by refraining from action; nor can he reach perfection by merely refusing to act.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.5 He cannot even for a moment remain really inactive, for the Qualities of Nature will compel him to act whether he will or no.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.6 He who remains motionless, refusing to act, but all the while brooding over sensuous object, that deluded soul is simply a hypocrite.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.7 But, O Arjuna! All honour to him whose mind controls his senses, for he is thereby beginning to practise Karma-Yoga, the Path of Right Action, keeping himself always unattached.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.8 Do thy duty as prescribed, for action for duty's sake is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of the body would be impossible if man remained inactive.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.9 In this world people are fettered by action, unless it is performed as a sacrifice. Therefore, O Arjuna, let thy acts be done without attachment, as sacrifice only.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.10 In the beginning, when God created all beings by the sacrifice of Himself, He said unto them: Through sacrifice you can procreate, and it shall satisfy all your desires.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.11 Worship the Powers of Nature thereby, and let them nourish you in return; thus supporting each other, you shall attain your highest welfare.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.12 For, fed, on sacrifice, nature will give you all the enjoyment you can desire. But he who enjoys what she gives without returning is, indeed, a robber.'

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.13 The sages who enjoy the food that remains after the sacrifice is made are freed from all sin; but the selfish who spread their feast only for themselves feed on sin only.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.14 All creatures are the product of food, food is the product of rain, rain comes by sacrifice, and sacrifice is the noblest form of action.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.15 All action originates in the Supreme Spirit, which is Imperishable, and in sacrificial action the all-pervading Spirit is consciously present.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.16 Thus he who does not help the revolving wheel of sacrifice, but instead leads a sinful life, rejoicing in the gratification of his senses, O Arjuna, he breathes in vain.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.17 On the other hand, the soul who meditates on the Self is content to serve the Self and rests satisfied within the Self; there remains nothing more for him to accomplish.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.18 He has nothing to gain by the performance or non-performance of action. His welfare depends not on any contribution that an earthly creature can make.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.19 Therefore do thy duty perfectly, without care for the results, for he who does his duty disinterestedly attains the Supreme.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.20 King Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone. Even for the sake of enlightening the world, it is thy duty to act;

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.21 For whatever a great man does, others imitate. People conform to the standard which he has set.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.22 There is nothing in this universe, O Arjuna, that I am compelled to do, nor anything for Me to attain; yet I am persistently active.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.23 For were I not to act without ceasing, O prince, people would be glad to do likewise.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.24 And if I were to refrain from action, the human race would be ruined; I should lead the world to chaos, and destruction would follow.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.25 As the ignorant act, because of their fondness for action, so should the wise act without such attachment, fixing their eyes, O Arjuna, only on the welfare of the world.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.26 But a wise man should not perturb the minds of the ignorant, who are attached to action; let him perform his own actions in the right spirit, with concentration on Me, thus inspiring all to do the same.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.27 Action is the product of the Qualities inherent in Nature. It is only the ignorant man who, misled by personal egotism, says: I am the doer.'

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.28 But he, O Mighty One, who understands correctly the relation of the Qualities to action, is not attached to the act for he perceives that it is merely the action and reaction of the Qualities among themselves.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.29 Those who do not understand the Qualities are interested in the act. Still, the wise man who knows the truth should not disturb the mind of him who does not.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.30 Therefore, surrendering thy actions unto Me, thy thoughts concentrated on the Absolute, free from selfishness and without anticipation of reward, with mind devoid of excitement, begin thou to fight.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.31 Those who always act in accordance with My precepts, firm in faith and without cavilling, they too are freed from the bondage of action.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.32 But they who ridicule My word and do not keep it, are ignorant, devoid of wisdom and blind. They seek but their own destruction.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.33 Even the wise man acts in character with his nature; indeed, all creatures act according to their natures. What is the use of compulsion then?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.34 The love and hate which are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them. They only obstruct the path.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.35 It is better to do thine own duty, however lacking in merit, than to do that of another, even though efficiently. It is better to die doing one's own duty, for to do the duty of another is fraught with danger.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.36 Arjuna asked: My Lord! Tell me, what is it that drives a man to sin, even against his will and as if by compulsion?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.37 Lord Shri Krishna: It is desire, it is aversion, born of passion. Desire consumes and corrupts everything. It is man's greatest enemy.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.38 As fire is shrouded in smoke, a mirror by dust and a child by the womb, so is the universe enveloped in desire.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.39 It is the wise man's constant enemy; it tarnishes the face of wisdom. It is as insatiable as a flame of fire.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.40 It works through the senses, the mind and the reason; and with their help destroys wisdom and confounds the soul.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.41 Therefore, O Arjuna, first control thy senses and then slay desire, for it is full of sin, and is the destroyer of knowledge and of wisdom.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.42 It is said that the senses are powerful. But beyond the senses is the mind, beyond the mind is the intellect, and beyond and greater than intellect is He.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.43 Thus, O Mighty-in-Arms, knowing Him to be beyond the intellect and, by His help, subduing thy personal egotism, kill thine enemy, Desire, extremely difficult though it be."

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.1 "Lord Shri Krishna said: This imperishable philosophy I taught to Viwaswana, the founder of the Sun dynasty, Viwaswana gave it to Manu the lawgiver, and Manu to King Ikshwaku!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.2 The Divine Kings knew it, for it was their tradition. Then, after a long time, at last it was forgotten.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.3 It is the same ancient Path that I have now revealed to thee, since thou are My devotee and My friend. It is the supreme Secret.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.4 Arjuna asked: My Lord! Viwaswana was born before Thee; how then canst Thou have revealed it to him?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.5 Lord Shri Krishna replied: I have been born again and again, from time to time; thou too,O Arjuna! My births are known to Me, but thou knowest not thine.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.6 have no beginning. Though I am imperishable, as well as Lord of all that exists, yet by My own will and power do I manifest Myself.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.7 Whenever spirituality decays and materialism is rampant, then, O Arjuna, I reincarnate Myself!

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.8 To protect the righteous, to destroy the wicked and to establish the kingdom of God, I am reborn from age to age.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.9 He who realises the divine truth concerning My birth and life is not born again; and when he leaves his body, he becomes one with Me.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.10 Many have merged their existences in Mine, being freed from desire, fear and anger, filled always with Me and purified by the illuminating flame of self-abnegation.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.11 Howsoever men try to worship Me, so do I welcome them. By whatever path they travel, it leads to Me at last.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.12 Those who look for success, worship the Powers; and in this world their actions bear immediate fruit.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.13 The four divisions of society (the wise, the soldier, the merchant, the labourer) were created by Me, according to the natural distribution of Qualities and instincts. I am the author of them, though I Myself do no action, and am changeless.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.14 My actions do not fetter Me, nor do I desire anything that they can bring. He who thus realises Me is not enslaved by action.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.15 In the light of wisdom, our ancestors, who sought deliverance, performed their acts. Act thou also, as did our fathers of old.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.16 What is action and what is inaction? It is a question which has bewildered the wise. But I will declare unto thee the philosophy of action, and knowing it, thou shalt be free from evil.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.17 It is necessary to consider what is right action, what is wrong action, and what is inaction, for mysterious is the law of action.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.18 He who can see inaction in action, and action in inaction, is the wisest among men. He is a saint, even though he still acts.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.19 The wise call him a sage, for whatever he undertakes is free from the motive of desire, and his deeds are purified by the fire of Wisdom.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.20 Having surrendered all claim to the results of his actions, always contented and independent, in reality he does nothing, even though he is apparently acting.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.21 Expecting nothing, his mind and personality controlled, without greed, doing bodily actions only; though he acts, yet he remains untainted.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.22 Content with what comes to him without effort of his own, mounting above the pairs of opposites, free from envy, his mind balanced both in success and failure; though he acts, yet the consequences do not bind him.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.23 He who is without attachment, free, his mind centered in wisdom, his actions, being done as a sacrifice, leave no trace behind.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.24 For him, the sacrifice itself is the Spirit; the Spirit and the oblation are one; it is the Spirit Itself which is sacrificed in Its own fire, and the man even in action is united with God, since while performing his act, his mind never ceases to be fixed on Him.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.25 Some sages sacrifice to the Powers; others offer themselves on the alter of the Eternal.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.26 Some sacrifice their physical senses in the fire of self-control; others offer up their contact with external objects in the sacrificial fire of their senses.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.27 Other again sacrifice their activities and their vitality in the Spiritual fire of self-abnegation, kindled by wisdom.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.28 And yet others offer as their sacrifice wealth, austerities and meditation. Monks wedded to their vows renounce their scriptural learning and even their spiritual powers.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.29 There are some who practise control of the Vital Energy and govern the subtle forces of Prana and Apana, thereby sacrificing their Prana unto Apana, or their Apana unto Prana.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.30 Others, controlling their diet, sacrifice their worldly life to the spiritual fire. All understand the principal of sacrifice, and by its means their sins are washed away.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.31 Tasting the nectar of immortality, as the reward of sacrifice, they reach the Eternal. This world is not for those who refuse to sacrifice; much less the other world.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.32 In this way other sacrifices too may be undergone for the Spirit's sake. Know thou that they all depend on action. Knowing this, thou shalt be free.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Shri Purohit Swami did not comment on this sloka

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.34 This shalt thou learn by prostrating thyself at the Master's feet, by questioning Him and by serving Him. The wise who have realised the Truth will teach thee wisdom.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.35 Having known That, thou shalt never again be confounded; and, O Arjuna, by the power of that wisdom, thou shalt see all these people as if they were thine own Self, and therefore as Me.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.36 Be thou the greatest of sinners, yet thou shalt cross over all sin by the ferryboat of wisdom.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.37 As the kindled fire consumes the fuel, so, O Arjuna, in the flame of wisdom the embers of action are burnt to ashes.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.38 There is nothing in the world so purifying as wisdom; and he who is a perfect saint finds that at last in his own Self.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.39 He who is full of faith attains wisdom, and he too who can control his senses, having attained that wisdom, he shall ere long attain Supreme Peace.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.40 But the ignorant man, and he who has no faith, and the sceptic are lost. Neither in this world nor elsewhere is there any happiness in store for him who always doubts.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.41 But the man who has renounced his action for meditation, who has cleft his doubt in twain by the sword of wisdom, who remains always enthroned in his Self, is not bound by his acts.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.42 Therefore, cleaving asunder with the sword of wisdom the doubts of the heart, which thine own ignorance has engendered, follow the Path of Wisdom and arise!"

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.1 "Arjuna said: My Lord! At one moment Thou praisest renunciation of action; at another, right action. Tell me truly, I pray, which of these is the more conducive to my highest welfare?

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.2 Lord Shri Krishna replied: Renunciation of action and the path of right action both lead to the highest; of the two, right action is the better.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.3 He is a true ascetic who never desires or dislikes, who is uninfluenced by the opposites and is easily freed from bondage.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.4 Only the unenlightened speak of wisdom and right action as separate, not the wise. If any man knows one, he enjoys the fruit of both.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.5 The level which is reached by wisdom is attained through right action as well. He who perceives that the two are one, knows the truth.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.6 Without concentration, O Mighty Man, renunciation is difficult. But the sage who is always meditating on the Divine, before long shall attain the Absolute.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.7 He who is spiritual, who is pure, who has overcome his senses and his personal self, who has realised his highest Self as the Self of all, such a one, even though he acts, is not bound by his acts.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.8 Though the saint sees, hears, touches, smells, eats, moves, sleeps and breathes, yet he knows the Truth, and he knows that it is not he who acts.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.9 Though he talks, though he gives and receives, though he opens his eyes and shuts them, he still knows that his senses are merely disporting themselves among the objects of perception.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.10 He who dedicates his actions to the Spirit, without any personal attachment to them, he is no more tainted by sin than the water lily is wetted by water.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.11 The sage performs his action dispassionately, using his body, mind and intellect, and even his senses, always as a means of purification.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.12 Having abandoned the fruit of action, he wins eternal peace. Others unacquainted with spirituality, led by desire and clinging to the benefit which they think will follow their actions, become entangled in them.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.13 Mentally renouncing all actions, the self-controlled soul enjoys bliss in this body, the city of the nine gates, neither doing anything himself nor causing anything to be done.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.14 The Lord of this universe has not ordained activity, or any incentive thereto, or any relation between an act and its consequences. All this is the work of Nature.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.15 The Lord does not accept responsibility for any man's sin or merit. Men are deluded because in them wisdom is submerged in ignorance.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.16 Surely wisdom is like the sun, revealing the supreme truth to those whose ignorance is dispelled by the wisdom of the Self.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.17 Meditating on the Divine, having faith in the Divine, concentrating on the Divine and losing themselves in the Divine, their sins dissolved in wisdom, they go whence there is no return.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.18 Sages look equally upon all, whether he be a minister of learning and humility, or an infidel, or whether it be a cow, an elephant or a dog.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.19 Even in this world they conquer their earth-life whose minds, fixed on the Supreme, remain always balanced; for the Supreme has neither blemish nor bias.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.20 He who knows and lives in the Absolute remains unmoved and unperturbed; he is not elated by pleasure or depressed by pain.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.21 He finds happiness in his own Self, and enjoys eternal bliss, whose heart does not yearn for the contacts of earth and whose Self is one with the Everlasting.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.22 The joys that spring from external associations bring pain; they have their beginning and their endings. The wise man does not rejoice in them.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.23 He who, before he leaves his body, learns to surmount the promptings of desire and anger is a saint and is happy.

author: Shri Purohit Swami
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
