content: 2.53. When your determining faculty, that had been [earlier] confused by your hearing [of scriptural declaration of fruits] shall stand stable in concentration, at that time you shall attain the Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.54. Arjuna said O Kesava ! What is the connotation of sthita-prajna (a man-of-stabilized-intellect), [applied] to a man fixed in concentration ? What would sthira-dhih (the fixed-minded) convey ? Where would the fixed-minded abide ? And what would be reach ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.55. The Bhagavat said O son of Prtha ! When a man casts off all desires existing in his mind and remains content in the Self by the self (mind), then he is called 'a man-of-stabilized-intellect.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.56. He, whose mind is undisturbed in the midst of sorrows; who is free from desire in the midst of pleasures; and from whom longing, fear and wrath have totally gone-he is said to be a firm-minded sage.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.57. He, who has no desire in anything; and who neither rejoices nor hates on getting this or that, good or bad-his intellect is properly stabilized.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.58. When he withdraws all his sense-organs from sense-objects, just as a tortoise does all of its own limbs, then he is declared to be a man-of-stabilized-intellect.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.59. Leaving their taste [behind], the sense-objects retreat from the embodied who abstain from food; his taste too disappears when he sees the Supreme.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.60. For, the turbulent sense-organs do carry away by force, the mind even of this person of discerning, O son of Kunti !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.61. Restraining them (the same-organs) by mind, the master of Yoga would sit making Me his goal; for, the intellect of that person is stabilized whose sense-organs are under control.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.62. In a person, meditating on sense-objects, attachment or them is born in succession; from attachment springs passion; from passion arises wrath.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.63. From wrath delusion comes to be; from delusion is the loss of memory; from the loss of memory is the loss of capacity to decide; due to the loss of capacity to decide, he perishes outright.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.64. On the contrary, one who moves about (consumes) the sense-objects by means of his senseorgans, that are freed from desire and hatred and are controlled in the Self-such one with a disciplined self (mind) attains serenity [of disposition].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.65. On attaining serenity, there arises in succession the extinction of all miseries; the capacity to decide gets stabilized soon indeed in the case of a serene-minded one.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.66. The capacity to decide is not for one who is not a master of Yoga; and concentration of mind is not for one who is not a master of Yoga; and peace is not for one who does not concentrate; wherefrom could happiness come to one who has no peace ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.67. That mind, which is directed to follow the wandering (enjoying) sense-organs-that mind carries away his knowledge just as wind does a ship on waters.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.68. Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the intellect of that person is stabilized, all of whose sense-organs, starting from sense-objects have been well restrained.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.69. What is night for every [other] being, in that a man of self-restraint is awake; wherein [every other] being is awake, that is night for the sage who sees [the truth].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.70. Just as waters enter into the ocean which is being filled continuously and which is [yet] firmly established, in the same way, he into whom all objects of desire enter-he attains peace; not he who longs for the objects of desire.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.71. That person, who, by abandoning all desires, consumes [objects] without longing, without a sense of possession and without egotism-he attains peace.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.72. O son of Prtha ! This is the Brahmanic state; having attained this, one never gets deluded [again]; and even by remaining in this [for a while] one attains at the time of death, the Brahman, the Tranil One.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.1. Arjuna said O Janardana, if knowledg is held to be superior to action by You, then why do You engage me in action that is terrible, O Kesava ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.2. You appear to perplex my intellect with Your speech that looks confusing. Hence tell me, with certainty, that particular thing by which I may attain the good (emancipation).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.3. The Bhagavat said The two-fold path in this world-[the one] with Yoga of knowledge for men of reflection [and the other] with Yoga of action for men of Yoga-has been declared to be one by Me formerly, O sinless one !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.4. A person attains actionlessness not [just] by non-commencement of actions; and not just by renunciation, he attains success (emancipation).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.5. For, no one can ever remain, even for a moment, as a non-performer of action; because everyone, being not master of himself, is forced to perform action by the Strands born of the Prakrti (Material cause)

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.6. Controlling organs of actions, whosoever sits with his mind, pondering over the sense objects-that person is a man of deluded soul and [he] is called a man of deluded action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.7. But, controlling sense-organs by mind, whosoever undertakes the Yoga of action with the action-senses he, the detached one, is superior [to others], O Arjuna !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.8. You must perform your action which has been enjoined. For, action is superior to inaction; and even the maintenance of your body could not be properly accomplished through inaction.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.9. The world is fettered by action which is other than the Yajnartha action; hence, O son of Kunti, being freed from attachment, you most properly perform Yajnartha action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.10. Having created creatures formerly [at the time of creation] together with necessary action, the Lord of creatures declared : 'By means of this, you shalll propagate yourselves; and let this be your wish-fulfilling-cow.'

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.11. 'With this you must gratify the devas and let the devas gratify you; [thus] gratifying one another, you shall attain the highest good.'

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.12. The devas, gratified with necessary action will grant you the things sacrificed. [Hence] whosoever enjoys their gifts without offering them to these devas-he is surely a thief.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.13. The righteous persons, who eat the remnants (objects enjoined) of the actions to be performed necessarily, are freed from all sins. But those who cook, intending their own selves, are sinners and eat sin.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.14. From food arise the things that are born; from the rain-cloud the food arises; from the sacrifice the rain-cloud arises; the sacrifices arises from action;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.15. Action arises from the Brahman, you should know this; the Brhaman arises from what does not stream forth; therefore the all-pervading Brahman is permanently based on the sacrifice.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.16. Whosoever does not roll forward the wheel, thus set in motion in this world, he is a man of sinful life rejoicing in the senses; and he lives in vain, O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.17. But the man, who simply rejoices in the Self; and who is satisfied in the Self; and who delights in the Self alone-there exists no action for him to be performed.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.18. No purpose is served for him by what he has done or by what he has not done. For him there is hardly any dependenc on any purpose among all beings.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.19. Therefore, unattached always, you should perform action that is to be performed; for, the person, performing action without attachment, attains the Supreme.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.20. It was by action alone that Janaka and others had attained emancipation. Further, at least having regard to hold the world (the society) together you should act.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.21. Whatsoever a great man does, other commoners do the same; whatever standard he sets up, the world follows that.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.22. O son of Prtha ! For Me, in the three worlds there is nothing that must be done; nor is there any thing unattained [so far] to be attained; and yet I exert in action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.23. For, if I were ever not at work unwearied, all men would follow My path, O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.24. These worlds would perish if I were not to perform action; and I would be a cause of confusion; I would destroy these people.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.25. [Therefore] just as the unwise persons, being attached to action, do, O son of Prtha, so the wise should perform, [But] being unattached and desiring to hold the world together.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.26. Let the wise master of Yoga fulfil (or destroy) all actions by performing them all, and let him not creat any disturbance in the mind of the ingnorant persons attached to action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.27. The actions are performed part by part, by the Strands of the Prakrti; [yet] the person, having his self (mind) deluded with egoity, imagines 'I am [alone] the doer'.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.28. But, O mighty-armed one, the knower of the real nature of the divisions of the Strands and of their [respective] divisions of work, realises : 'The Strands are at their [respective] purposes' And hence he is not attached.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.29. Men, completely deluded by the Strands of the Prakrti, are attached to the actions of the Strands. Man, who know fully, should not confuse them, the dullard, who do not know fully.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.30. Renouncing all actions in Me, with mind that concentrates on the Self; being free from the act of reesting and from the sense of possession; and [conseently being free from [mental] fever; you should fight.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.31. Those who constantly follow this doctrine of Mine-such men, with faith and without finding fault [in it], are freed from [the results of] all actions.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.32. But those who, finding fault, do not follow this doctrine of Mine-be sure that these men to be highly deluded in all [branches of] knowledge and to be lost and brainless.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.33. Even a man of knowledge acts in conformity to his own Prakrti, the elements go [back] to the Prakrti; [and] what will the restraint avail ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.34. [For a man of worldly life] there are likes and dislikes clearly fixed with regard to the objects of each of his sense organs. These are the obstacles for him. [The wise] would not come under the control of these.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.35. Better is one's own duty, [though] it lacks in merit, than the well-performed duty of another; better is the ruin in one's own duty than the good fortune from another's duty.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.36. Arjuna said Then, induced by what, does this person [of the world] commit sin-eventhough he does not desire it-as if instigated by a force, overpowering [him] ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.37. The Bhagavat said This desire, this wrath, born of the Rajas-Strand, is a swallower of festival [and] a mighty bestower of sins. Know this to be the enemy here.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.38. As the fire is concealed by smoke and a mirror by dirt, and as the embryo is concealed by membrance-cover, so He is concealed by this (foe).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.39. O son of Kunti ! The knowledge of the wise is concealed by this eternal foe, which looks like a desired one, and which is the fire insatiable.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.40. It basis is said to be the sense-organs, the mind and the intellect. With these it deludes the embodied by concealing knowledge.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.41. Therefore, O best among the Bharatas, by controlling completely the sense-organs in the beginning [itself], you must avoid this sinful one, destroying the knowledge-action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.42. Different are the sense-organs [from their objects], they say; from the sense-organs different is the mind; from the mind too the intellect is different; what is different from the intellect is That (Self).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.43. Thus being conscious : 'That is different from the intellect'; and steadying the self with the self; kill the foe that is of the form of desire and that is hard to approach.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.1. The Bhagavat said This changeless Yoga I had properly taught thus to Vivasvat; Vivasvat correctly told it ot Manu; and Manu declared to Iksvaku.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.2. Thus the regal sages knew this, received in regualr succession. By the passage of long time, this Yoga has been however lost, O scorcher of enemies !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.3. The self-same ancient Yoga has been taught now by Me to you on the ground that you are My devotee and friend too. This is the highest secret.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.4. Arjuna said Your birth is later, [while] the birth of Vivasvat is earlier; how am then to understand that You had properly taught [him this] in the beginnig ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.5. The Bhagavat said O Arjuna, many births of Mine, as well as of yours have passed. All of them I do know, but you do not, O scorcher of foes !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.6. Though [I am] unborn and the changeless Self; though I am the the Lord of [all] beings; yet presiding over My own nature I take birth by My own Trick-of-illusion.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.7. For, whenever there is a decay of righteousness and the rise of unrighteousness, then, O descendant of Bharata, I send forth (or create) that is which the Self is unimportant.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.8. For the protection of the good people, and for the destruction of evil-doers, and for the purpose of firmly establishing righteousness, I take birth in every age.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.9. Whosoever knows thus correctly the divine birth and action of Mine, he, on abandoning the body does not go to rirth, [but] goes to Me, O Arjuna !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.10. Many persons, who are free from passion, fear and anger; are full of Me; take refuge in Me; and have become pure by the austerity of wisdom-they have come to My being.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.11. The way in which men resort to Me, in the same way I favour them. O son of Prtha, all sorts of men follow the path of Mine.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.12. Those, who are desirous of success of their actions, perform sacrifices intending the deities. For, the success born of [ritualistic] actions is ick in the world of men.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.13. The four-fold caste-structure has been created by Me, according to the division of [their respective] alities and actions. Though I am the creator of this, know Me as a changeless non-creator.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.14. Actions do not stain Me; nor do I have a desire for the fruits [of actions] also. Whosoever comprehends Me as such, he is not bound by actions.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.15. Realizing in this fashion, action had been under-taken also by ancient seekers of salvation. Hence, you too should perform, by all means, the more ancient action that had been performed by the ancients.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.16. Even the wise are perplexed about what is action and what is non-action; I shall preperly teach you the action, by knowing which you shall be freed from evil.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.17. Something has got to be understand of [good] action also; and something is to be understood of the wrong action; and something is to be understood of non-action. Difficult is to comprehend the way of action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.18. He, who finds non-action in the action, and action in the non-action, is an intelligent one, among men and is said to be a performer or destroyer of all actions.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.19. He, whose every exertion is devoid of intention for the desirable objects, and whose actions are burnt up by the fire of wisdom-him the wise call a man of learning.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.20. By abandoning attachment for fruits of actions, remaining ever content and depending on nothing, that person, even though he is engaged in action, does not at all perform anything.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.21. Being rid of cravings, having mind and self (body) all controlled, abandoning all sense of possession, and performing exclusively bodily action, he does not incur any sin.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.22. Remaining contended wiht the gain brought by chance, transcending the dualities (pairs of opposites), entertaining no jealously, and remaning eal in success and in failure, he does not get bound, even when he acts.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.23. The action gets dissolved completely in the case of the person who undertakes it for the sake of sacrifice; who is rid of attachment and is freed; and who has his mind fixed in wisdom.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.24. The Brahman-oblation that is to be offered ot the Brahman, is poured into the Brahman-fire by the Brahman; it is nothing but the Brahman that is to be attained by him whose deep contemplation is the [said] Brahman-action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.25. Certain other men of Yoga are completely devoted to yajna, connected with the devas and offer that yajna, simply as a yajna, into the insatiable fire of the Brahman.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.26. [Yet] others offer the sense-organs like sense-of-hearing and the rest into the fiires of [their] restrainer; others offer the objects like sound and the rest into the fires of the sense-organs.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.27. Some others offer all actions of their sense-organs and the actions of their life-breath into the fire of Yoga of the self control, set ablaze by wisdom.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.28. [These] are [respectively] the performs of sacrifices with material objects, the performers of sacrifices with penance, and the performers of sacrifices with Yoga. Likewise [there are] yet other ascetics with rigid vows whose sacrifices are the svadhyaya-knowledge.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.29. - 4.30. [Some sages] offer the prana into the apana; like-wise others offer the apana into the prana. Having controlled both the courses of the prana and apana, the same sages, with their desire fulfilled by the above activities, and with their food restricted, offer the pranas into pranas. All these persons know what sacrifices are and have their sins destroyed by sacrifices.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.29. - 4.30. [Some sages] offer the prana into the apana; like-wise others offer the apana into the prana. Having controlled both the courses of the prana and apana, the same sages, with their desire fulfilled by the above activities, and with their food restricted, offer the pranas into pranas. All these persons know what sacrifices are and have their sins destroyed by sacrifices.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.31. The eaters of the sacrifice-ordained (or sacrificial remnant) nectar, attain the eternal Brahman. [Even] this world is not for a non-sacrificer, how can there be the other ? O best of the Kurus !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.32. Thus, sacrifices of many varieties have been elaborated in the mouth of the Brahman. Know them all as having sprung from actions. By knowing thus you shall be liberated.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Dr.S.Sankaranarayan did not comment on this sloka

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.34. This you should learn [from those, endowed with knowledge], by prostration, by iniry and by service [all offered to them]; those who are endowed with knowledge and are capable of showing the truth will give you the truth nearby;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.35. By knowing which you shall not get deluded once again in this manner, O son of Pandu; and by which means you shall see all beings without exception in [your] Self i.e., in Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.36. Even if you are the highest sinner amongst all sinners, you shall cross over [the ocean of] all the sin just by the boat of knowledge.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.37. Just as the fire, well inflamed, reduces the fuels to ashes, so also the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.38. In this world there exists no purifier comparabel to knowledge. One who becomes perfect in Yoga finds this, on his own accord, in his Self in course of time.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.39. He, who has faith, gains knowledge, if he is solely intending upon it and has his sense-organs well-controlled; having gained the knowledge, he attains, before long, the Peace Supreme.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.40. But he, who is ignorant and has no faith, perishes, with his self (mind) full of doubts. Neither this world nor the other, nor happiness is for a person, who is by nature is full of doubts.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.41. O Dhananjaya ! Actions do not bind him who has renounced [all] actions through Yoga; who has cut off his doubts by the sword of knowledge; and who is a master of his own self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.42. Therefore, thus cutting off, by means of knowledge-sword, the doubt that has sprung from ignornace and exists in [your] heart, practise the Yoga ! Stand up ! O descendant of Bharata !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.1. Arjuna said O krsna, you commend renunciation of action and again the Yoga of action; which one of these two is superior [to the other] ? Please tell me that for certain.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.2. The Bhagavat said Both renunciation and the Yoga of action effect salvation. But, of these two, the Yoga of action is better than renunciation of action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.3. That person may be considered a man of permanent renunciation, who neither hates nor desires. For, O mighty-armed ! he who is free from the pairs [of opposites] is easily released from bondage [of action].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.4. The childish, and not the wise, proclaim the paths of knowledge and the Yoga as different. He, who has properly resorted to even one [of these two], gets the fruit of both.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.5. What state is reached by men of knowledge-path the same is reached by men of Yoga subseently. [So] whosoever sees the knowledge-path and the Yoga to be one, he sees [correctly].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.6. O mighty-armed (Arjuna) ! Renunciation is certainly hard to attain excepting through Yoga; the sage who is the master of Yoga attains the Brahman, before long.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.7. A master of Yoga, whose self (mind and intellect) is very pure and is fully subdued, the sense-organs controlled, and Soul is [realised to be] the Soul of all beings-he is not stained, eventhough he is a performer [of actions].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.8. A master of Yoga, knowing the reality would think 'I do not perform any action at all'. For, he who, while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping and breathing;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.9. Taking, rejecting, receiving, opening and closing the eyes, bears in mind that the sense-organs are on their respective objects; and

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.10. Who performs actions by offering them to the Brahman and giving up attachment-he is not stained by sin just as the lotus-leaf is [not stained] by water.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.11. Having given up attachment, the men of Yoga perform action, just with the body, with the mind, with intellect and also with sense-organs, for attaining the Self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.12. Having abandoned [the attachment for] the fruit of actions, the master of Yoga attains the highest Peace. [But] the person, other than the master of Yoga, attached to the fruit of action, is bound by his action born of desire.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.13. Having renounced all actions by mind, a man of self-control, dwells happily in his body, a nine-win-dowed mansion, neither performing, nor causing others to perform [actions].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.14. The Lord (Self) acires neither the state of being a creator of the world, nor the actions, nor the connecting with the fruits of their actions. But it is the inherent nature [in It] that exerts.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.15. The Omnimanifest (Soul) takes [upon Itself] neither sin nor merit [born] of any [action]. But, the perfect knowledge is clouded by Illusion and hence the creatures are deluded.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.16. In the case of those whose Illusion has been, however, destroyed by the Self-knowledge, then for them that knowledge illumines itself, like the sun.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.17. Those, who have their intellect and self (mind) gone to This; who have established themselves in This and have This [alone] as their supreme goal; and who have washed off their sins by means of [perfect] knowledge-they reach a state from which there is no more return.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.18. The wise men look, by nature, eally upon a Brahmana, rich in learning and humility, on a cow, on an elephant, and on a mere dog and on a dog-cooker (an out-caste).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.19. The Brahman-knower, who is disillusioned, who is established in Brahman and has a firm intellect, would neither rejoice on meeting a friend nor get agitated on meeting a foe.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.20. He who, with his self (mind) not attached to the external contacts, finds happiness in the Self-that person, with his self engaged in the Yoga, pervades easily, suffering no loss, the Brahman.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.21. The enjoyments that are born of contacts [with objects] are indeed nothing but sources of misery and have beginning and end. [Hence], an intelligent man does not get delighted in them, O son of Kunti !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.22. Whosoever, right here, before abandoning the body, is capable of bearing the force sprung from desire and wrath-he is considered to be a man of Yoga and a happy man.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.23. He, whose pleasure, delight and again light are just within-O son of Prtha ! he attains the supreme Yoga, himself becoming the Brahman.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.24. The seers, whose dirts have decayed; by whom dualities have been out off; whose self (mind) is controlled; and who are delighted in the welfare of all; they gain the Brahman, the Tranil One.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.25. At all times there is the tranil Brahman for the ascetics who have severed their connection with desire and anger, who have controlled their mind and have realised their Self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.26. Warding off the external contacts outside; making the sense of sight in the middle of the two wandering ones; counter-balancing both the forward and backward moving forces that travel within what acts crookedly;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.27. The sage, who has controlled his sense-organs, mind and intellect; whose chief aim is emancipation; and from whom desire, fear and wrath have departed-he remains just free always.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.28. Having known Me as the Enjoyer of [the fruits of] sacrifices and austerties, as the great Lord of all the worlds, and as the Friend of all beings, he (the man of Yoga) attains peace.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.29. There is no such translation for this sloka.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.1. The Bhagavat said He who performs his bounden action, not depending on its fruit, in the man of renunciation and also the man of Yoga ! and not he, who remains [simply] without his fires and actions [is a Samnyasin or a Yogin]

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.2. What [the learned] call renunciation, O son of Pandu, know that to be [the same as] the Yoga. For without renouncing intention [for fruit], one does not become a man of Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.3. For a sage, who is desirous of mounting upon the Yoga, action is said to be the cause; for the same [sage], when he has mounted upon the Yoga, ietude is said to be the cause.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.4. When, a person indulges himself neither in what is desired by the senses nor in the actions [for it], then [alone], being a man renouncing all intentions, he is said to have mounted on the Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.5. Let a person lift the Self by self and let him not depress the Self. For, the self alone is the friend of the Self and self alone is the foe of the Self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.6. The self is the friend of that Self by Which the self has been verily subdued; but [in the case of] a person with an unsubdued self, the self alone would abide in enmity like an enemy.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.7. The thinking of the person, with subdued mind and [hence] with complete calmness, remains in eilibrium in the case of others and of himself, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, like-wise in honour and dishonour.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.8. He, whose self (mind) is satisfied with knowledge and with what consists of varied thoughts; who remains peak-like and has completely subdued his sense organs; and to whom a clod, a stone and a piece of gold are the same-that man of Yoga is called a master of Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.9. He whose mind is eal in the case of the friend, companion, enemy, the indifferent one, the one who remains in the middle, the foe, the relative, the righteous and also the sinful-he excells [all].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.10. Let the man of Yoga yoke always the self (mind) by remaining alone in a lonely place, with his mind and self (body) controlled, without desire and without the sense of possession.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.11. Setting up in a clean place his own [suitable] firm seat which is predominantly of cloth, skin and kusa-grass, and which, is neither too high nor too low for him;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.12. Sitting there on the seat and making the mind single-pointed, let him, with the activities of his mind and senses subdued, practise Yoga for self-purification.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.13. Holding the body, the head and the neck erect and motionless; remaining firm; looking properly at his own nose-tip; and not looking at [different] directions;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.14. Being calm-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of celibacy; controlling mind fully; let the master of Yoga remain, fixing his mind in Me and having Me [alone] as his supreme goal.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.15. Yoking his self (mind) incessantly in this manner, My devotee, with mind not attached to anything else, realises peace which culminates in the nirvana and is in the form of ending in Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.16. Yoga is neither for him who eats too much; nor for him who totally abstains from eating; nor for him who is prone to sleep too much; and nor for him who keeps awake too much.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.17. The Yoga becomes a misery-killer for him whose effort for food is appropriate, exertion in activities is proper, and sleep and waking are proportionate.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.18. When [his] well-controlled mind gets established in nothing but the Self and he is free from craving for any desired object-at that time his is called a master of Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.19. 'Just as a lamp in the windless place does not shake' - This simile is recalled in the case of the man of Yoga, with subdued mind, practising the Yoga in the Self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.20. Where the mind, well-restrained through Yoga-practice, remains iet; again where, observing, by the self, nothing but the Self, he (Yogi) is satisfied in the Self;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.21. Where he realises that limitless Bliss Which is to be grasped by intellect and is beyond sences; remaining Where he does not stir out from the Reality;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.22. And having attained Which, he does not think of any other gain as superior to That; being established in Which he is not shaken much by misery, however powerful that may be;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.23. That he would realise to be the cause for [his] cessation of [his] contact with misery and to be the one made known by Yoga. With determination That is to be yoked in Yoga by a person of undepressed mind (or of the depressed mind).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.24. In order ot renounce completely all desires that are born of intention, let a person, restraining the group of sense-organs from all sides by mind alone;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.25. Very slowly remain iet, keeping the mind well established in the Self by means of the intellect held in steadiness; and lest him not think of anything (object).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.26. By whatever things the shaky and unsteady mind goes astray, from those things let him restrain it and bring it back to the control of the Self alone.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.27. Indeed the Supreme Bliss comes to this highly tranil-minded man of Yoga, whose passions remain ietened, who has become the Brahman and who is free from sins.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.28. Thus yoking the self always, the man of Yoga, with subdued mind, easily attains a complete union [viz.,] the Brahman.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.29. He, who has yoked the self in Yoga and observes everything eally perceives the Self to be abiding in all beings and all beings to be abiding in the Self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.30. He who observes Me in all and observes all in Me-for him I am not lost and he too is not lost for me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.31. He, who, established firmly in the oneness (of Me), experiences Me immanent in all beings-that man of Yoga, is never stained, in whatever stage he may be.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.32. Whosoever finds pleasure or pain eally in all as in the case of himself-that person is considered to be a great man of Yoga, O Arjuna !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.33. Arjuna said This Yoga of eal-mindedness which has been spoken of by You, O slayer of Mandhu, I do not find [any] proper foundation for it, because of the unsteadiness of the mind.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.34. O Krsna ! The mind is indeed unsteady, destructive, strong and obstinate; to control it, I believe, is very difficult, just as to control the wind.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.35. The Bhagavat said O mighty-armed ! No doubt, the mind is unsteady and is hard to control. But it is controlled by practice and through an attitude of desirelessness, O son of Kunti !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.36. My belief is that attaining Yoga is difficult for a man of uncontrolled self (mind); but it is possible to attain by [proper] means by a person who exerts with his subdued self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.37. Arjuna said A person who has faith and is desirous of reaching the path (goal) of the good; [but] whose mind has severed from the Yoga; to which goal does he go, having failed to attain the success in Yoga ? O Krsna !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Dr.S.Sankaranarayan did not comment on this sloka

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.39. Please dispel this doubt of mine completely. But for Yourself, O Krsna, no eradicator of this doubt is possible.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.40. The Bhagavat said O dear Partha ! Neither in this [world], nor in the other is there a destruction for him. Certainly, no performer of an auspicious act does ever come to a grievous state.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.41. Having attained the worlds of performers of pious acts, [and] having resided there for years of Sasvata, the fallen-from-Yoga is born [again] in the house of the pure persons, who are rich.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.42. Or, he is born (rorn) nowhere other than in the family of the intelligent men of Yoga; for, this birth is more difficult to get in the world.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.43. There in that life, he gains (regains) that link of mentality transmitted from his former body. Conseently once again he strives for a full success, O rejoicer of the Kurus !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.44. Being not a master of himself, he is dragged only by that former practice (its mental impression); only a seeker of the knowledge of the Yoga passes over what strengthens the [sacred] text.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.45. After that, the assiduously striving man of Yoga, having his sins completely cleansed and being perfected through many briths, reaches the Supreme Goal.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.46. The man of Yoga is superior to the men of austerities and is considered superior even to the men of knowledge; and the man of Yoga is superior to the men of action. Therefore, O Arjuna ! you shall become a man of Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.47. He, who has faith and serves Me with his inner self gone to Me, he is considered by Me as the best master of Yoga, among all the men of Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.1. The Bhagavat said O son of Prtha, hear [from Me] how, having your mind attached to Me, practising Yoga and taking refuge in Me, you shall understand Me fully, without any doubt.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.2. I Shall teach you this knowledge in full together with action; for a person who has known this there remains in this world nothing else to be known.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.3. Among thousands of men, perchance, one makes effort for the determined knowledge. Among those, having the determined knowledge-even though they make effort-perchance one realises Me correctly.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.4. My nature is divided eightfold, such as the Earth, the Water, the Fire, the Wind, the Ether, the Mind, and also the Intellect and the Ego;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.5. This is the lower [nature of Mine]. Not different from this is My superior nature which has become the individual Soul and by which this world is maintained. O mighty armed (Arjuna), you must know this.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.6. All beings are born of this womb. Hence keep [them] nearby. I am the origin as well as the dissolution of the entire world.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.7. There exists nothing beyond Me, O Dhananjaya; all this is strung on Me just as the groups of pearls on a string.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.8. O son of Kunti ! I am the taste in waters; the light in the moon and the sun; the best hymn (OM) in the entire Vedas; the sound that exists in the ether (or the mystic hymnal sound in the entire Vedas-a sound that is in the ether); and the manly vigour in men.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.9. I am the pure smell in the earth; I am also the brilliance in the sun; I am the life in al beings and austerity in the ascetics.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.10. O son of Prtha ! Know Me as the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intellect of the intellectuals and the brillinace of the brilliant.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.11. Of the strong, I am the strength that is free from desire and attachment. O best of the Bharatas, in [all] beings I am the desire which is not opposed to attributes.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.12. Whatever beings are there [in the universe]-whether they are of the Sattva or of Rajas or of Tamas (Strands)- be sure that they are from Me; I am not in them, but they are in Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.13. Being duluded by these three beings of the Strands, this entire world does not recognise Me Who am eternal and transcending these [Strands].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.14. This is My play (daivi), trick-of-Illusion composed of the Strands and is hard to cross over. Those, who resort to Me alone-they cross over the trick-of-Illusion.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.15. The deluded evil-doers, the vilest men, who are robbed of knowledge by the trick-of-Illusion and have taken refuge in the demoniac nature-they do not resort to Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.16. Men of good action who worship Me always are of four types: the afflicted, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth and the man of wisdom, O best among the Bharatas !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.17. Of them, the man of wisdom, being always attached [to Me] with single-pointed devotion excels [others]. For, I am dear to the man of wisdom above all personal gains and he is dear to Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.18. All these are noble persons, indeed. But the man of wisdom is considered as the very Soul of [Mine]. For, with his self (mind) that has mastered the Yoga, he has resorted to nothing but Me as his most supreme goal.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.19. At the end of many births, one attains Me with the conviction that 'All is Vasudeva' - that noble Soul is very difficult to get.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.20. Being robbed of their wisdom by innumerable desires [and] being controlled by their own nature, persons take refuge in other deities by following one or the other religious regulations.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.21. Whatever may be the form [of the deity] a devotee-whosoever he may be-desires to worship with faith, I assume that form which is firm and is according to [his] faith.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.22. Endowed with that faith, he seeks to worship that deity and therefrom receives his desired objects that are ordained by none but Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.23. But, that fruit of those men of poor intellect is finite. Those, who perform sacrifices, aiming at the gods, go to gods, and My devotees go to Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.24. The men of poor intellect, are not conscious of the higher, changeless and supreme nature of Mine; and hence, they regard Me, the Unmanifest, to be a manifest one.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.25. Being surrounded by the trick-of-yoga-Illusion, I am not clear to all; [and hence] this deluded world [of perceivers] does not recognise Me, the unborn and the undying.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.26. O Arjuna, I know the beings that are gone off, that are present and are yet to be born; but no one, knows Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.27. O descendant of Bharata, O scorcher of foes ! At the time of creation, all beings get delusion because of the illusion of pairs [of opposites] arising from desire and hatred.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.28. But those men of virtuous deeds, whose sin has come to an end-they, being free from the delusion of pairs [of opposites], worship Me with firm resolve.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.29. Those, who, relying on Me, strive to achieve freedom from old age and death-they realise all to be the Brahman and realise all the actions governing the Self.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.30. Those who realise Me as one [identical] with what governs the beings, deities and with what governs the sacrifices-they, even at the moment of their journey, experience Me, with their mastering the Yoga.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Dr.S.Sankaranarayan did not comment on this sloka

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.2. Who is Lord-of-sacrifices (adhiyajna) [and] how ? Who in this body ? O slayer of Madhu ! How are You to be realised by the self-controlled ones at the time of their journey (i.e., death) also ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.3. The Bhagavat said The immutable Absolute is the Brahman. Its intrinsic nature is called the Lord of the self. The emitting activity that causes the birth of both the animate and the inanimate is named 'action '.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.4. The changing nature is the lord of the material beings; the Person alone is the lord of the divinites; I am alone the Lord of sacrifices and I, the best of the embodied (Souls), dwell in this body.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.5. Whosoever, at the time of death also remembering Me alone, sets forth by abandoning his body [behind], he attains My being. There is no doubt about it.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.6. And also remembering whatever being, a person leaves his body at the end [of his life], that being alone he attains, O son of Kunti ! [Because] he has been constantly thinking about that being.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.7. Therefore at all times keep Me in the mind and also fight; then, having your mind and intellect dedicated to Me, you will doubtlessly attain Me alone.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.8. He, who is engaged in the after-reflection (who meditates) on the Supreme Divine Soul with his mind, remaining fixed in the practice-Yoga and [hence] passing over no other object - that person attains [that Supreme], O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.9. He, who meditates continuously on the Ancient Seer, the Ruler, the Subtler than the subtle, the Supporter of all, the Unimaginable-formed, the Sun-coloured, and That which is beyond the darkness;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.10. That person endowed with a steady mind, with devotion and also with the Yoga-power, reaches at the time of journey that Supreme Divine Soul, by fixing properly the life-breath in between his eye brows.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.11. That Unchanging One which the Veda-knowers speak of; Which the passion-free ascetics enter into; seeking Which they practise celibacy (or spiritual life); that Goal together with means [to reach It] I shall tell you.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.12. Properly controlling all the gates [in the body]; well restraining the mind in the heat; fixing one's own prana in the head; taking resort to the firmness of the Yoga;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.13. Reciting the single-syllabled Om, the very Brahman; meditating on Me; whosoever travels well, casting away [his] body-surely he attains My State.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.14. And whosoever constantly bears Me in mind never attached to any other object-for this Yogin, ever devout, I am easy to attain, O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.15. Having attained Me, the men of great soul who have achieved the supreme perfection, do not get the transient rirth, a store-house of all troubles.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.16. Till the Brahman [is attained], people do return from [each and every] world, O Arjuna ! But there is no rirth for one who has attained Me, O son of Kunti !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.17. Those who know the day of Brahma as compassing one thousand yugas (world-ages), and night [also] as compassing one thousand yugas-those men know the day and night of Brahma.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.18. While the day approaches, all manifestations issue forth from the unmanifest and while the night approaches they dissolve into the same that bears the name 'the unmanifest.'

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.19. Being born and born again, the self same multitude of beings gets dissolved while the night approaches, and issues forth willy-nilly while the day approaches, O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.20. But there exists another Being which is beyond this, and It is both manifest and unmanifest and is etnernal. It is this Being that does not perish while all [the other] beings perish.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.21. [The scriptures] speak of This as Unmanifest and Changeless and declare This is to be the highest Goal. Having attained which people do not return, this is My highest abode.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.22. The Supreme Soul. O son of Prtha, is attainable through devotion that admits no other things; having attained Which Soul, the men of Yoga do not get birth again; within Which exist the beings; and in Which everything is well established, O Arjuna !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.23. Departing at what times the Yogins attain the non-return or the return only-those times I shall declare to you, O chief of the Bharatas !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.24. The northern course [of the sun] consisting of six months, is fire, light, day and bright one. Departing in it, the Brahman-knowing men attain the Brahman .

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.25. The southern course [of the sun], consisting of six months, is smoke, night, and also dark. [Departing] in it, the Yogin attains the moon's light and he returns.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.26. For, these two bright and dark courses are considered to be perpetual for the world. One attains the non-return by the first of these, and one returns back by the other one.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.27. O son of Prtha, not a single Yogin, knowing these two courses, gets deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, be practising Yoga connected with all times.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 8.28. Having understood all this, the Yogin goes beyond whatever fruit of merit is ordained [in the scriptures] in case the Vedas [are recited], the sacrifices [performed], the austerities [observed], and also gifts [donated]; and he goes to the Supreme Primeval Abode.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.1. The Bhagavat said To you, who is entertaining no displeasure, I shall clearly declare also this most secret knowledge, together with action, by knowing which you shall be free from evil.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.2. This shines among the sciences; (this is) the secret of monarchs; it is a supreme purifier, it is comprehensible by immediate perception, is righteous, easy to do, and imperishable.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.3. O scorcher of foes ! Having no faith in this Dharma, persons do not attain Me and remain eternally in the circuit of mundane existence, wrought with death.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.4. This entire universe is pervaded by Me, having the unmanifest form (aspect); all beings exist in Me and I do not exist in them.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.5. Yet, the beings do not exist in Me. Look at the Sovereign Yoga of Mine. My Self is the sustainer of the beings, does not exist in beings, and cuases beings to be born.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.6. Just as the mighty wind exists in the ether, always moving [in it] everywhere, in the same manner all beings exist in Me. Be sure of it.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.7. O son of Kunti, all beings pass into the nature [of Mine] at the end of the Kalpa (the age of universe); I send them forth again at the beginning of the [next] Kalpa.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.8. Taking hold of My own nature I send forth again and again this entire host of beings, which is powerless under the control of [My] nature.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.9. O Dhananjaya ! These acts do not bind Me, remaining as if unconcerned and unattached in these actions.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.10. O son of Kunti ! On account of Me, Who remain (only) as an observer and as prime cause, the nature [of Mine] gives birth to [both] the moving and unmoving; hence this world moves in a circle.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.11. Being unaware of the immutable highest Absolute Supreme nature of Mine, the deluded ones disregard Me dwelling in the human body.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.12. [They] are of futile aspirations, futile actions, futile knowledge and wrong intellect; and they take recourse only to the delusive nature that is demoniac and also devilish.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.13. O son of Prtha ! The great-souledmen, however, taking hold of the divine nature and having nothing else in their mind, adore Me by viewing Me as the imperishable prime cuase of beings.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.14. Ever speaking of My glory, striving with firm resolve, paying homage to Me and being permanently endowed with devotion they worship Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.15. [Of them] some worship Me by knowledge-sacrifice and others by offering sacrifices; [thus] they worship Me, the Universally-faced [either] as One [or] as Many.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.16. I am determination; I am sacrifice; I am Svadha; I am the juice of the herb; I am the (Vedic) hymn; I am alone the clarified butter also; I am the [sacrificial] fire; (and) I am the act of offering.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.17. I am the father, the mother, the sustainer and the paternal-grandsire of this world; [I am] the sacred object of knowledge, the syullable Om, the Rk, the Saman, and the Yajus too.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.18. [I am] the method, the nourisher, the lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the good-hearted (friend), the origin, the dissolution, the sustenance, the repository and the imperishable seed [of the world].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.19. I give heat; I hold back and also end forth rains; I am immortality and also death, the real and also the unreal, O Arjuna !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 9.20. The masters of the three Vedas, the Somadrinkers, purified of their sins, aspire for the heavengoal by offering sacrifices to Me. They attain the meritorious world of the lord of gods and taste in the heaven the heavenly pleasures of the gods.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
