alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.21. But, what is given to get a return of favour or again with a view to a fruit, and which is very much vexed - that gift is held to be of the Rajas.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.22. The gift which is given, at a wrong place, at a wrong time and to unworthy persons; and which is converted into a bad act and is disrespected - that is declared to be of the Tamas.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.23. OM TAT SAT : This is held to be the three-fold indication of the Brahman. By means of that, the Vedas, and also the sacrifices had been fashioned formerly by Brahma.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.24. Therefore, the scripture-prescribed acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity of those who are habituated to have Brahman-discourses, commence (or take place) invariably, with the utterance of OM.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.25. With [the utterance of] TAT and without aiming at the fruit, the acts of sacrifice and austerity and the various acts of gifts are performed by those who seek emancipation.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.26. In the sense of 'right one' (or 'manifesting as being') and in the sense of 'proper one' (or 'manifesting perfectly'), this word SAT is employed. Likewise the word SAT is used with regard to the praiseworthy act; O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.27. The steadfastness is performing sacrifice, in austerity and in giving gift is also called SAT; and also the act for such purpose is [hence] just called SAT.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.28. Without faith, whatever oblation is offered, what-ever gift is made, whatever austerity is practised, and whatever action is undertaken, that is called ASAT and it is of no avail after one's death and in this world.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.1. Arjuna said O Mighty-armed ! I desire to know severally the distinctive nature of renunciation and of relinishment, O Hrsikesa ! O Slayer of Kesin !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.2. The Bhagavat said The seers understand the act of renouncing the desire-motivated actions as renunciation; the experts declare the relinishment of the fruits of all actions to be relinishment.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.3. Certain wise men delcare that the harmful action is to be relinished while others say that the actions of performing sacrifices, giving gifts and observing austerities should not be relinished.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.4. O best of Bharata's descendants ! Listen to My considered view about relinishing : Indeed the act of relinishing is rightly spoken to be three-fold, O best among men !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.5. The actions of [Vedic] sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinished and they must necessarily be performed; for the men of wisdom the [Vedic sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the means of purification.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.6. Even these actions too must be performed by relinishing attachment and fruits : This is my considered best opinion, O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.7. The renunciation of the enjoined action does not stand to reason; and completely relinishing it, out of ignorance is proclaimed, on all sides, as an act of the Tamas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.8. He who would, out of fear of bodily exertion, relinish an action, just because it is painful-that person, having [thus] made relinishment, an act of the Rajas (Strand), would not at all gain the fruit of [that] relinishment.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.9. 'This is a thing to be performed.'-just on that ground whatever usual action is performed relinishing attachment and also fruit-that act of relinishment is deemed to be of the Sattva (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.10. The man of relinishment, who is well possessed of the Sattva, is wise and has his doubts destroyed-he hates not the unskilled action and clings not to the skilled action.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.11. Indeed, to relinish actions entirely is not possible for a body-bearing one; but whosoever relinishes the fruits of actions, he is said to be a man of [true] relinishment.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.12. The three-fold fruit of action, viz., the undesired, the desired and the mixed, accrues [even] after death ot those who are not men of relinishment, but never to those who are men of renunciation.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.13. O mighty-armed one ! Learn from Me these following five causes that have been declared in the conclusion of deliberations [on proper knowledge], for the accomplishment of all actions.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.14. The basis, as well as the agent, and diverse instruments, and distinct activity of various kinds and Destiny, which is certainly the fifth [factor].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.15. O Arjuna ! Whatever action is undertaken with the body, speech or the mind, whether it is lawful or otherwise, its factors are these five.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.16. But this being the case, whosoever views himself as the sole agent (cause of actions) due to his imperfect intellect - he, the defective-minded one, does not view [things rightly].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.17. He, whose mental disposition is not dominated by the sense 'I', and whose intellect is not stained - he, even if he slays these worlds, does not [really] slay any and he is not fettered.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.18. The instrument of knowledge, the object-of-knowledge, and the knowing subject-the prompting-in-action, consisting of these three-fold elements is [itself] the proper grasping of action with three-fold elements viz., the instrument, the object and the agent.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.19. The instrument of knowledge, the object and the agent are just three kinds because of the differences in the Strands-thus it is declared in enumerating the Strands. These also you must listen to [from Me] as they are.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.20. That instrument-of-knowledge, by means of which one perceives in all beings the singular immutable Existence, the Unclassified in the classified ones - that you must know to be born of the Sattva (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.21. That instrument-of-knowledge, by means of which one considers the varied natures of different sorts in all beings as [really] different-that is regarded to be of the Rajas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.22. That [instrument-of-knowledge], because of which, one, not realising the whole, gets indulged, without reason, in a particular activity, and which is unconcerned with the real nature of things and is insignificant - that is declared to be of the Tamas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.23. The object that has been acired with determination, without attachment and without desire or hatred, by one who does not crave to reap the fruit [of his action] - that is declared to be of the Sattva (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.24. The object which is abundant in afflictions; and which is further reired by one who craves to attain the desired thing with the feeling of 'I'-that is considered to be of the Rajas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.25. The object which is gained, due to ignorance, without considering the result, the loss, the injury to others and the strength [of one's own]-that is declared to be of the Tamas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.26. The agent who is free from attachment; who does not make any speech of egoism; who is full of contentment and enthusiasm; and who does not change [mentally] in success or in failure-that agent is said to be of the Sattva (Strand) nature.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.27. The agent, who is a man of passion; who craves for the fruit of his action, and is avaricious; who is injurious by nature, is impure and is overpowered by joy and griefthat agent is proclaimed to be of the Rajas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.28. The agent, who does not exert, is vulgar, obstinate and deceitful; who is a man of wickedness and is lazy, sorrowful, and procrastinating - that agent is said to be of the Tamas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.29. You must listen [from Me] to the three-fold division of the intellect and also of content both being expounded completely and individually, [by Me] basing on the Strands, O Dhananjaya !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.30. The intellect which knows the activity and the cessation from the activity, the proper and improper actions, the fear and non-fear, and the bondage and emancipation-that intellect is considered to be of the Sattva (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.31. The intellect, by means of which one decides incorrectly the righteous and the unrighteous ones and what is a proper action and also an improper onethat intellect is of the Rajas (Strand), O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.32. The intellect which, containing darkness (ignorance), conceives the unrighteous one as righteous and all things topsy-turvy-that intellect is deemed to be of the Tamas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.33. The unfailing content because of which one restrains, with Yoga, the activities of mind, the living breath and the senses-that content is considered to be of the Sattva (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.34. O Arjuna ! The content by which one restrains one's bounden duty, pleasure and wealth, and conseently desiring the fruits [of action]-that content is of the Rajas (Strand), O son of Prtha !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.35. The content, whery a foolish man does not give up his sleep, fear, grief, despondency and also arrogancethat content is deemed to be of the Tamas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.36. O best among the Bharatas ! Now from Me you must also listen to the three-fold happiness where one gets delighted by practice, and attains the end of suffering.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.37. [The happiness] which is like poison at its time but is like nectar at the time of its result-that happiness, born of serenity of the Soul and intellect, you must know to be of the Sattva (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.38. [The happiness] which is like nectar at its time due to the contact between the senses and sense-objects; but which is like poison at the time of its result-that is considered to be of the Rajas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.39. The happiness which, [both] at the beginning and subseently, is of the nature of deluding the Self; and which results from sleep, indolence and heedleness-that is stated to be of the Tamas (Strand).

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.40. Whether on the earth, or again among the gods in the heaven, there exists not a single being, which is free from these three Strands, born of the Material-Nature.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.41. The duties of the Brahmanas, the Ksatriyas, the Vaisyas, and of the Sudras are properly classified according to the Strands which are the sources of their nature, O scorcher of foes !

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.42. Quietude, self-control, as well as purity, for-bearance, and also straightforwardness, knowledge, wisdom, and faith in another world are the duties of the Brahmanas, born of their nature.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.43. Heroic deed, fiery energy, firmness, dexterity, and also non-feeling form battle, giving gifts, overlordship, are the duties of the Ksatriyas, born of their nature.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.44. Ploughing, cattle-tending and trading are the actions of the Vaisyas, born of their nature. The action, in the form of service, is of the Sudras, born of their nature.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.10. Who performs actions by offering them to the Brahman and giving up attachment-he is not stained by sin just as the lotus-leaf is [not stained] by water.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.46. That, whence the activities of the beings arise; by which this universe is pervaded-worshipping That by one's own prescribed action, a man attains success.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.47. Better is one's own prescribed duties, [born of one's nature, even though] it is devoid of ality, than another's duty well executed; the doer of duty, dependent on (or prescribed according to) one's own nature, does not incur sin.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.48. O son of Kunti ! One should not give up the nature-born duty, even if it is (appears to be) defective. For, all beginnings are enveloped by harm just as the fire by smoke.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.49. He, whose mind entertains no attachment to anything, who is self-conered and is free from craving-he attains by means of renunciation the supreme success of actionlessness.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.50. Having attained the success, how he attains the Brahman, an attainment which is confirmed to be the final beatitude of true knowledge-that you must learn from Me briefly.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.51. He, who has got a totally pure intellect by fully controlling his self (mind) with firmness, and renouncing sense-objects, sound etc., and driving out desire and hatred;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.52. Who enjoys solitude, eats lightly, has controlled his speech-organ, body and mind; who is permanently devoted to the meditation-Yoga; and who has taken shelter in the perennial desirelessness;

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.53. Relinshing egotism, violence, pride, desire, wrath, and the sense of possession-he, the unselfish and calm one, is capable of becoming the Brahman.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.54. Having become the Brahman, the serene-minded one neither grieves nor rejoices; remaining eal to all beings, he gains the highest devotion to Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.55. Through devotion he comes to know of Me : Who I am and how, in fact, I am-having correctly known Me, he enters Me. Then afterwards,

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.56. Performing all [his] actions all the time and taking refuge in Me, he attains, through My Grace, the eternal, changeless state.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.57. [Hence] renouncing by mind all actions in Me, O descendant of Bharata, and taking hold of the knowledge-Yoga, you must always be with your thought-organ [turned] towards Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.58. Having your thought-organ turned towards Me, you shall pass over all obstacles by Me Grace. On the other hand, if you don't give up your sense of ego, you will not liberated yourself, [instead] you will perish.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.59. In case, holding fast to the sense of ego, you think (decide) 'I shall not fight', that resolve of yours will be just useless. [For] your own natural condition will incite you [to fight].

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.60. O son of Kunti ! Being bound fully by your own duty, born of your own nature, and also being [hence] not independent, you would perform what you do not wish to perform, because of your-delusion.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.61. O Arjuna ! This Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, causing, by His trick-of-Illusion, all beings to whirl round [as if they are] mounted on a [revolving] mechanical contrivance.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.62. To Him alone you must go for refuge with all your thought, O descendant of Bharata ! Through My Grace you will attain the success, the eternal abode.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.63. Thus the [path of] wisdom, a better secret than all the secrets has been expounded to you by Me; comprehend it fully and then act as you please.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.64. Yet again, you must listen to My ultimate (or supreme) message which is the highest secret of all. You are My dear one and have a firm intellect. Hence I shall tell you what is good to you :

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.65. Be with your mind fixed in Me; be My devotee; offer oblation to Me and render salutation to Me; you shall come to Me alone. Really I promise you, (because) you are dear to Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.66. Abandoning all attributes, come to Me as your sole refuge; I shall rescue you from all sins; don't be sorrowful.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.67. This [knowledge] is for you, and it should never be imparted to one who does not observe austerities; to him who has no devotion; to him who has no desire to listen; and to him who is indignant towards Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.68. Whosoever shall declare this highest secret to My devotees, he, cultivating an utmost devotion towards Me, and not entertaining any doubt, shall reach Me.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.69. And, excepting him there would be none among men who is the best performer of what is dear to Me; and other than him there shall be none else who is dearer to Me on earth.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.70. Whosoever would learn this sacred dialogue of both of us, by him I am worshipped (delighted) through the knowledge-sacrifice : This is My opinion

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.71. A man who would at least hear to [this] with faith and without indignation-he too, freed [from sins], will attain the auspicious worlds of men of meritorius acts.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.72. O son of Prtha ! Has this been heared by you with attentive mind ? O Dhananjaya ! Has your strong delusion, born of ignorance, been totally destroyed ?

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.73. Arjuna said My delusion is destroyed; recollection is gained by me through your Grace, O Acyuta ! I stand firm, free of doubts; I shall excute your ?nd.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.74. Sanjaya said Thus I have heard this wonderful and thrilling dailogue of Vasudeva and the mighty-minded son of Prtha.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.75. Through the grace of Vyasa, I have heard this highly secret supreme Yoga from Krsna, the Lord of the Yogins, while He was Himself imparting it personally.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.76. O king ! By recollecting and recollecting this wonderful pious dialogue of Kesava and Arjuna, I feel also delighted again and again.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.77. O great king ! On recalling in the mind that extremely wonderful supreme form of Hari, I am amazed and I feel joyous again and again.

author: Dr. S. S. Sankaranarayan
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.78. Where Krsna, the Lord of Yogins remains, where the son of Prtha holds his bow, there lie fortune, victory, prosperity and firm justice-so I believe.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.1 Dhrtarastra said On the holy field of Kuruksetra, gathered together eager for battle, what did my people and the Pandavas do, O Sanjaya?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.2 Sanjaya said King Duryodhana, on seeing the Pandava army in battle array, approached his teacher Drona and said these words:

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.3 Behold, O teacher, this mighty army of the Pandavas, arrayed by the son of Drupada, your intelligent disciple.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.4 There (in that army) are heroes, great bowmen, like Bhima and Arjuna; Yuyudhana,Virata and Drupada a mighty warrior;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.5 Dhrstaketu, Cekitana, and the valiant king of Kasi; Purujit and Kuntibhoja, and Saibya the best among men;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.6 Yudhamanyu the valiant, and Uttamaujas the strong; and also the son of Subhadra and the sons of Draupadi, all mighty warriors.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.7 Know, O best of Brahmanas, those who are important on our side - those who are the commanders of my army. I shall name them to refresh your memory.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.8 Yourself, Bhisma and Karna, the victorious Krpa, Asvatthama, Vikarna and Jayadratha the son of Somadatta;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.9 And there are many other heroes who are determined to give up their lives for my sake. They all are experts in using manifold missiles and are dexterous in battle.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.10 Inadequate is this force of ours, which is guarded by Bhisma, while adequate is that force of theirs, which is guarded by Bhima.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.11 Therefore all of you taking your places firmly in your respective divisions, guard Bhisma at all cost.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.12 Then the valiant grandsire Bhisma, seniormost of the Kuru clan, roaring like a lion, blew his conch with a view to cheer up Duryodhana.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.13 Then suddenly conchs and kettle drums, trumpets, tabors and blow horns blared forth; and the sound was terrific.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.14 Then Sri Krsna and Arjuna, stationed in their great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conchs.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.15 Sri Krsna blew his conch, Pancajanya, Arjuna his Devadatta and Bhima of terrible deeds his great conch Paundra.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.16 King Yudhisthira the son of Kunti blew his conch Anantavijaya and Nakula and Sahadeva blew their conchs Sughosa and Manipuspaka.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.17 And the King of Kasi the supreme bowman, Sikandi the mighty warrior, Dhrstadyumna and Virata; and Satyaki the invincible;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.18 Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, and the strong-armed son of Subhadra - all, O King, blew their several conchs again and again.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.19 And that tumultuous uproar, resounding through heaven and earth, rent the hearts of Dhrtarastra's sons.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.20 Then Arjuna, who had Hanuman as his banner crest, on beholding the sons of Dhrtarastra in array, took up his bow, while missiles were beginning to fly.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.21 And he spoke, O lord of earth, these words to Sri Krsna... Arjuna said: ...Draw up my chariot, O Krsna, between the two armies,

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.22 So that I may have a good look at those who are standing eager to fight and know with whom I have to fight in this enterprise of war.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.23 I wish to see those gathered here ready to fight in this battle in order to please the evil-minded son of Dhrtarastra.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.24 - 1.25 Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krsna drew up that best of chariots between the two armies before the view of Bhisma and Drona and all the other kings, O Dhrtarastra, and said, 'O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas.'

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.24 - 1.25 Sanjaya said: Thus addressed by Arjuna, Sri Krsna drew up that best of chariots between the two armies before the view of Bhisma and Drona and all the other kings, O Dhrtarastra, and said, 'O Arjuna, behold these assembled Kauravas.'

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.26 Then as Arjuna looked on, he saw standing there fathers and grand-fathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and comrades;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.27 Fathers-in-law and dear friends in both armies. When Arjuna saw all these kinsmen in array,

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.28 He was filled with deep compassion and said these words in despair :...Arjuna said:...O Krsna, when I look on these, my kinsmen present here, eager for battle,

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.29 My limbs are weakened, my mouth gets parched, my body trembles and my hairs stand erect.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.30 The bow Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin is burning. I can stand no longer. My mind seems to reel.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.31 I see, Krsna, inauspicious omens. I foresee no good in killing my kinsmen in the fight.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.32 I desire no victory, nor empire, nor pleasures. What have we to do with empire, O Krsna, or enjoyment or even life ?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.33 Those for whose sake we do desire empire, enjoyment and pleasures, stand here in war renouncing life and wealth----

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.34 Teachers, fathers, sons and also grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law and grandsons, brothers-in-law and other kinsmen---

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.35 These I would not slay, though they might slay me, even for the sovereignty of the three worlds - how much less for this earth O Krsna?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.36 If we kill the sons of Dhrtarastra, what joy will be ours, O Krsna? Sin alone will accrue to us if we kill these murderous felons.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.37 Therefore, it is not befitting that we slay our kin, the sons of Dhrtarastra. For if we kill our kinsmen, O Krsna, how indeed can we be happy?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.38 Though these people, whose minds are overpowered by greed, see no evil in the destruction of a clan and no sin in treachery to friends,

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.39 Why should we not learn to shun this crime - we who see the evil of ruining a clan, O Krsna?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.40 With the ruin of a clan, perish its ancient traditions, and when traditions perish, lawlessness overtakes the whole clan

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.41 When lawlessness prevails, O Krsna, the women of the clan become corrupt; when women become corrupt, there arises intermixture of classes.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.42 This mixing of classes leads to hell the clan itself and its destroyers; for the spirits of their ancestors fall degraded, deprived of the ritual offerings of food and water.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.43 By the sins of the clan-destroyers who bring about inter-mixture of classes, the ancient traditions of the clan and class are destroyed.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.44 For those whose clan-laws are destroyed, dwelling in hell is ordained, O Krsna; thus have we heard.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.45 Alas! We have resolved to commit a great sin in that we are ready to slay our kith and kin out of desire for sovereignty and enjoyments.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.46 If the well-armed sons of Dhrtarastra should slay me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that will be better for me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.47 Sanjaya said : Having spoken thus on the battle-field, Arjuna threw aside his how and arrows and sat down on the seat of the chariot, his heart overwhelmed with grief.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.1 Sanjaya said To him, who was thus overcome with pity, whose eyes were wet with tears, who was sorrow-stricken and who bore a bewildered look Sri Krsna spoke as follows:

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.2 The Lord said Whence comes on you this despondency, O Arjuna, in this crisis? It is unift for a noble person. It is disgraceful and it obstructs one's attainment of heaven.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.3 Yield not to unmanliness, O Arjuna, it does not become you. Shake off this base faint-heartedness and arise, O scorcher of foes!

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.4 Arjuna said How can I, O slayer of foes, aim arrows in battle against Bhisma and Drona who are worthy of reverence?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.5 It is better even to live on a beggar's fare in this world than to slay these most venerable teachers. If I should slay my teachers, though degraded they be by desire for wealth, I would be enjoying only blood-stained pleasures here.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.6 We do not know, which of the two is better for us - whether our vanishing them, or their vanishing us. The very sons of Dhrtarastra, whom, if we slay, we should not wish to live, even they are standing in array against us.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.7 With my heart stricken by the fault of weak compassion, with my mind perplexed about my duty, I reest you to say for certain what is good for me. I am your disciple. Teach me who have taken refuge in you.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.8 Even if I should win unchallenged sovereignty of a prosperous earth or even the kingdom on lordship over the Devas, I do not feel that it would dispel the grief than withers up my senses.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.9 Sanjaya said Having spoken thus to Sri Krsna, Arjuna, the coneror of sleep and the scorcher of foes, said, 'I will not fight' and became silent.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.10 O King, to him who was thus sorrowing between the two armies, Sri Krsna spoke the following words, as if smiling (by way of ridicule).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.11 The Lord said You grieve for those who should not be grieved for; yet you speak words of wisdom. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.12 There never was a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor any of these kings of men. Nor will there be any time in future when all of us shall cease to be.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.13 Just as the self associated with a body passes through childhood, youth and old age (pertaining to that body), so too (at death) It passes into another body. A wise man is not deluded by that.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.14 The contact of senses with their objects, O Arjuna, gives rise to feelings of cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go, never lasing long. Endure them, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.15 For, he whom these do not affect, O chief of men, and to whom pain and pleasure are the same - that steadfast man alone is worthy of immortality.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.16 The unreal can never come into being, the real never ceases to be. The conclusion about these two is seen by the seers of truth.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.17 Know That to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. None can cause the destruction of This Immutable.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.18 These bodiesof the Jiva (the embodied self) are said to have an end while the Jiva itself is eternal, indestructible and incomprehensibel. Therefore, fight O Bharata (Arjuna).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.19 He who deems It (the self) a slayer, and he who thinks of It as slain - both are ignorant. For, the self neither slays nor is slain.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.20 It (the self) is never born; It never dies; having come into being once, It never ceases to be. Unborn, eternal, abiding and primeval, It is not slain when the body is slain.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.21 He who knows this (self) to be indestructible, unborn, unchanging and hence eternal - how and whom, O Arjuna, does he cause to be killed, and whom he kill?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.22 As a man casts off worn-out garments and puts on others that are new, so does the embodied self cast off Its worn-out bodies and enter into others that are new.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.23 Weapons do not cleave It (the self), fire does not burn It, waters do not wet It, and wind does not dry It.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.24 It cannot be cleft; It cannot be burnt; It cannot be wetted and It cannot be dried, It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable and primeval.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.25 This (self) is said to be unmanifest, inconceivable and unchanging. Therefore, knowing It thus, it does not befit you to grieve.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.26 Or if you hold this self as being constantly born and as constantly dying, even then, O mighty-armed one, it does not become you to feel grief.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.27 For, death is certain for the born, and re-birth is certain for the dead; therefore you should not feel grief for what is inevitable.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.28 O Arjuna, beings have an unknown beginning, a known middle and an unknown end. What is there to grieve over in all this?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.29 One looks upon This (self) as a wonder; likewise another speaks of It as a wonder; still another hears of It as a wonder; and even after hearing of It, one knows It not.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.30 The self in the body, O Arjuna, is eternal and indestructible. This is so in the case of the selves in all bodies. Therefore, it is not fit for you to feet grief for any being.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.31 Further, considering also your own duty, it does not befit you to waver. For, to a Ksatriya, there is no greater good than a righteous war.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.32 Happy are the Ksatriyas, O Arjuna, to whom a war like this comes of its own accord; it opens the gate to heaven.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.33 But if you do not fight this righteous war, you will be turning away from your duty and honoured position, and will be incurring sin.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.34 Further, people will speak ill of you for all time, and for one accustomed to be honoured, dishonour is worse than death.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.35 The great warriors will think that you have fled from battle in fear. These men who held you in high esteem will speak lightly of you now.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.36 Your enemies, slandering your prowess, will use words which should never be uttered. What could be more painful than that?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.37 If slain, you shall win heaven; or if victorious, you shall enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise, O Arjuna, resolved to fight.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.38 Holding pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as alike, gird yourself up for the battle. Thus, you shall not incur any sin.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.39 This Buddhi concerning the self (Sankhya) has been imparted to you. Now listen to this with regard to Yoga, by following which you will get rid of the bondage of Karma.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.40 Here, there is no loss of effort, nor any accrual of evil. Even a little of this Dharma (called Karma Yoga) protects a man from the great fear.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.41 In this (Karma Yoga), O Arjuna, the resolute mind is one-pointed; the minds of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.42 - 2.44 O! Partha, the unwise, who rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, say, 'There is nothing else.' They are full only of wordly desires and they hanker for heaven. They speak flowery words which offer rirth as the fruit of work. They look upon the Vedas as consisting entirely of varied rites for the attainment of pleasure and power. Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a concentrated mind.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.42 - 2.44 O! Partha, the unwise, who rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, say, 'There is nothing else.' They are full only of wordly desires and they hanker for heaven. They speak flowery words which offer rirth as the fruit of work. They look upon the Vedas as consisting entirely of varied rites for the attainment of pleasure and power. Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a concentrated mind.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.42 - 2.44 O! Partha, the unwise, who rejoice in the letter of the Vedas, say, 'There is nothing else.' They are full only of wordly desires and they hanker for heaven. They speak flowery words which offer rirth as the fruit of work. They look upon the Vedas as consisting entirely of varied rites for the attainment of pleasure and power. Those who cling so to pleasure and power are attracted by that speech (offering heavenly rewards) and are unable to develop the resolute will of a concentrated mind.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.45 The Vedas have the three Gunas for their sphere, O Arjuna. You must be free from the three Gunas and be free from the pairs of opposites. Abide in pure Sattva; never care to acire things and to protect what has been acired, but be established in the self.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.46 What use a thirsty person has for a water reservoir when all sides of it are flooded - that much alone is the use of all the Vedas for a Brahmana who knows.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.47 To work alone you have the right, and not to the fruits. Do not be impelled by the fruits of work. Nor have attachment to inaction.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.48 Abandoning attachment and established in Yoga, perfom works, viewing success and failure with an even mind. Evenness of mind is said to be Yoga.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.49 Action with attachment is far inferior, O Arjuna, to action done with evenness of mind. Seek refuge in evenness of mind. Miserable are they who act with a motive for results.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.50 A man with evenness of mind discards here and now good and evil. Therefore endeavour for Yoga. Yoga is skill in action.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.51 The wise who possess evenness of mind, relinishing the fruits born of action, are freed from the bondage of birth, and go to the region beyond all ills.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.52 When your intellect has passed beyond the tangle of delusion, you will yourself feel disgusted regarding what you shall hear and what you have already heard.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.53 When your intellect, well enlightened by hearing from Me and firmly placed, stands unshaken in a concentrated mind, then you will attain the vision of the self.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.54 Arjuna said What is the mode of speech of him who is of firm wisdom, who is established in the control of the mind? What will a man of firm wisdom speaks, O Krsna? How does he sit? How does he move?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.55 The Lord said When a man renounces all the desires of the mind, O Arjuna, when he is satisfied in himself with himself, then he is said to be of firm wisdom.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.56 He whose mind is not perturbed in pain, who has no longing for pleasures, who is free from desire, fear and anger - he is called a sage of firm wisdom.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.57 He who has no love on any side, who when he finds good or evil, neither rejoices nor hates - his wisdom is firmly set.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.58 When one is able to draw his senses from the objects of sense on every side, as a tortoise draws in its limbs, then his wisdom is firmly set.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.59 The objects of senses, excepting relish for the objects, turn away from the abstinent dweller in the body. Even the relish turns aswy from him when what is supreme over the senses i.e., the self, is seen.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.60 The turbulent senses, O Arjuna, do carry away perforce the mind of even a wise man, though he is ever striving.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.61 Having controlled all the senses, let him remain in contemplation, regarding Me as supreme; for, his knowledge is firmly set whose senses are under control.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.62 To a man thinking about sense-objects, there arises attachment to them; form attachment arises desire, from desire arises anger;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.63 From anger there comes delusion; from delusion, the loss of memory; from the loss of memory, the destruction of discrimination; and with the destruction of discrimination, he is lost.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.64 But he who goes through the sense-objects with the senses free from love and hate, disciplined and controlled, attains serenity.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.65 In that serenity there is loss of all sorrow; for in the case of the person with a serene mind, the Buddhi soon becomes well established.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.66 There is no Buddhi for the unintegrated, nor for him is there contemplation of the self, and for him without contemplation of the self, there is no peace; and for one lacking peace, where is happiness?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.67 For, when the mind follows the senses experiencing their objects, his understanding is carried away by them as the wind carries away a ship on the waters.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.68 Therefore, O mighty-armed, he whose senses are restrained from going after their objects on all sides, his wisdom is firmly set.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.69 What is night for all beings, in it the controlled one is awake; when all beings are awake, that is the night to the sage who sees.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.70 He into whom all desires enter as the waters enter the full and undisturbed sea, attains to peace, and not he who longs after objects of desire.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.71 The man who, abandoning all desires, abides without longing and possession and the sense of 'I' and 'mine', wins peace.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.72 This is the Brahmi-state, O Arjuna. None attaining to this is deluded. By abiding in this state even at the hour of death, one wins the self.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.1 Arjuna said If, O Krsna, you consider that Buddhi (knowledge) is superior to works, why do you engage me in this terrible deed?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.2 You confuse my mind with statements that seem to contradict each other; tell me for certain that one way by which I could reach the highest good.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.3 The Lord said In this world a two-fold way was of yore laid down by Me, O sinless one: by Jnana Yoga for the Sankhyas and by Karma Yoga for the Yogins.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.4 No man experiences freedom from activity (Naiskarmya) by abstaining from works; and no man ever attains success by mere renunciation of works.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.5 No man can, even for a moment, rest without doing work; for everyone is caused to act, in spite of himself, by the Gunas born of Nature.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.6 He who, controlling the organs of action, lets his mind dwell on the objects of senses, is a deluded person and a hypocrite.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.7 But he who, subduing his senses by the mind, O Arjuna, begins to practise Karma Yoga through the organs of action and who is free from attachment - he excels.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.8 You must perform your obligatory action; for action is superior to non-action (Jnana Yoga). For a person following non-action not even the sustentation of the body is possible.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.9 This world is held in the bondage of work only when work is not performed as sacrifice. O Arjuna, you must perform work to this end, free from attachment.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.10 In the beginning the Lord of all beings, creating man along with the sacrifice, said: 'By this shall you prosper; this shall be the cow of plenty granting all your wants.'

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.11 By this, please the gods, and the gods will support you. Thus nourishing one another, may you obtain the highest good.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.12 The gods, pleased by the sacrifice, will bestow on you the enjoyments you desire. He who enjoys the bounty of the gods without giving them anything in return, is but a thief.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.13 Pious men who eat the remnants of sacrifices are freed from all sins. But the sinful ones who cook only for their own sake earn only sin.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.14 From food arise all beings (i.e., their bodies); from rain food is produced; from sacrifice comes rain; and sacrifice springs from activity.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.15 Know that activity springs from 'Brahman', i.e., the physical body, 'Brahman' arises from the imperishable (self); therefore the all-pervading 'Brahman' is ever established in sacrifice.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.16 He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion here, lives in sin, satisfying the senses, O Arjuna. He lives in vain.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.17 But the man whose delight is only in the self, who is satisfied with the self, who rejoices in the self, for him nothing remains to be accomplished.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.18 He has no purpose to gain by work done or left undone, nor has he to rely on any end.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.19 Therefore without attachment do your work which ought to be done. For, a man who works without attachment attains to the Supreme.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.20 Indeed by Karma Yoga alone did Janaka and others reach perfection. Even recognising its necessity for the guidance of the world, you must perform action.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.21 Whatever a great man does, other men also do. Whichever standard he sets, the world follows it.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.22 For me, Arjuna, there is nothing in all the three worlds which ought to be done, nor is there anything unacired that ought to be acired. Yet I go on working.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.23 If I did not continue to work unwearied, O Arjuna, men would follow my path.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.24 If I do not do work, these men would be lost; and I will be causing chaos in life and thery ruining all these people.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.25 Just as the ignorant, attached to their work, act, O Arjuna, so too the learned should act without any attachment, and only for the welfare of the world.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.26 He should not bewilder the minds of the ignorant who are attached to work; rather himself performing work with devotion, he should cause others to do so.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.27 Actions are being performed in every way by the Gunas of Prakrti. He whose nature is deluded by egoism, thinks, 'I am the doer.'

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.28 But he who knows the truth about the division of the Gunas and works, O mighty-armed one, through his knowledge that 'Gunas operate on their products,' is not attached.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.29 Those who are deluded by the Gunas of Prakrti are attached to the works of the Gunas. But he who knows the whole truth should not unsettle the ignorant who do not know the whole truth.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.30 Surrendering all your actions to Me with a mind focussed on the self, free from desire and selfishness, fight with the heat of excitement abated.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.31 Those men who, full of faith, ever practise this teaching of Mine and those who receive it without cavil - even they are released from Karma.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.32 But those who calumniate it, and those who do not practise this teaching of Mine - know them to be absolutely senseless and devoid of all knowledge, and therefore lost.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.33 Even the man of knowledge acts according to his nature; all beings follow their nature. What will repression do?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.34 Each sense has fixed attachment to, and aversion for, its corresponding object. But no one should come under their sway; for they are his foes.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.35 Better is one's own duty, though ill-done, than the duty of another well-performed. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is fraught with fear.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.36 Arjuna said But, impelled by what, O Krsna, does one (practising Jnana Yoga), commit sin even against his own will, constrained as it were, by force?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.37 The Lord said It is desire, it is wrath, born of the Guna of Rajas; it is a great devourer, an impeller to sin. Know this to be the foe here.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.38 As a fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror is covered by dust, and as an embryo is encased in the membrane, so is this (worldA) enveloped by it (desire).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.39 The knowledge of the intelligent self is enveloped by this constant enemy, O Arjuna, which is of the nature of desire, and which is difficult to gratify and is insatiable.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.40 The senses, the mind and the intellect are said to be its instruments. By these it overpowers the embodied self after enveloping Its knowledge.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.41 Therefore, O Arjuna, controlling the senses in the very beginning, slay this sinful thing that destroys both knowledge and discrimination.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.42 The senses are high, they say: the mind is higher than the senses; the intellect is higher than the mind; but what is greater than intellect is that (desire).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.43 Thus, knowing that which is higher than the intellect and fixing the mind with the help of the intellect in Karma Yoga, O Arjuna, slay this enemy which wears the form of desire, and which is difficult to overcome.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.1 The Lord said I taught this imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan; Vivasvan taught it to Manu; Manu declared it to Iksvaku.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.2 Thus handed down in succession, the royal sages knew this (Karma Yoga). But with long lapse of time, O Arjuna, that Yoga was lost to the world.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.3 It is the same ancient Yoga which is now taught to you by Me, as you are My devotee and My friend. For, this is a supreme mystery.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.4 Arjuna said Later was your birth, and earlier the birth of Vivasvan. How then am I to understand that you taught it in the beginning?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.5 The Lord said Many births of Mine have passed, O Arjuna, and so is it with you also. I know them all, but you do not know them.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.6 Though I am birthless and of immutable nature, though I am the Lord of all beings, yet by employing My own Nature (Prakrti) I am born out of My own free will.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.7 Whenever there is a decline of Dharma, O Arjuna, and uprising of Adharma, then I incarnate Myself.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.8 For the protection of the good and also for the destruction of the wicked, for the establishment of Dharma, am I born from age to age.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.9 He who thus knows in truth My divine birth and actions does not get rirth after leaving the body; he will come to Me, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.10 Freed from desire, fear and wrath, absorbed in Me, depending upon Me, purified by the austerity of knowledge, many have attained My state.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.11 Whoever resortt to Me in any manner, in the same manner do I favour them; men experience Me alone in different ways, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.12 Those who desire the fruits of their ritualistic acts, sacrifice to the gods here; for, success born of such acts ickly accrues in the world of men.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.13 The system of four stations was created by Me according to distinction of Gunas and Karma. Though I am their creator, know Me as non-agent and immutable.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.14 Works do not contaminate Me. In Me there is no desire for fruits of actions. He who understands Me thus is not bound by actions.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.15 Knowing thus, even ancient seekers for liberation and work. Therefore, do your wok only as the ancients did in olden times.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.16 What is action? What is non-action? Even the wise are puzzled in respect of these. I shall declare to you that kind of action by knowing which you will be freed from evil.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.17 For, there is what ought to be known in action. Likewise there is what ought to be known in multi-form action. And there is what ought to be understood in non-action. Thus mysterious is the way of action.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.18 He who sees non-action in action and also action in non-action is wise among men. He is fit for release and has carried out all actions.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.19 He whose every undertaking is free from desire and delusive identification (of the body with the self), whose actions are burnt up in the fire of knowledge - him the wise describe as a sage.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.20 Having renounced attachment to the fruits of his actions, ever contented with the eternal self, and dependent on none, one does not act at all, even though engaged in action.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.21 Free from desire, his intellect and mind controlled, giving up all possessions, and doing bodily work only, he is not subject to evil:

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.22 Content with what chance may bring, rising above the pairs of opposites, free from ill-will, even-minded in success and failure, though he acts, he is not bound.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.23 Of one whose attachments are gone, who is free, whose mind is established in knowledge, who works only for sacrifices, his Karma is entirely dissolved.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.24 Brahman is the instrument to offer with; Brahman is the oblation. By Brahman is the oblation offered into the fire of Brahman; Brahman alone is to be reached by him who meditates on Him in his works.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.25 Some Yogins resort only to the sacrifice relating to gods. Others offer sacrifice into the fire of Brahman solely by means of sacrifice.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.26 Others offer as oblations hearing and other senses in the fires of restraint. Some others offer as oblations the objects of the senses, such as sound and the rest, into the fires of their senses.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
