11.39 (a) You are Yayu, Yama, Agini, Varuna, Sasanka, Prajapati and the great-grandsire৷৷.
(b) ৷৷. Hail, Hail unto You, a thousand times! Hail unto You again and yet again!

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
11.40 (a) Salutation to You from before and behind! Salutation to You from all sides, O All!৷৷.
(b) ৷৷. O You of infinite prowess and heroic action which are measureless! You pervade all beings and therefore are all.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.41 Unaware of this majesty of Yours, and either from negligence or love, or considering You to be a friend, whatever I have rudely said as 'O Krsna, O Yadava, O Comrade.'

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.42 And whatever disrespect has been shown to You in jest, while playing, resting, while sitting or eating, while alone or in the sight of others, O Acyuta - I implore You for forgiveness, You who are incomprehensible.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.43 You are the father of this world, of all that moves and that does not move. You are its teacher and the one most worthy of reverence. There is none eal to You. How then could there be in the three worlds another greater than You, O Being of matchless greatness?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.44 Therefore, bowing down, prostrating the body. I implore Your mercy, O adorable Lord. As a father hears with his son or a friend with his friend, it is meet, O Lord, that You, who are dear to me, should bear with me who am dear to You.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.45 Seeing what was never seen before, I am delighted. But my mind is also agog with awe. Show me, O Lord! Your other form. O Lord of the gods! Be gracious, O Abode of the universe!

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.46 I wish to see You ever as before, with crown and with mace and discus in hand. Assume again that four-armed shape, O Thou the thosand armed, of Universal Form!

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.47 The Lord said By My grace, O Arjuna this Supreme Form, luminous, universal, infinite, primal, never seen before by anyone but you, has been revealed to you through My own free will.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.48 Neither through the study of the Vedas, nor by sacrifices, nor by recitals of the scriptures, nor by gifts, nor by rituals, nor by strict austerities can I be realised in a form like this in the world of men by any one else but you. O Arjuna!

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.49 You need not fear any more, nor be perplexed, looking on this awesome form of Mine. Free from fear and with a gladdened heart, behold again that other form of Mine.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.50 Sanjaya said Having spoken thus to Arjuna, Sri Krsna revealed to him once more His own form. The Mahatman, assuming again a benign form, reassured him who had been struck with awe.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.51 Arjuna said Having behold the human and pleasing form of Yours, O Krsna, I have now become composed in mind and I am restored to my normal nature.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.52 The Lord said It it very hard to behold this form of Mine which you have seen. Even the gods ever long to behold this form.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.53 Sri Krsna says Not by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by gifts, nor by sacirifce, can I seen in such a form as You have seen Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.54 But by single-minded devotion, O Arjuna, it is possible to truly know, to see and to enter into Me, who am of this form, O harasser of foes.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 11.55 Whosoever works for Me, looks upon Me as the highest and is devoted to Me, free from attached and without enmity towards any creature, he comes to Me, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.1 Arjuna said Those devotees, who, ever integrated, thus meditate on You, and those again, who meditate on the Imperishable and the Unmanifest - which or these have greater knowledge of Yoga?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.2 The Lord said Those who, ever integrated with Me and possessed of supreme faith, worship Me, focusing their minds on Me - these are considered by Me the highest among the Yogins.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Adidevananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.4 Having subdued all the senses, being even-minded, engaged in the welfare of all beings - they too come to Me only.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.5 Greater is the difficulty of those whose minds are thus attached to the unmanifest. For the way of the unmanifest is hard to reach by embodied beings.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.6 For, those who dedicate all actions to Me, hold Me as their supreme goal, intent on Me, and worship Me meditating on Me with exclusive devotion;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.7 Of those whose minds are thus focused on Me, I become soon their saviour from the ocean of mortal life.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.8 Focus your mind on Me alone; and let your Buddhi enter into Me. Then, you will live in Me alone; there is no doubt.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.9 If now you are unable to focus your mind on Me, then seek to reach Me, O Arjuna, by the practice of repetition.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.10 If you are incapable of even this practice of repetition, then devote yourself to My deeds (service). For even by working for My sake, you will attain perfection.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.11 If you are unable to do even this, i.e., taking refuge in My Yoga, then, with your self controlled, renounce the fruits of every action.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.12 Far better is knowledge of the self then the repeated practice (of remembrance of the Lord). Better is meditation than this knowledge; Better is renunciation of fruits of action than meditation. From such renunciation, peace ensues.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.13 He who never hates any being, who is friendly and compassionate, who is free from the feelings of I and mine, who looks upon all pain and pleasure the same as and who is enduring;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.14 He who is content, who ever meditates and is self-restrained and who is firm in his convictions, who has his mind and reason dedicated to Me - he is dear to Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.15 He from whom the world has no cause to be frightened, who is not frightened by the world, who is free from joy and impatience, fear and repulsion - he is dear to me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.16 He who is free from desires, who is pure, expert, indifferent and free from agony, who has renounced every undertaking - he is dear to Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
12.17 He who rejoices not, nor hates, nor grieves, nor desires, who renounces good and evil, who is full of devotion to me - dear to me is such
a devotee.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Adidevananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.19 He who regards alike both blame and praise, who is silent and content with any lot, who has no home, who is firm of mind, and who is devoted to Me - dear to Me is such a man.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 12.20 But those devotees who follow this nectar of virtuous-duty as taught above, who are full of faith and who regard Me as the Supreme - they are exceedingly dear to Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.2 The Lord said This body, O Arjuna, is called the Field, Ksetra. He who knows it is called the Filed-knower, Ksetrajna, by those who know the self.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.3 And know Me also as the Field-Knower in all Fields, O Arjuna. The knowledge of the Field and its knower is, in My view, the true knowledge.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.4 Listen briefly from Me what the Field is, and what it is like, what is modifications are, what purpose it serves, what it is; and who the self is and what Its powers are.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.5 It has been sung by seers in various ways, in various distinctive hymns, and also in the well-reasoned and conclusive words of the Brahma-sutras.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.6 The great elements, the Ahankara, the Buddhi, the Avyakta, the ten senses and the one, besides, the five objects of the senses;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.7 Desire, hatred, pleasure and pain and the combination that constitutes the basis of consciousness (or the individual self). Thus this Ksetra has been briefly described with its modifications.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.8 Modesty, absence of ostentation, non-injury, patience, sincerity, service of the preceptor, purity, firmness and self-restraint;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.9 Absence of desire with regard to sense-objects, and also absence of egotism, the perception of evil in birth, death, old age, disease and sorrow;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.10 Non-attachment, absence of clinging to son, wife, home and the like, and constant even-mindedness to all desirable and undesirable events;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.11 Constant devotion directed to Me alone, resort to solitary places and dislike for crowds:

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.12 Constant contemplation on the knowledge pertaining to the self, reflection for the attainment of knowledge of the truth - this is declared to be knowledge, and what is contrary to it is ignorance.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.13 I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains the immortal self. It is beginningless brahman having Me for the Highest (Anadi matparam); it is said to be neither being nor-being.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.14 Everywhere are Its hands and feet; Its eyes, heads and mouths are everywhere; Its ears are on all sides; and It exists encompassing all things.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.15 Shining by the functions of the senses, and yet devoid of the senses, detached and yet supporting all, devoid of Gunas and yet experiencing the Gunas;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.16 It is within and without all beings; It is unmoving and yet moving; It is so subtle that none can comprehend It; It is far away, and yet It is very near.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.17 Undivided and yet remaining as if divided among beings, this self is to be known as the supporter of elements. It devours them and causes generation.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.18 The light of all lights, this is said to be beyond Tamas (darkness). It is known to be knowledge. It is to be attained by knowledge. It is present in the heart of all.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.19 Thus the Ksetra, knowledge and the object of knowledge have been briefly set forth. On knowing this, My devotee becomes fit to attain My state of being.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.20 Know that both Prakrti and the self (Purusa) are without beginning; know that all modifications and the attributes are born of Prakrti.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.21 The Prakrti is said to be the cause of agency to the body (Karya) and sense-organs (Karana). The self is said to be the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
13.22 (a) Indeed, the self seated in Prakrti experiences the Gunas born of Prakrti৷৷.
(b) ৷৷. Its attachment to these Gunas is the cause of birth in good and evil wombs.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.23 The self in the body is called spectator, approver, supporter, experiencer, the great lord and also the supreme self in the body.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.24 He who understands the self and the Prakrti thus with the Gunas is not born again, in whatever state he may be placed.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.25 Some perceive the self within the self (body) by meditation by the self (mind), others by Sankhya Yoga, and still others by Karma Yoga.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.26 But some, who do not know thus, having heard from others, worship accordingly - these too, who are devoted to what they hear, pass beyond death.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.27 Whatever being is born, whether it is moving or stationary, know, O Arjuna, that it is through the combination of the Ksetra (body) and Ksetrajna (knower of the Field).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.28 Who sees the supreme ruler dwelling alike in all bodies and nevr perishing when they perish, he sees indeed.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.29 For, seeing the ruler (i.e., self) abiding alike in every place, he does not injure the self by the self (mind) and therefore reaches the highest goal.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.30 He who sees that all acts are done universally by Prakrti alone and likewise that the self is not the doer, he sees indeed.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.31 When he perceives the independent modes of existence of all beings centred in one, and as also their expansion from It alone, then he attains to brahman.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.32 This supreme self, though dwelling in the body, is immutable, O Arjuna, being without beginning. It neither acts nor is tainted, as It is without Gunas.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.33 As the all-pervading etther is not tainted because of its subtlety, even so, the self abiding in the body everywhere, is not tainted.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.34 As the one sun illumines this whole world, so does the Knower of the Field (Ksetrin, the self), O Arjuna, illumine the whole Field (the body).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 13.35 Those who thus discern with the eye of knowledge the difference between the body or the Field (Ksetra) and the knower of the body or Field-knower (Ksetrajna), and the means of deliverance from the manifested Prakrti - they attain the Supreme.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.1 The Lord said I shall declare again another kind of knowledge: It is the best of all forms of knowledge, by knowing which all the sages have attained the state of perfection beyond this world.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.2 Resorting to this knowledge, partaking of My Nature, they are not born at the time of creation, nor do they suffer at the time of dissolution.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.3 My womb is the great brahman (i.e. Prakrti). In that I lay the germ. From that, O Arjuna, is the birth of all beings.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.4 Whatever forms are produced in any womb, O Arjuna, the Prakrti is their great womb and I am the sowing father.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.5 Sattva, Rajas and Tamas are the Gunas that arise from the Prakrti. They bind the immutable self in the body, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.6 Of these, Sattva, being without impurity, is luminous and free from morbidity. It binds, O Arjuna, by attachment to pleasure and to knowledge.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.7 Know, O Arjuna, that Rajas is of the nature of passion springing from thirst and atttachment. It binds the embodied self with attachment to work.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.8 Know that Tamas is born of false knowledge and deludes all embodied selves. It binds, O Arjuna, with negligence, indolence and sleep.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.9 Sattva generates attachment to pleasure, Rajas to action, O Arjuna. But Tamas, veiling knowledge, generates attachment to negligence.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.10 Prevailing over Rajas and Tamas, Sattva preponderates, O Arjuna. Prevailing over Tamas and Sattva, Rajas preponderates. Prevailing over Rajas and Sattva, Tamas preponderates.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.11 When knowledge as light illumines from all gateways (i.e., the senses), then, one should know that Sattva prevails.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.12 Greed, activity, undertaking of work, unrest and longing - these arise, O Arjuna, when Rajas prevails.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.13 Non-illumination, inactivity, negligence and even delusion - these arise, O Arjuna, when Tamas prevails.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.14 If the embodied self meets with dissoution when Sattva prevails, then It proceeds to the pure worlds of those who know the highest.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
14.15 (a) Meeting with dissolution when Rajas is prevalent, one is born among those attached to work৷৷.
(b) Similarly, one who has met with dissolution when Tamas prevails, is born in the womb of beings lacking in intelligence.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.16 The fruits of a good deed, they say, is pure and is of the nature of Sattva. But the fruit of Rajas is pain; and the fruit of Tamas is ignorance.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.17 From the Sattva arises knowledge, and from Rajas greed, from Tamas arise negligence and delusion, and, indeed ignorance.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.18 Those who rest in Sattva rise upwards; those who abide in Rajas remain in the middle; and those, abiding in the tendencies of Tamas go downwards.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.19 When the seer beholds no agent of action other than the Gunas, and knows what transcends the Gunas, he attains to My state.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.20 The embodied self, crossing beyond these three Gunas which arise in the body, and freed from birth, death, age and pain, attains immortality.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.21 Arjuna said What are the marks of a man who has crossed beyond the three Gunas? What is his behaviour? And how does he cross beyond the three Gunas?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.22 The Lord said He hates not illumination, nor activity nor even delusion, O Arjuna, while these prevail, nor longs for them when they cease.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.23 He who sits like one unconcerned, undisturbed by the Gunas; who knows, 'It is the Gunas that move,' and so rests unshaken;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.24 He who is alike in pleasure and pain, who dwells in his self, who looks upon a clod, a stone and piece of gold as of eal value, who remains the same towards things dear and hateful and who is intelligent, who regards both blame and praise of himself as eal;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.25 He who is the same in honour and dishonour, and the same to friend and foe, and how has abandoned all enterprises - he is said to have risen above the Gunas.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.26 And he who, with unswerving Bhakti Yoga, serves Me, he, crossing beyond the Gunas, becomes fit for the state of Brahman.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 14.27 For I am the ground of Brahman, the immortal and immutable, of eternal Dharma and of perfect bliss.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.1 The Lord said They speak of an immutable Asvattha tree with its roots above and branches below. Its leaves are the Vedas. He who knows it knows the Vedas.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
15.2 (a) Its branches extend both above and below, nourished by the Gunas. Their shoots are sense objects ৷৷.
(b) ৷৷. And their secondary roots extend downwards, resulting in acts which bind in the world of men.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.3 Its form as such is not perceived here, nor its end, nor its beginning, nor its support. Having cut off this firm-rooted Asvattha with the strong axe of detachment৷৷.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.4 Then, one should seek that goal attaining which one never returns. One should seek refuge with that Primal Person from whom streamed forth this ancient activity.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.5 Without the delusion of perverse notions (concerning the self), victorious over the evil of attachment, ever devoted to the self, turned away from desires and liberated from dualities called pleasure and pain, the undeluded go to that imperishable status.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.6 That supreme light (i.e. the individual self), reaching which they do not return any more, is Mine; the sun does not illumine It, nor moon, nor the fire.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.7 An everlasting part of Myself, having become the bound self in the world of life, attracts the senses, of which the mind is the sixth, and which abide in Prakrti.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.8 Whatever body Its lord acires and from whatever body It departs, It goes on Its way, taking these senses as the wind carrying scents from their places.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.9 Presiding over the ear, the eye, the sense of touch, the tongue and the nose, and the mind, It experiences these objects of senses.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.10 The deluded do not perceive It (i.e., the self) conjoined with the Gunas when departing or staying or experiencing. They who have the eye of knowledge see It.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.11 The striving Yogins see It established in themselves. But, though striving, those of unrefined minds, devoid of intelligence, perceive It not.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.12 That brilliance in the sun which illumines the whole universe, that in the moon and that in fire, know that brilliance as Mine.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.13 And entering the earth I uphold all beings by My strength. I nourish all herbs, becoming the juicy Soma.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.14 Becoming the digestive fire, I function within the bodies of all living beings. In union with inward and outward breath, I digest the four kinds of food.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.15 And I am seated in the hearts of all. From Me are memory, knowledge and their removal also. Indeed I alone am to be known from all the Vedas. I bring about the fruition of the rituals of Vedas; I alone am the knower of the Vedas.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.16 There are two kinds of Persons (Purusas) spoken of in the Sastra - the perishable (Ksara) and the imperishable (Aksara). The perishable is all beings and the imperishable is called the unchanging (Kutastha).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.17 There is the Supreme Person other than these. He is named the Supreme Self (Paramatma) in all the Vedas. He who, as the Immutable One and the Lord, entering the threefold world, supports it.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.18 Because I transcend the perishable Person and am also higher than the imperishable person, therefore I am styled in the Smrti and the Veda as the Supreme Person (Purusotama).

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.19 He who, without delusion thus knows Me as the Supreme Self, knows all, O Arjuna, and worships Me in every way.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.20 Thus, O sinless one, has this most mysterious doctrine been imparted by Me. By understanding this, a man will become truly wise and will have fulfilled his duty.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.1 The Lord said Fearlessness, purity of mind, devotion to meditation on the knowledge (of the self), alms-giving, self-control, worship, study of Vedas, austerity, uprightness:

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.2 Non-injury, truth, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranillity, non-slandering others, compassion to all beings, freedom from desire, gentleness, the sense of shame, freedom from fickleness;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.3 Grandeur, patience, fortitude, purity, freedom from hatred, and from over-pride - these, O Arjuna, belong to him who is born to a divine destiny.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.4 Pomposity, arrogance, self-conceit, wrath, rudeness and ignorance - these, O Arjuna, belong to him who is born to a demoniac destiny.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.5 The divine destiny is deemed to lead to liberation, the demoniac to bondage. Grieve not, O Arjuna, you are born to a divine destiny.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.6 There are two types of beings in this world - the divine and the demoniac. The divine has been described at length. Hear from Me, O Arjuna, about the demoniac.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.7 The demoniac men know neither action nor renunciation. Cleanliness is not in them, nor even right conduct, nor truth.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.8 They maintain: 'The universe is without truth, without any foundation and without a Lord (Isvara). What else can exist without mutual causation? It has lust for its cause.'

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.9 Holding this view, these men of lost souls and fele understanding do cruel deeds for the destruction of the world.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.10 Turning to insatiable desires, seizing through delusion unjustly acired wealth, and following impious vows, they act, full of ostentation, pride and arrogance.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.11 Obsessed by unlimited cares which end with dissolution, looking upon enjoyment of desires as their highest aim, and convinced that this is all;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.12 Bound by hundreds of fetters of hopes, given over to desire and anger, they strive unjustly to gather wealth for the gratification of their desires.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.13 'This I have gained today, and this desire I shall attain. This wealth is mine, and this also shall be mine hereaftter .

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.14 'This enemy is slain by me; and others also I shall slay. I am the Lord, I am the enjoyer, I am successful, I have strength, I have happiness.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.15 ' I am wealthy and high-born; who else is eal to me? I shall sacrifice, I shall give alms, I shall rejoice.' Thus they think, deluded byignorance.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.16 Bewildered by many thoughts, ensnared by the net of delusion, addicted to sensual enjoyments, they fall into a foul Naraka.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.17 Self-conceited, self-sufficient, possessed of the intoxication of wealth and pride, they perform sacrifices in name only, with ostentation and not according to the injunctions of the Sastras.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.18 Depending on their egoism, power and pride, and also of desire and wrath, these malicious men hate Me in their own bodies and in those of others.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.19 Those haters, cruel, the vilest and the most inauspicious of mankind, I hurl forever into the cycles of births and deaths, into the wombs of demons.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.20 Fallen into demoniac wombs in birth after birth, these deluded men, not attaining Me, further sink down to the lowest level, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.21 Desire, wrath and greed - this is the triple gateway to Naraka, ruinous to the self. Therefore one should abandon these three.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.22 One who has been released from these threefold gates of darkness, O Arjuna, works for the good of the self. Hence he reaches the supreme state.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.23 He who, abandoning the injunctions of the Sastras, acts under the influence of desire, attains neither perfection nor pleasure, nor the supreme state.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.24 Therefore, let the Sastra be your authority for determining what should be done and what should not be done. Knowing what is enjoined in the injunctions of the Sastra, you should perform work here.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.1 Arjuna said Now what, O Krsna, is the position or basis of those who leave aside the injunction of the Sastra, yet worship with faith? Is it Sattva, Rajas or Tamas?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.2 The Lord said Threefold is the faith of embodied beings, born of their own nature, constituted of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Listen now about it.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.3 The faith of everyone, O Arjuna, is in accordance with his internal organ (Antahkarana). Man consists of faith. Whatever his faith is, that verily is he.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.4 The Sattvika types worship the gods. The Rajasa types worship Yaksas and Raksasas. And the others, the Tamasa types, worship the departed ancestors and hosts of Bhutas.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.5 Those men who practise terrible austerity not enjoined by the Sastras, given to ostentation and conceit, and prompted by the force of sensual desires and passion;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.6 These foolish men, torturing the group of elements in their bodies and Me also who dwell within the body - know them to be demoniacal in their resolves.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.7 Even the food which is dear to all is threefold. So are sacrifices, austeritty and gifts. Listen about this distinction among them.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.8 Foods which promote longevity, intellectual alertness, strength, health, pleasure and happiness and those that are sweet, oil, substantial and agreeable, are dear to Sattvika men.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.9 Foods that are bitter, sour, very salty, exceedingly heating, very pungent, dry and burning, are all dear to Rajasika men; they produce pain, sorrow and disease.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.10 That food which is stale, tasteless, putrid, decayed, refuse, unclean, is dear to Tamasika men.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.11 The sacrifice (worship) marked by Sattva is what is offered by those desiring no fruit, and having the conviction that it should be performed as enjoined in the Sastras.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.12 But that sacrifice which is offered with the fruit in view and for the sake of ostentation, know it, O Arjuna, to be Rajasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.13 That sacrifice which is bereft of authority, which uses offerings not sanctioned by the Sastras, which is performed without recitation of hymns and bereft of gifts and faith - that, they say, is marked by Tamas.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.14 Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the preceptors, the enlightened ones, purity, uprightness, continence and non-injury, these are called austerity of the body.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.15 Speech that causes no shock (hurt and fear etc.) and which is true, pleasant and beneficial, and also the practice of recitation of the scriptures are called the austerity of speech.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.16 Serenity of mind, benevolence, silence, self-control, purity of mind - these are called austerity of the mind.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.17 The threefold austerity, practised with supreme faith by men who desire no fruit and are devoted - they call it austerity of Sattva.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.18 That austerity, pracitsed with ostentation for the sake of gaininng respect, praise and reverence, is here said to be Rajasa. It is unsteady and impermanent.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.19 That austerity which is practised from deluded notions by means of self-torture or in order to injure another is said to be Tamasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.20 Gifts given with the feeling, that it is one's own duty to give to one who makes no return, at the proper place and time to the deserving person - that is said to be Sattvika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.21 But that which is given as a consideration for something receievd or in expectation of future reward, or grudgingly, is called Rajasika gift.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.22 That gift which is given at the wrong place and wrong time to unworthy recipients, without due respect and with contempt, is called the gift of Tamasa nature.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.23 Om, Tat, Sat - thus Brahman is denoted by this threefold expression. Associated with these, Brahmanas, the Vedas and sacrifices were ordained in the past.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.24 Therefore, the Veda-enjoined sacrificial acts, gifts and austerity by these expounders of the Veda, or those belonging to the first three stations are always and at all times begun after pronouncing Om at the beginning.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.25 Acts of sacrifice, of austeritty and of various gifts are performed without aiming at reward by those who seek release, after pronouncing Tat.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.26 This term Sat is used in the sense of existence and goodness. And so also, O Arjuna, the word Sat is applied to an auspicious action.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.27 Devotion to sacrifice, austerities and gifts is also called Sat; and so any act for such purposes is named Sat.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.28 Whatever offering or gift is made, whatever austerity is practised and whatever action is performed without faith, that is called Asat, O Arjuna. It is naught here or hereafter.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.1 Arjuna said I desire to know the truth about renunciation (Sannyasa) and abnegation (Tyaga) severally, O Krsna.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.2 The Lord said The sages hold that Sannyasa is the giving up of all works which are motivated by desire. The wise declare Tyaga to be the abandonment of fruits of all works.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.3 Some sages say that all actions should be given up as evil; others declare that works such as sacrifices, gifts and austerities should not be given up.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.4 Listen to My decision, O Arjuna, about abandonment; for abandonment (Tyaga) is declared to be of three kinds.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
18.5 (a) The acts of sacrifice, gifts and austerities should not be relinished; but should be performed৷৷.
(b). ৷৷.For sacrifices, gifts and austerities are the means of purification for the wise.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.6 It is My decided and final view that even these acts should be done, O Arjuna, with relinishment of attachment and the fruits thereof.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.7 But the renunciation of obligatory acts is not proper. Abandonment of these through delusion is declared to be Tamasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.8 He who renounces acts as painful from fear of bodily suffering, performs a Rajasika abandonment; he does not gain the fruit of abandonment.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.9 When actions are performed as what ought to be done, O Arjuna, renouncing attachment and also fruits, such abandonment is regarded as Sattvika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.10 One who has abandoned, who is imbued with Sattva, who is wise, whose doubts have been dispelled - such a person hates not disagreeable acts nor clings to agreeable ones.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.11 For, it is impossible for one who bears a body to abandon actions entirely. But he who gives up the fruits of works, is called the abandoner.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.12 Undesirable, desirable and mixed - thus threefold is the fruit of work that accrues after death to those who have not renounced; but to those who have renounced, none whatsoever.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.13 Learn from Me, O Arjuna, these five causes for the accomplishment of all acts, as described in Sankhya-krtanta - the science of the exact understanding of things for the accomplishment of works.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.14 The seat of action and likewise the agent, the various kinds of organs, the different and distinctive functions of vital air and also the fifth among these, Divinity.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.15 For whatever action a man undertakes by his body, speech and mind, whether right or wrong, i.e., enjoined or forbidden by the Sastras, the following five are its causes:

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.16 Such being the case, he who sees only the self as the agent on account of the uncultivated understanding - he, of wicked mind, does not see at all.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.17 He who is free from the notion 'I am the doer,' and whose understanding is not tainted - slays not, though he slays all these men, nor is he bound.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.18 Knowledge, object of knowledge and the knower are the threefold incitements to action. The instrument, the act and the agent are the threefold constituents of action.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.19 Knowledge, act and agent are declared in the science of Gunas to be of three kinds, according to the difference in the Gunas. Listen about them also as they are.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.20 Know that Knowledge to be Sattvika by which one sees in all beings, one immutable existence undivided in the divided.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.21 But that knowledge which sees all beings, by reason of their individuality, as entities of distinct nature - know that knowledge to be Rajasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.22 But that knowledge is declared to be Tamasika which clings to one single act as if it were the whole, which is not founded on reason, and which is untrue and insignificant.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.23 That obligatory act is said to be Sattvika which is done without attachment, without desire or aversion, by one who seeks no fruit.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.24 But that act is said to be Rajasika which is performed with great effort by one who seeks to gratify his desires and under the prompting of egoism.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.25 That act is said to be Tamasika which is undertaken through delusion, without regard to conseences, loss, injury and one's own capacity.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.26 That agent is said to be Sattvika who is free from attachment, who does not make much of himself, who is endued with steadiness and zeal and is untouched by success and failure.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.27 That doer is called Rajasika who is passionate, who seeks the fruits of his acts, who is greedy, harmful, impure and who is moved by delight and grief.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.28 That doer is said to be Tamasika who is unalified, unrefined, stubborn, depraved, dishonest, indolent, despondent and dilatory.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.29 Hear now, the threefold division of Buddhi (reason) and Dhrti (fortitude), O Arjuna, according to the Gunas, fully and severally to be set forth.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.30 That Buddhi, O Arjuna, which knows activity and renunciation, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and release - that (Buddhi) is Sattvika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.31 The Buddhi which gives an erroneous knowledge of Dharma and Adharma (its opposite) and also of what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, O Arjuna, is Rajasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.32 That Buddhi, O Arjuna, which, enveloped in darkness, regards Adharma as Dharma and which reverses every value, is Tamasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.33 That Dhrti (fortitude or persisting perseverance) by which one maintains the unswerving activities of the mind and vital force and these sense-organs through Yoga - that Dhrti is of the nature of Sattva.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.34 That Dhrti, O Arjuna, by which one, who is desirous of fruits, longs for them with intense attachment, and holds fast to duty, desire and wealth - that Dhrti is Rajasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.35 That Dhrti by which a foolish person does not give up sleep, fear, grief, depression and passion, O Arjuna, is of the nature of Tamas.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.36 Now hear from Me, O Arjuna, the threefold division of pleasure৷৷. that in which a man rejoices by long practice and in which he comes to the end of pain;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.37 That which is like a poison at first but becomes like elixir in the end, born from the serene state of mind focusing on the self - such pleasure is said to be Sattvika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.38 That pleasure which arises from the contact of senses with their objects, which is like elixir at first but like poison in the end, is said to be Rajasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.39 That pleasure which, at the beginning and at the end, deludes the self, through sleep, sloth and error - is declared to be Tamasika.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.40 There is no creature, either on earth or again among the gods in heaven, that is free from these three Gunas born of Prakrti.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.41 The duties of the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and the Sudras are clearly divided, O Arjuna, according to Gunas, born of their nature.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.42 Control of the senses and the mind, austerity, purity, forbearance, uprightness, knowledge, special knowledge, and faith - all these constitute the duty of Brahmana born of his inherent nature.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.43 Valour, invincibility, steadiness, adroitness and non-fleeing in battle, generosity and lordliness are the duties of a Ksatriya born of his inherent nature.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.44 Agriculture, cattle-breeding and trade are the duties of the Vaisya born of his nature৷৷. And the duty of a Sudra is one of service, born of his nature.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.10 He who acts without attachment, reposing all actions on Brahman (Prakrti), is untouched by evil, as a lotus-leaf by water.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.46 He from whome arise the activity of all beings and by whom all this is pervaded - by worshipping Him with his own duty man reaches perfection.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.47 Better is one's own duty, though ill done, than the duty of another, though well-performed৷৷৷৷৷৷ When one does the duty ordained by his own nature, he incurs no stain.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.48 One should not relinish one's works, O Arjuna, though it may be imperfect; for, all enterprises are enveloped by imperfections as fire by smoke.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.49 He whose understanding is on all sides unattached, whose self is conered, who is free from desires - he attains by renunciation the supreme perfection transcending all activity.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.50 Learn from me in brief, O Arjuna, how, one who has attained perfection, attains the brahman (or the self), who is the supreme consummation of knowledge.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.51 Endowed by a purified understanding, subduing the mind by steadiness, relinishing sound and other objectts of the senses and casting aside love and hate;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.52 Resorting to solitude, eating but little, restraining speech, body and mind, ever engaged in the Yoga of meditation and taking refuge in dispassion;

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.53 Forsaking egoism, power, pride, desire, wrath and possession, with no feeling of 'mine' and tranil - he becomes worthy for the state of brahman.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.54 Having realised the state of Brahman, tranil, he neither grieves nor craves. Regarding all beings alike, he attains supreme devotion to Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.55 Through devotion, he comes to know Me fully - who and what I am in reality, who I am and how I am. Knowing Me thus in truth, he forthwith enters into Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.56 Taking refuge in Me and performing all works constantly, one, by My grace, attains the eternal and immutable realm.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.57 Surrendering all acts to me by your mind, thinking of Me as the goal, and resorting to Buddhi-yoga, focus your thought ever on Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.58 Focusing your thought on Me, you shall, by My grace, cross over all difficulties. If, however, out of self-conceit, you do not heed Me, you shall perish.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.59 If, in your self-conceit, you think, 'I will not fight,' your resolve is in vain. Nature will compel you.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.60 O Arjuna, bound by your own duty born out of your own inner disposition, and having no control over your own will, you will be compelled to do that very thing which you now desire not to do through delusion.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.61 The Lord, O Arjuna, abides in the heart of every being, spinning them round and round, mounted on a wheel as it were, by His power.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.62 Seek refuge in Him alone, O Arjuna, with the whole of your being. By His grace, you shall find supreme peace and eternal abode.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.63 Thus the knowledge, the mystery of mysteries, has been declared to you be Me. Reflecting on it fully, do what you will.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.64 Hear again My supreme word, the most secret of all; as you are exceedingly loved by Me, I am telling what is good for you.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.65 Focus your mind on Me. Be My devotee. Be My worshipper. Prostrate before Me. You shall come to Me alone. I promise you, trully; for you are dear to Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.66 Completely relinishing all Dharmas, seek Me alone for refuge. I will release you from all sins. Grieve not:

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.67 Never should this be told by you to one who is not austere, who is not a devotee, nor to one who has no wish to listen, nor certainly to him who traduces Me.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.68 He who proclaims among My devotees this supreme mystery, shall come to Me, aciring supreme devotion towards Me. There is no doubt about this.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.69 Not among men is there any one who does dearer service to Me than he. Nor shall there be another on earth dearer to Me than he.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.70 And he who will study his dialogue of ours which is consistent with Dharma, by him I shall be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge; such is My view.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.71 And the man who listens to it with faith and without cavilling, he too shall be released, and shall reach the auspicious realms of those who have performed virtuous deeds.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.72 Have you heard this, O Arjuna, with one-pointed mind? Has your delusion, caused by ignorance, been dispelled?

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.73 Arjuna said Destroyed is my delusion and I have, by your grace, O Krsna, gained knowledge (Smrti). Freed from doubts, I stand steadfast, I will fulfil Your world.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.74 Sanjaya said Thus have I heard this wondrous dialogue between Vasudeva and the great-minded Arjuna, which makes my hair stand on end.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.75 By the grace of Vyasa have I heard this supreme mystery of Yoga as declared in person by Krsna, the Lord of Yoga.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.76 O King, remembering again and again this wondrous and auspicious dialogue betweenn Sri Krsna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.77 And remembering over and over again that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my amazement, O King, and I rejoice again and again.

author: Swami Adidevananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.78 Wherever there is Sri Krsna, the Lord of Yoga, and Arjuna the archer, there are ever fortune, victory, wealth and sound morality. This is my firm conviction.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.1. Dhrtarastra said O Sanjaya, what did my sons (and others) and Pandu's sons (and others) actually do when, eager for battle, they assembled on the sacred field, the Kuruksetra (Field of the Kurus)?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.2 Sanjaya said But then, seeing the army of the Pandavas in battle array, King Duryodhana approached the teacher (Drona) and uttered a speech:

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.3 O teacher, (please) see this vast army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed for battle by the son of Drupada, your intelligent disciple.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.4 Here are the heroes wielding great bows, who in battle are compeers of Bhima and Arjuna: Yuyudhana (Satyaki) and Virata, and the maharatha (great chariot-rider) Drupada;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.5 Dhrstaketu, Cekitana, and the valiant king of Kasi (Varanasi); Purujit and Kuntibhoja, and Saibya, the choicest among men;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.6 And the chivalrous Yudhamanyu, and the valiant Uttamaujas; son of Subhadra (Abhimanyu) and the sons of Draupadi all (of whom) are, verily, maharathas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.7 But, O best among the Brahmanas, please be appraised of those who are foremost among us, the ?nders of my army. I speak of them to you by way of example.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.8 (They are:) Your venerable self, Bhisma and Karna, and Krpa who is ever victorious in battle; Asvatthama, Vikarna, Saumadatti and Jayadratha.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.9 There are many heroes who have dedicated their lives for my sake, who possess various kinds of weapons and missiles, (and) all of whom are skilled in battle.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.10 Therefore, our army under the complete protection of Bhisma and others is unlimited. But this army of these (enemies), under the protection of Bhima and others is limited.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.11 However, venerable sirs, all of you without exception, while occupying all the positions in the different directions as alloted (to you respectively), please fully protect Bhisma in particular.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.12 The valiant grandfather, the eldest of the Kurus, loudly sounding a lion-roar, blew the conch to raise his (Duryodhana's) spirits.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.13 Just immediately after that conchs and kettledrums, and tabors, trumpets and cow-horns blared forth. That sound became tumultuous.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.14 Then, Madhava (Krsna) and the son of Pandu (Arjuna), stationed in their magnificent chariot with white horses yoked to it, loudly blew their divine conchs.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.15 Hrsikesa (Krsna) (blew the conch) Pancajanya; Dhananjaya (Arjuna) (the conch) Devadatta; and Vrkodara (Bhima) of terrible deeds blew the great conch Paundra;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.16 King Yudhisthira, son of Kunti, (blew) the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva, the Sughosa and the Manipuspaka (respectively).

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.17 And the King of Kasi, wielding a great bow, and the great chariot-rider Sikhandi, Dhrstadyumna and Virata, and Satyaki the unconered;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.18 Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, and the son of Subhadra, (Abhimanyu) the mighty-armed all (of them) together, O king, blew their respective conchs.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.19 That tremendous sound pierced the hearts of the sons of Dhrtarastra as it reverberated through the sky and the earth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.20 O king, thereafter, seeing Dhrtarastra's men standing in their positions, when all the weapons were ready for action, the son of Pandu (Arjuna) who had the insignia of Hanuman of his chariot-flag, raising up his bow, said the following to Hrsikesa.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.21 Arjuna said O Acyuta, please place my chariot between both the armies .

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.22 until I survey these who stand intent on fighting, and those who are going to engage in battle with me in this impending war.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.23 These who have assembled here and want to accomplish in the war what is dear to the perverted son of Dhrtarastra, I find them to be intent on fighting.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.24 1.25 Sanjay said O scion of the line of Bharata (Dhrtararastra), Hrsikesa, being told so by Gudakesa (Arjuna), placed the excellent chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhisma and Drona as also all the rulers of the earth, and said, 'O Partha (Arjuna), see these assempled people of the Kuru dynasty.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.24 1.25 Sanjay said O scion of the line of Bharata (Dhrtararastra), Hrsikesa, being told so by Gudakesa (Arjuna), placed the excellent chariot between the two armies, in front of Bhisma and Drona as also all the rulers of the earth, and said, 'O Partha (Arjuna), see these assempled people of the Kuru dynasty.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.26 Then Partha (Arjuna) saw, marshalled among both the armies, (his) uncles as also grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers (and (cousins), sons, grandsons, as well as comrades and fathers-in-law and friends.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.27 The son of Kunti (Ajuna), seeing all those rlatives arrayed (there), became overwhelmed by supreme compassion and said this sorrowfully:

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.28 Arjuna said O Krsna, seeing these relatives and friends who have assembled here with the intention of fighting, my limbs become languid and my mouth becomes completely dry.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.29 And there is trembling in my body, and there is horripillation; the Gandiva (bow) slips from the hand and even the skin burns intensely.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.30 Moreover, O Kesava (Krsna), I am not able to stand firmly, and my mind seems to be whirling. And I notice the omens to be adverse.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.31 Besides, I do not see any good (to be derived) from killing my own people in battle. O Krsna, I do not hanker after victory, nor even a kingdom nor pleasures.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.32 1.34 O Govinda! What need do we have of a kingdom, or what (need) of enjoyments and livelihood? Those for whom kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures ae desired by us, viz teachers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law as also relatives-those very ones stand arrayed for battle risking their lives and wealth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.32 1.34 O Govinda! What need do we have of a kingdom, or what (need) of enjoyments and livelihood? Those for whom kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures ae desired by us, viz teachers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law as also relatives-those very ones stand arrayed for battle risking their lives and wealth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
