alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.32 1.34 O Govinda! What need do we have of a kingdom, or what (need) of enjoyments and livelihood? Those for whom kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures ae desired by us, viz teachers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law as also relatives-those very ones stand arrayed for battle risking their lives and wealth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.35 O Madhusudana, even if I am killed, I do not want to kill these even for the sake of a kingdom extending over the three worlds; what to speak of doing so for the earth!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.36 O Janardana, what happiness shall we derive by killing the sons of Dhrtarastra? Sin alone will accrue to us by killing these felons.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.37 Therefore, it is not proper for us to kill the sons of Dhrtarastra who are our own relatives. For, O Madhava, how can we be happy by killing our kinsmen?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.38 1.39 O Janardana, although these people, whose hearts have become perverted by greed, do not see the evil arising from destroying the family and sin in hostility towards, friends, yet how can we who clearly see the evil arising from destroying the family remain unaware of (the need of) abstaining from this sin?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.38 1.39 O Janardana, although these people, whose hearts have become perverted by greed, do not see the evil arising from destroying the family and sin in hostility towards, friends, yet how can we who clearly see the evil arising from destroying the family remain unaware of (the need of) abstaining from this sin?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.40 From the ruin of the family are totally destroyed the traditional rites and duties of the family. When rites and duties are destroyed, vice overpowers the entire family also.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.41 O Krsna, when vice predominates, the women of the family become corrupt. O descendent of the Vrsnis, when women become corrupted, it results in the intermingling of castes.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.42 And the intermingling in the family leads the ruiners of the family verily into hell. The forefathers of these fall down (into hell) because of being deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and water.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.43 Due to these misdeeds of the ruiners of the family, which cause intermingling of castes, the traditional rites and duties of the castes and families become destroyed.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.44 O Janardana, we have heard that living in hell becomes inevitable for those persons whose family duties get destroyed.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.45 What a pity that we have resolved to commit a great sin by being eager to kill our own kith and kin, out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.46 If, in this battle, the sons of Dhrtarastra armed with weapons kill me who am non-resistant and unarmed, that will be more beneficial to me.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 1.47 Sanjaya narrated: Having said so, Arjuna, with a mind afflicted with sorrow, sat down on the chariot in the midst of the battle, casting aside the bow along with the arrows.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.1 Sanjaya said To him who had been thus filled with pity, whose eyes were filled with tears and showed distress, and who was sorrowing, Madhusudana uttered these words:

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.2 The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, in this perilous place, whence has come to you this impurity entertained by unenlightened persons, which does not lead to heaven and which brings infamy?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.3 O Partha, yield not to unmanliness. This does not befit you. O scorcher of foes, arise, giving up the petty weakness of the heart.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.4 Arjuna said O Madhusudana, O destroyer of enemies, how can I fight with arrows in battle against Bhisma and Drona who are worthy of adoration?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.5 Rather than killing the noble-minded elders, it is better in this world to live even on alms. But by killing the elders we shall only be enjoying here the pleasures of wealth and desireable things drenched in blood.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.6 We do not know this as well as to which is the better for us, (and) whether we shall win, or whether they shall coner us. Those very sons of Dhrtarastra, by killing whom we do not wish to live, stand in confrontation.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.7 With my nature overpowered by weak commiseration, with a mind bewildered about duty, I supplicate You. Telll me for certain that which is better; I am Your disciple. Instruct me who have taken refuge in You.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.8 Because, I do not see that which can, even after aciring on this earth a prosperous kingdom free from enemies and even sovereignty over the gods, remove my sorrow (which is) blasting the senses.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.9 Sanjaya said Having spoken thus to Hrsikesa (Krsna), Gudakesa (Arjuna), the afflictor of foes, verily became silent, telling Govinda, 'I shall not fight.' fight.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.10 O descendant of Bharata, to him who was sorrowing between the two armies, Hrsikesa, mocking as it were, said these words:

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.11 The Blessed Lord said You grieve for whose who are not to be grieved for; and you speak words of wisdom! The learned do not grieve for the departed and those who have not departed.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.12 But certainly (it is) not (a fact) that I did not exist at any time; nor you, nor these rulers of men. And surely it is not that we all shall cease to exist after this.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.13 As are boyhood, youth and decrepitude to an embodied being in this (present) body, similar is the acisition of another body. This being so, an intelligent person does not get deluded.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.14 But the contacts of the organs with the objects are the producers of cold and heat, happiness and sorrow. They have a beginning and an end, (and) are transient. Bear them, O descendant of Bharata.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.15 O (Arjuna, who are) foremost among men, verily, the person whom these do not torment, the wise man to whom sorrow and happhiness are the same he is fit for Immortality.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.16 Of the unreal there is no being; the real has no nonexistence. But the nature of both these, indeed, has been realized by the seers of Truth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.17 But know That to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded. None can bring about the destruction of this Immutable.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.18 These destructible bodies are said to belong to the everlasting, indestructible, indeterminable, embodied One. Therefore, O descendant of Bharata, join the battle.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.19 He who thinks of this One as the killer, and he who thinks of this One as the killed both of them do not know. This One does not kill, nor is It killed.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.20 Never is this One born, and never does It die; nor is it that having come to exist, It will again cease to be. This One is birthless, eternal, undecaying, ancient; It is not killed when the body is killed.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.21 O Partha, he who knows this One as indestructible, eternal, birthless and undecaying, how and whom does that person kill, or whom does he cause to be killed! [This is not a estion but only an emphatic denial.-Tr.]

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.22 As after rejecting wornout clothes a man takes up other new ones, likewise after rejecting wornout bodies the embodied one unites with other new ones.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.23 Weapons do not cut It, fire does not burn It, water does not moisten It, and air does not dry It.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.24 It cannot be cut, It cannot be burnt, cannot be moistened, and surely cannot be dried up. It is eternal, omnipresent, stationary, unmoving and changeless.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.25 It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.26 On the other hand, if you think this One is born continually or dies constantly, even then, O mighty-armed one, you ought not to grieve thus.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.27 For death of anyone born is certain, and of the dead (re-) birth is a certainly. Therefore you ought not to grieve over an inevitable fact.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.28 O descendant of Bharata, all beings remain unmanifest in the beginning;; they become manifest in the middle. After death they certainly become unmanifest. What lamentation can there be with regard to them?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.29 Someone visualizes It as a wonder; and similarly indeed, someone else talks of It as a wonder; and someone else hears of It as a wonder. And some one else, indeed, does not realize It even after hearing about It.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.30 O descendant of Bharata, this embodied Self existing in everyone's body can never be killed. Therefore you ought not to grieve for all (these) beings.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.31 Even considering your own duty you should not waver, since there is nothing else better for a Ksatriya than a righteous battle.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.32 O son of Partha, happy are the Ksatriyas who come across this kind of a battle, which presents itself unsought for and which is an open gate to heaven.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.33 On the other hand, if you will not fight this righteous battle, then, forsaking your own duty and fame, you will incur sin.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.34 People also will speak of your unending infamy. And to an honoured person infamy is worse than death.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.35 The great chariot-riders will think of you as having desisted from the fight out of fear; and you will into disgrace before them to whom you had been estimable.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.36 And your enemies will speak many indecent words while denigrating your might. What can be more painful than that?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.37 Either by being killed you will attain heaven, or by winning you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, O Arjuna, rise up with determination for fighting.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.38 Treating happiness and sorrow, gain and loss, and conest and defeat with eanimity, then engage in battle. Thus you will not incur sin.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.39 O Partha, this wisdom has been imparted to you from the standpoint of Self-realization. But listen to this (wisdom) from the standpoint of Yoga, endowed with which wisdom you will get rid of the bondage of action.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.40 Here there is no waste of an attempt; nor is there (any) harm. Even a little of this righteousness saves (one) from great fear.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.41 O scion of the Kuru dynasty, in this there is a single, one-pointed conviction. The thoughts of the irresolute ones have many branches indeed, and are innumerable.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.42-2.43 O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence , they remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as the goal.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.42-2.43 O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence , they remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as the goal.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.44 One-pointed conviction does not become established in the minds of those who delight in enjoyment and affluence, and whose intellects are carried away by that (speech).

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.45 O Arjuna, the Vedas [Meaning only the portion dealing with rites and duties (karma-kanda).] have the three alities as their object. You become free from worldliness, free from the pairs of duality, ever-poised in the ality of sattva, without (desire for) acisition and protection, and self-collected.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.46 A Brahmana with realization has that much utility in all the Vedas as a man has in a well when there is a flood all around.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.47 Your right is for action alone, never for the results. Do not become the agent of the results of action. May you not have any inclination for inaction.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.48 By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.49 O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.50 Possessed of wisdom, one rejects here both virtue and vice. Therefore devote yourself to (Karma-) yoga. Yoga is skilfulness in action.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.51 Because, those who are devoted to wisdom, (they) becoming men of Enlightenment by giving up the fruits produced by actions, reach the state beyond evils by having become freed from the bondage of birth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.52 When your mind will go beyond the turbidity of delusion, then you will acire dispassion for what has to be heard and what has been heard.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.53 When your mind that has become bewildered by hearing [S. takes the word sruti in the sense of the Vedas.-Tr.] will become unshakable and steadfast in the Self, then you will attain Yoga that arises from discrimination.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.54 Arjuna said O kesava, what is the description of a man of steady wisdom who is Self-absorbed? How does the man of steady wisdom speak? How does he sit? How does he move about?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.55 The Blessed said O Partha, when one fully renounces all the desires that have entered the mind, and remains satisfied in the Self alone by the Self, then he is called a man of steady wisdom.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.56 That monk is called a man of steady wisdom when his mind is unperturbed in sorrow, he is free from longing for delights, and has gone beyond attachment, fear and anger.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.57 The wisdom of that person remains established who has not attachment for anything anywhere, who neither welcomes nor rejects anything whatever good or bad when he comes across it.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.58 And when this one fully withdraws the senses from the objects of the senses, as a tortoise wholly (withdraws) the limbs, then his wisdom remains established.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.59 The objects recede from an abstinent man, with the exception of the taste (for them). Even the taste of this person falls away after realization the Absolute.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.60 For, O son of Kunti, the turbulent organs violently snatch away the mind of an intelligent person, even while he is striving diligently.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.61 Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.62-2.63 In the case of a person who dwells on objects, there arises attachment for them. From attachment grows hankering, from hankering springs anger.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.63 From anger follows delusion; from delusion, failure of memory; from failure of memory, the loss of understanding; from the loss of understanding, he perishes.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.64 But by perceiving objects with the organs that are free from attraction and repulsion, and are under his own control, the self-controlled man attains serenity.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.65 When there is serenity, there follows eradication of all his sorrows, because the wisdom of one who has a serene mind soon becomes firmly established.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.66 For the unsteady there is no wisdom, and there is no meditation for the unsteady man. And for an unmeditative man there is no peace. How can there be happiness for one without peace?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.67 For, the mind which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, that (mind) carries away his wisdom like the mind (diverting) a boat on the waters.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.68 Therefore, O mighty-armed one, this wisdom becomes established whose organs in all their varieties are withdrawn from their objects.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.69 The self-restrained man keeps awake during that which is night for all creatures. That during which creatures keep awake, it is night to the seeing sage.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.70 That man attains peace into whom all desires enter in the same way as the waters flow into a sea that remains unchanged (even) when being filled up from all sides. Not so one who is desirous of objects.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.71 That man attains peace who, after rejecting all desires, moves about free from hankering, without the idea of ('me' and) 'mine', and devoid of pride.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 2.72 O Partha, this is the state of being established in Brahman. One does not become deluded after attaining this. One attains identification with Brahman by being established in this state even in the closing years of one's life.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.1 Arjuna said O Janardana (krsna), if it be Your opinion that wisdom is superior to action, why they do you urge me to horrible aciton, O Kesava ?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.2 You bewilder my understanding, as it were, by a seemingly conflicting statement! Tell me for certain one of these by which I may attain the highest Good.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.3 The Blessed Lord said O unblemished one, two kinds of steadfastness in this world were spoken of by Me in the days of yore-through the Yoga of Knowledge for the men of realization; through the Yoga of Action for the yogis.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.4 A person does not attain freedom from action by abstaining from action; nor does he attain fulfilment merely through renunciation.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.5 Because, no one ever remains even for a moment without doing work. For all are made to work under compulsion by the gunas born of Nature.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.6 One, who after withdrawing the organs of action, sits mentally recollecting the objects of the senses, that one, of deluded mind, is called a hypocrite.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.7 But, O Arjuna, one who engages in Karma-yoga with the organs of action, controlling the organs with the mind and becoming unattached-that one excels.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.8 You perform the obligatory duties, for action is superior to inaction. And, through inaction, even the maintenance of your body will not be possible.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.9 This man becomes bound by actions other than that action meant for God. Without being attached, O son of Kunti, you perform actions for Him.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.10 In the days of yore, having created the beings together with the sacrifices, Prajapati said: 'By this you multiply. Let this be your yielder of coveted objects of desire.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.11 'You nourish the gods with this. Let those gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you shall attain the supreme Good.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.12 'Being nourished by sacrifices, the gods will indeed give you the coveted enjoyments. He is certainly a theif who enjoys what have been given by them without offering (these) to them.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.13 By becoming partakers of the remembers of sacrifices, they become freed from all sins. But the unholy persons who cook for themselves, they incur sin.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.14 From food are born the creatures; the origin of food is from rainfall; rainfall originates from sacrifice; sacrifice has action as its origin.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.15 Know that actin has the veda as its origin; the Vedas has the Immutable as its source. Hence, the all-pervading Veda is for ever based on sacrifice.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.16 O Partha, he lives in vain who does not follow here the wheel thus set in motion, whose life is sinful, and who indulges in the senses.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.17 But that man who rejoices only in theSelf and is satisfied with the Self, and is contented only in the Self-for him there is no duty to perform.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.18 For him there is no concern here at all with performing action; nor any (concern) with nonperformance. Moreover, for him there is no dependence on any object to serve any purpose.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.19 Therefore, remaining unattached, always perform the obligatory duty, for, by performing (one's) duty without attachment, a person attains the Highest.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.20 For Janaka and others strove to attain Liberation through action itself. You ought to perform (your duties) keeping also in view the prevention of mankind from going astray.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.21 Whatever a superior person does, another person does that very thing! Whatever he upholds as authority, an ordinary person follows that.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.22 In all the three worlds, O Partha, there is no duty whatsoever for Me (to fulfil); nothing remains unachieved or to be achieved. [According to S. the translation of this portion is: There is nothing unattained that should be attained.-Tr.] (Still) do I continue in action.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.23 For, O Partha, if at any time I do not continue [Ast. and A.A. read varteya instead of varteyam.-Tr.] vigilantly in action, men will follow My path in ever way.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.24 These worlds will be ruined if I do not perform action. And I shall become the agent of intermingling (of castes), and shall be destroying these beings.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.25 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, as the unelightened poeple act with attachment to work, so should the enlightened person act, without attachment, being desirous of the prevention of people from going astray.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.26 The enlightened man should not create disturbance in the beliefs of the ignorant, who are attached to work. Working, while himself remaining deligen [Some translate yuktah as, 'in the right manner'. S. takes it in the sense of Yoga-yuktah, merged in yoga.-Tr.], he should make them do [Another reading is yojayet, meaning the same as josayet.-Tr.] all the duties.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.27 While actions are being done in every way by the gunas (alities) of Nature, one who is deluded by egoism thinks thus: 'I am the doer.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.28 But, O mighty-armed one, the one who is a knower of the facts about the varieties of the gunas (alities) and actions does not become attached, thinking thus: 'The organs rest (act) on the objects of the organs.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.29 Those who are wholly deluded by the gunas of Nature become attached to the activities of the gunas. The knower of the All should not disturb those of dull intellect, who do not know the All.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.30 Devoid of the fever of the soul, engage in battle by dedicating all actions to Me, with (your) mind intent on the Self, and becoming free from expectations and egoism.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.31 Those men who ever follow this teaching of Mine with faith and without cavil, they also become freed from actions.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.32 But those who, decaying [Finding fault where there is none.] this, do not follow My teaching, know them-who are deluded about all knoweldge [Knowledge concerning the alified and the un-alified Brahman.] and who are devoid of discrimination-to have gone to ruin.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.33 Even a man of wisdom behaves according to his own nature. Being follow (their) nature. What can restraint do?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.34 Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.35 One's own duty [Customary or scripturally ordained observances of different castes and sects.-Tr.], though defective, is superior to another's duty well-performed. Death is better while engaged in one's own duty; another's duty is fraught with fear.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.36 Arjuna said Now then, O scion of the Vrsni dynasty (Krsna), impelled by what does this man commit sin even against his wish, being constrained by force, as it were?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.37 The Blessed Lord said This desire, this anger, born of the ality of rajas, is a great devourer, a great sinner. Know this to be the enemy here.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.38 As fire is enveloped by smoke, as a mirror by dirt, and as a foetus remains enclosed in the womb, so in this shrouded by that.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.39 O son of Kunti, Knowledge is covered by this constant enemy of the wise in the form of desire, which is an insatiable fire.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.40 The organs, mind, and the intellect are said to be its abode. This one diversely deludes the embodied being by veiling Knowledge with the help of these.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.41 Therefore, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, after first controlling the organs, renounce this one [A variant reading is, 'prajahi hi-enam, completely renounce this one'.-Tr.] which is sinful and a destroyer of learning and wisdom.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.42 They say that the organs are superior (to the gross body); the mind is superior to the organs; but the intellect is superior to the mind. However, the one who is superior to the intellect is He.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 3.43 [The Ast, introdcues this verse with, 'Tatah kim, what follows from that?'-Tr.] Understanding the Self thus [Understanding৷৷.thus:that desires can be conered through the knowledge of the Self.] as superior to the intellect, and completely establishing (the Self) is spiritual absorption with the (help of) the mind, O mighty-armed one, vanish the enemy in the form of desire, which is difficult to subdue.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.1 The Blessed Lord said I imparted this imperishable Yoga to Vivasvan, Vivasvan taught this to Manu, and Manu transmitted this to Iksavaku.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.2 The king-sages knew this (yoga) which was received thus in regular succession. That Yoga, O destroyer of foes, in now lost owing to a long lapse of time.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.3 That ancient Yoga itself, which is this, has been taught to you by Me today, considering that you are My devotee and friend, For, this (Yoga) is a profound secret.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.4 Arjuna said Your birth was later, (whereas) the birth of Vivasvan was earlier. How am I to understand this that You instructed (him) in the beginning?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.5 The Blessed Lord said O Arjuna, many lives of Mine have passed, and so have yours. I know them all, (but) you know not, O scorcher of enemies!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.6 Though I am birthless, undecaying by nature, and the Lord of beings, (still) by subjugating My Prakriti, I take birth by means of My own Maya.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.7 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, whenever there is a decline one virtue and increase of vice, then do I manifest Myself.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.8 For the protection of the pious, the destruction of the evil-doers, and establishing virtue, I manifest Myself in every age.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.9 He who thus knows truly the divine birth and actions of Mine does not get rirth after casting off the body. He attains Me, O Arjuna.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.10 Many who were devoid of attachment, fear and anger, who were absorbed in Me, who had taken refuge in Me, and were purified by the austerity of Knowledge, have attained My state.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.11 According to the manner in which they approach Me, I favour them in that very manner. O son of Partha, human beings follow My path in every way.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.12 Longing for the fruition of actions (of their rites and duties), they worship the gods here. For, in the human world, success from action comes ickly.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.13 The four castes have been created by Me through a classification of the gunas and duties. Even though I am the agent of that (act of classification), still know Me to be a non-agent and changeless.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.14 Actions do not taint Me; for Me there is no hankering for the results of actions. One who knows Me thus, does not become bound by actions.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.15 Having known thus, duties were performed even by the ancient seekers of Liberation. Thererfore you undertake action itself as was performed earlier by the ancient ones.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.16 Even the intelligent are confounded as to what is action and what is inaction. I shall tell you of that action by knowing which you will become free from evil.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.17 For there is something to be known even about action, and something to be known about prohibited action; and something has to be known about inaction. The true nature of action is inscrutable.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.18 He who finds inaction in action, and action in inaction, he is the wise one [Possessed of the knowledge of Brahman] among men; he is engaged in yoga and is a performer of all actions!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.19 The wise call him learned whose actions are all devoid of desires and their thougts, [Kama-sankalpa is variously translated as 'desires and purposes', 'plans and desires for results', 'hankering for desires', etc. But Sankarcarya shows sankalpa as the cause of kama. -Tr.] and whose actions have been burnt away by the fire of wisdom.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.20 Having given up attachment to the results of action, he who is ever-contented, dependent on nothing, he really does not do anything even though engaged in action.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.21 One who is without solicitation, who has the mind and organs under control, (and) is totally without possessions, he incurs no sin by performing actions merely for the (maintenance of the) body.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.22 Remaining satisfied with what comes unasked for, having transcended the dualities, being free from spite, and eipoised under success and failure, he is not bound even by performing actions.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.23 Of the liberated person who has got rid of attachment, whose mind is fixed in Knowledge, actions undertaken for a sacrifice get totally destroyed.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.24 The ladle is Brahman [Some translate as 'Brahman is the ladle৷৷.,' etc.-Tr.], the oblations is Brahman, the offering is poured by Brahman in the fire of Brahman. Brahman alone is to be reached by him who has concentration on Brahman as the objective [As an object to be known and attained. (Some translate brahma-karma-samadhina as, 'by him who sees Brahman in action'.)

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.25 Other yogis undertake sacrifice to gods alone, Others offer the Self, as a sacrifice by the Self itself, in the fire of Brahman.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.26 Others offer the organs, viz ear etc., in the fires of self-control. Others offer the objects, viz sound etc., in the fires of the organs.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.27 Others offer all the activities of the organs and the activities of the vital force into the fire of the yoga of sel-control which has been lighted by Knowledge.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.28 Similarly, others are performers of sacrifices through wealth, through austerity, through yoga, and through study and knowledge; others are ascetics with severe vows.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.29 Constantly practising control of the vital forces by stopping the movements of the outgoing and the incoming breaths, some offer as a sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming breath; while still others, the incoming breath in the outgoing breath.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.30 Others, having their food regulated, offer the vital forces in the vital forces. All of them are knowers of the sacrifice and have their sins destroyed by sacrifice.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.31 Those who partake of the nectar left over after a sacrifice, reach the eternal Brahman. This world ceases to exist for one who does not perform sacrifices. What to speak of the other (world), O best among the Kurus (Arjuna)!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.32 Thus, various kinds of sacrifices lie spread at the mouth of the Vedas. Know them all to be born of action. Knowing thus, you will become liberated.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Gambirananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.34 Know that through prostration, iniry and service. The wise ones who have realized the Truth will impart the Knowledge to you.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.35 Knowing which, O Pandava (Arjuna), you will not come under delusion again in this way, and through which you will see all beings without exception in the Self and also in Me.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.36 Even if you be the worst sinner among all sinners, still you will cross over all the wickedness with the raft of Knowledge alone.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.37 O Arjuna, as a blazing fire reduces pieces of wood to ashes, similarly the fire of Knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.38 Indeed, there is nothing purifying here comparable to Knowledge. One who has become perfected after a (long) time through yoga, realizes That by himself in his own heart.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.39 The man who has faith, is diligent and has control over the organs, attains Knowledge. Achieving Knowledge, one soon attains supreme Peace.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.40 One who is ignorant and faithless, and has a doubting mind perishes. Neither this world nor the next nor happiness exists for one who has a doubting mind.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.41 O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), actions do not bind one who has renounced actions through yoga, whose doubt has been fully dispelled by Knowledge, and who is not inadvertent.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 4.42 Therefore, O scion of the Bharata dyasty, take recourse to yoga and rise up, cutting asunder with the sword of Knowledge this doubt of your own in the heart, arising from ignorance.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.1 Arjuna said O Krsna, You praise renunciation of actions, and again, (Karma-) yoga. Tell me for certain that one which is better between these two.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.2 The Blessed Lord said Both renunciation of actions and Karma-yoga lead to Liberation. Between the two, Karma-yoga, however, excels over renunciation of actions.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.3 He who does not hate and does not crave should be known as a man of constant renunciation.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.4 The fools, not the learned ones, speak of Sankhya (the path of Knowledge) and (Karma-) yoga as different. Any one who properly resorts to even one (of them) gets the result of both.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.5 The State [Sthana (State) is used in the derivative sense of 'the place in which one remains established, and from which one does not become relegated'.] that is reached by the Sankhyas, that is reached by the yogis as well. He sees who sees Sankhya and yoga as one.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.6 But, O mighty-armed one, renunciation is hard to attain without (Karma-) yoga. The meditative man eipped with yoga attains Brahman without delay.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.7 Endowed with yoga, [i.e. devoted to the performance of the nitya and naimittika duties.] pure in mind, controlled in body, a coneror of the organs, the Self of the selves of all beings-he does not become tainted even while performing actions. [The construction of the sentence is this: When this person resorts to nitya and naimittika rites and duties as a means to the achievement of fully Illumination, and thus becomes fully enlightened, then, even when he acts through the apparent functions of the mind, organs, etc., he does not become afflected.]

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.8-5.9 Remaining absorbed in the Self, the knower of Reality should think, 'I certainly do not do anything', even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing, speaking, releasing, holding, opening and closing the eyes-remembering that the organs function in relation to the objects of the organs.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.8-5.9 Remaining absorbed in the Self, the knower of Reality should think, 'I certainly do not do anything', even while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, moving, sleeping, breathing, speaking, releasing, holding, opening and closing the eyes-remembering that the organs function in relation to the objects of the organs.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.10 One who acts by dedicating actions to Brahman and by renouncing attachment, he does not become polluted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not by water.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.11 By giving up attachment, the yogis undertake work merely through the body, mind, intellect and even the organs, for the purification of themselves.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.12 Giving up the result of work by becoming resolute in faith, one attains Peace arising from steadfastness. One who is lacking in resolute faith, being attached to the result under the impulsion of desire, becomes bound.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.13 The embodied man of self-control, having given up all actions mentally, continues happily in the town of nine gates, without doing or causing (others) to do anything at all.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.14 The Self does not create agentship or any objects (of desire) for anyone; nor association with the results of actions. But it is Nature that acts.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.15 The Omnipresent neither accepts anybody's sin nor even virtue. Knowledge remains covered by ignorance. Thery the creatures become deluded.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.16 But in the case of those of whom that ignorance of theirs becomes destroyed by the knowledge (of the Self), their Knowledge, like the sun, reveals that supreme Reality.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.17 Those who have their intellect absorbed in That, whose Self is That, who are steadfast in That, who have That as their supreme Goal-they attain the state of non-returning, their dirt having been removed by Knowledge.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.18 The learned ones look with eanimity on a Brahmana endowed with learning and humality, a cow, an elephant and even a dog as well as an eater of dog's meat.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.19 Here [i.e. even while living in the body.] itself is rirth conered by them whose minds are established on sameness. Since Brahman is the same (in all) and free from defects, therefore they are established in Brahman.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.20 A knower of Brahman, who is established in Brahman, should have his intellect steady and should not be deluded. He should not get delighted by getting what is desirable, nor become dejected by getting what is undesirable.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.21 With his heart unattached to external objects, he gets the bliss that is in the Self. With his heart absorbed in meditation on Brahman, he acires undecaying Bliss.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.22 Since enjoyments that result from contact (with objects) are verily the sources of sorrow and have a beginning and an end, (therefore) O son of Kunti, the wise one does not delight in them.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.23 One who can withstand here itself-before departing from the body-the impulse arising from desire and anger, that man is a yogi; he is happy.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.24 One who is happy within, whose pleasure is within, and who has his light only within, that yogi, having become Brahman, attains absorption in Brahman.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.25 The seers whose sins have been attenuated, who are freed from doubt, whose organs are under control, who are engaged in doing good to all beings, attain absorption in Brahman.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.26 To the monks who have control over their internal organ, who are free from desire and anger, who have known the Self, there is absorption in Brahman either way.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.27-5.28 Keeping the external objects outside, the eyes at the juncture of the eye-brows, and making eal the outgoing and incoming breaths that move through the nostrils, the contemplative who has control over his organs, mind and intellect should be fully intent on Liberation and free from desire, fear and anger. He who is ever is verily free.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.27-5.28 Keeping the external objects outside, the eyes at the juncture of the eye-brows, and making eal the outgoing and incoming breaths that move through the nostrils, the contemplative who has control over his organs, mind and intellect should be fully intent on Liberation and free from desire, fear and anger. He who is ever is verily free.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.29 One attains Peace by knowing Me who, as the great Lord of all the worlds, am the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, (and) who am the friend of all creatures.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.1 The Blessed Lord said He who performs an action which is his duty, without depending on the result of action, he is a monk and a yogi; (but) not (so in) he who does not keep a fire and is actionless.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.2 That which they call monasticism, know that to be Yoa, O Pandava, For, nobody who has not given up expectations can be a yogi.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.3 For the sage who wishes to ascend to (Dhyana-) yoga, action is said to be the means. For that person, when he has ascended to (Dhyana-)yoga, inaction alone is said to be the means.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.4 Verily, [Verily: This word emphasizes the fact that, since attachment to sense objects like sound etc. and to actions is an obstacle in the path of Yoga, therefore the removal of that obstruction is the means to its attainment.] when a man who has given up thought about everything does not get attached to sense-objects or acitons, he is then said to be established in Yoga.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.5 One should save oneself by oneself; one should not lower oneself. For oneself is verily one's onw friend; oneself is verily one's own enemy.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.6 Of him, by whom has been conered his very self by the self, his self is the friend of his self. But, for one who has not conered his self, his self itself acts inimically like an enemy.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.7 The supreme Self of one who has control over the aggregate of his body and organs, and who is tranil, becomes manifest. (He should be eipoised) [These words are supplied to complete the sentence.] in the midst of cold and heat, happiness and sorrow, as also honour and dishonour.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.8 One whose mind is satisfied with knowledge and realization, who is unmoved, who has his organs under control, is sadi to be Self-absorbed. The yogi treats eally a lump of earth, a stone and gold.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.9 He excels who has sameness of view with regard to a benefactor, a friend, a foe [Ari (foe) is one who does harm behind one's back.], a neutral, an arbiter, the hateful, [Dvesyah is one who openly hateful.] a relative, good people and even sinners.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.10 A yogi should constantly concentrate his mind by staying in a solitary place, alone, with mind and body controlled, free from expectations, (and) free from acisition.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.11 Having firmly established in a clean place his seat, neither too high nor too low, and made of cloth, skin and kusa-grass, placed successively one below the other;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.12 (and) sitting on that seat, he should concentrate his mind for the purification of the internal organ, making the mind one-pointed and keeping the actions of the mind and senses under control.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.13 Holding the body, head and neck erect and still, being steady, looking at the tip of his own nose-and not looking around;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.14 He should remain seated with a placid mind, free from fear, firm in the vow of a celibate, and with the mind fixed on Me by controlling it through concentration, having Me as the supreme Goal.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.15 Concentrating the mind thus for ever, the yogi of controlled mind achieves the Peace which culminates in Liberation and which abides in Me.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.16 But, O Arjuna, Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all; neither for one who habitually sleeps too long, nor surely for one who keeps awake.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.17 Yoga becomes a destroyer of sorrow of one whose eating and movements are regulated, whose effort in works is moderate, and whose sleep and wakefulness are temperate.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.18 A man who has become free from hankering for all desirable objects is then said to be Self-absorbed when the controlled mind rests in the Self alone.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.19 As a lamp kept in a windless place does not flicker, such is the simile thought of for the yogi whose mind is under control, and who is engaged in concentration on the Self.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.20 At the time when the mind restrained through the practice of Yoga gets withdrawn, and just when by seeing the Self by the self one remains contented in the Self alone [A.G. construes the word eva (certainly) with tusyati (remains contented).-Tr.];

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.21 When one experienece that absolute Blisss which can be intuited by the intellect and which is beyond the senses, and being established (thus) this person surely does not swerve from Reality;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.22 Obtaining which one does not think of any other acisition to be superior to that, and being established in which one is not perturbed even by great sorrow;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.23 One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga has to be practised with perservance and with an undepressed heart.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.24 By totally eschewing all desires which arise from thoughts, and restraining with the mind itself all the organs from every side;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.25 One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.26 (The yogi) should bring (this mind) under the subjugation of the Self Itself, by restraining it from all those causes whatever due to which the restless, unsteady mind wanders away.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.27 Supreme Bliss comes to this yogi alone whose mind has become perfectly tranil, whose (ality of) rajas has been eliminated, who has become identified with Brahman, and is taintless.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.28 By concentrating his mind constantly thus, the taintless yogi easily attains the absolute Bliss of contact with Brahman.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.29 One who has his mind Self-absorbed through Yoga, and who has the vision of sameness every-where, see this Self existing in everything, and every-thing in his Self.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.30 One who sees Me in everything, and sees all things in Me-I do not out of his vision, and he also is not lost to My vision.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.31 That yogi who, being established in unity, adores Me as existing in all things, he exist in Me-in whatever condition he may be.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.32 O Arjuna, that yogi is considered the best who judges what is happiness and sorrow in all beings by the same standard as he would apply to himself.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.33 Arjuna said O Madhusudana (Krsna), this Yoga that has been spoken of by You as sameness, I do not see its steady continuance, owing to the restlessness (of the mind).

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.34 For, O Krsna, the mind is unsteady, turbulent, strong and obstinate. I consider its control to be as greatly difficult as of the wind.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.35 The Blessed Lord said O mighty-armed one, undoubtedly the mind is untractable and restless. But, O son of Kunti, it is brought under control through practice and detachment.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.36 My conviction is that Yoga is difficult to be attained by one of uncontrolled mind. But it is possible to be attained through the (above) means by one who strives and has a controlled mind.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.37 Arjuna said O krsna, failing to achieve perfection in Yoga, what goal does one attain who, though possessed of faith, is not diligent and whose mind becomes deflected from Yoga?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: Swami Gambirananda did not comment on this sloka

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.39 O Krsna, You should totally eradicate this doubt of mine. For, none other than Yourself can be the dispeller of this doubt!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.40 The Blessed Lord said O Partha, there is certainly no ruin for him here or hereafter. For, no one engaged in good meets with a deplorable end, My son!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.41 Attaining the worlds of the righteous, and residing there for eternal years, the man fallen from Yoga is born in the house of the pious and the properous.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.42 Or he is born in the family of wise yogis [Persons possessing knowledge of Brahman. (S. concedes that some rare householders also can have this knowledge, and he cites the instances of Vasistha, Agastya, Janaka and Asvapati of olden days, and Vacaspati and the author of Khanada of recent times.)] only. Such a birth as is of this kind is surely more difficult to get in the world.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.43 There he becomes endowed with that wisdom acired in the previous body. and he strives more than before for perfection, O scion of the Kuru dynasty.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.44 For, by that very past practice, he is carried forward even in spite of himself! Even a seeker of Yoga transcends the result of the performance of Vedic rituals!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.45 However, the yogi, applying himself assiduously, becoming purified from sin and attaining perfection through many births, thery acheives the highest Goal.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.46 A yogi is higher than men of austerity; he is considered higher even than men of knowledge. The yogi is also higher than men of action. Therefore, O Arjuna, do you become a yogi.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 6.47 Even among all the yogis, he who adores Me with his mind fixed on Me and with faith,he is considered by Me to be the best of the yogis.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.1 The Blessed Lord said O Partha, hear how you, having the mind fixed on Me, practising the Yoga of Meditation and taking refuge in Me, will know Me with certainly and in fulness.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.2 I shall tell you in detail of this Knowledge which is combined with realization, [From the statement, 'jnasyasi, you will know', in the earlier verse, one may conclude that the Lord is speaking of indirect or theoretical knowledge. The word 'idam, this' rules out such a conclusion; and it has also been said that this Knowledge is 'savijnanam, combined with direct experienece, realization'; it is Consciousness.] after experience which there remains nothing else here to be known again.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.3 Among thousands of men a rare one endeavours for perfection. Even of the perfected ones who are diligent, one perchance knows Me in truth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.4 This Prakrti of Mine is divided eight-fold thus: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and also egoism.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.5 O mighty-armed one, this is the inferior (Prakrti). Know the other Prakrti of Mine which, however, is higher than this, which has taken the from of individual souls, and by which this world is uphelp.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.6 Understand thus that all things (sentient and insentient) have these as their source. I am the origin as also the end of the whole Universe.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.7 O Dhananjaya, there is nothing else whatsoever higher than Myself. All this is strung on Me like pearls on a string.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.8 O son of Kunti, I am the taste of water, I am the effulgence of the moon and the sun; (the letter) Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and manhood in men.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.9 I am also the sweet fragrance in the earth; I am the brillinace in the fire, and the life in all beings; and I am the austerity of the ascetics.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.10 O Partha, know Me to be the eternal Seed of all beings. I am the intellect of the intelligent, I am the courage of the courageous.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.11 And of the strong I am the strength which is devoid of passion and attachment. Among creatures I am desire which is not contrary to righteousness, O scion of the Bharata dyansty.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.12 Those things that indeed are made of (the ality of ) sattva, and those things that are made of (the ality of) rajas and tamas, know them to have sprung from Me alone. However, I am not in them; they are in Me!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.13 All this world, deluded as it is by these three things made of the gunas (alities), does not know Me who am transcendental to these and undecaying.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 7.14 Since this divine Maya of Mine which is constituted by the gunas is difficult to cross over, (therefore) those who take refuge in Me alone cross over this Maya.
