author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.2 The branches of that (Tree), extending down-wards and upwards, are strengthened by the alities and have sense-objects as their shoots. And the roots, which are followed by actions, spread down-wards in the human world [According to A.G. and M.S. manusya-loke means a body distinguished by Brahminhood etc.].

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.3 Its form is not perceived here in that way; nor its end, nor beginning, nor continuance, After felling this Peepul whose roots are well developed, with the strong sword of detachment-;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.4 Thereafter, that State has to be sought for, going where they do not return again: I take refuge in that Primeval Person Himself, from whom has ensued the eternal Manifestation.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.5 The wise ones who are free from pride and non-discrimination, who have conered the evil of association, [Hatred and love arising from association with foes and friends.] who are ever devoted to spirituality, completely free from desires, free from the dualities called happiness and sorrow, reach that undecaying State.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.6 Neither the sun nor the moon nor fire illumines That. That is My supreme Abode, reaching which they do not return.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.7 It is verily a part of Mine which, becoming the eternal individual soul in the region of living beings, draws (to itself) the organs which have the mind as their sixth, and which abide in Nature.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.8 When the master leaves it and even when he assumes a body, he departs taking these, as wind (carries away) odours from their receptacles.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.9 This one enjoys the objects by presiding over the ear, eyes, skin and tongue as also the nose and the mind.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.10 Persons who are diversely deluded do not see it even when it is leaving or residing (in this body), or experiencing, or in association with the alities. Those with the eye of knowledge see.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.11 And the yogis who are diligent see this one as existing in themselves. The non-discriminating ones who lack self-control do not see this one-though (they be) diligent.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.12 That light in the sun which illumines the whole world, that which is in the moon, and that which is in fire,-know that light to be Mine.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.13 And entering the earth I sustain the beings through (My) power; and nourish all the plants by becoming Soma [According to S. and most other translators, Soma means the moon.-Tr.] which is of the nature of sap.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.14 Taking the form of Vaisvanara and residing in the bodies of creatures, I, in association with Prana and Apana, digest the four kinds of food.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.15 And I am seated in the hearts of all. From Me are memory, knowledge and their loss. I alone am the object to be known through all the Vedas; I am also the originator of the Vedanta, and I Myself am the knower of the Vedas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.16 There are these two persons in the world-the mutable and the immutable. The mutable consists of all things; the one existing as Maya is called the immutable.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.17 But different is th supreme Person who is spoken of as the transcendental Self, who, permeating the three worlds, upholds (them), and is the imperisahble God.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.18 Since I am transcendental to the mutable and above even the immutable, hence I am well known in the world and in the Vedas as the supreme Person.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.19 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, he who, being free from delusion, knows Me the supreme Person thus, he is all-knowing and adores Me with his whole being.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 15.20 O sinless one, this most secret scripture has thus been uttered by Me. Understanding this, one becomes wise and has his duties fulfilled, O scion of the Bharata dynasty.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.1 The Blessed Lord said Fearlessness, purity of mind, persistence in knowledge and yoga, charity and control of the external organs, sacrifice, (scriptural) study, austerity and recititude;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.2 Non-injury, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, control of the internal organ, absence of vilification, kindness to creatures, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, freedom from restlessness;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.3 Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice, absence of haughtiness-these, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, are (the alties) of one born destined to have the divine nature.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.4 O son of Prtha, (the attributes) of one destined to have the demoniacal nature are religious ostentation, pride and haughtiness, [Another reading is abhimanah, self-conceit.-Tr.], anger as also rudeness and ignorance.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.5 The divine nature is the Liberation, the demoniacal is considered to be for inevitable bondage. Do not grieve, O son of Pandu! You are destined to have the divine nature.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.6 In this world there are are two (kinds of) creation of beings: the divine and the demoniacal. The divine has been spoken of elaborately. Hear about the demoniacal from Me, O son of Prtha.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.7 Neither do the demoniacal persons under-stand what is to be done and what is not to be done; nor does purity, or even good conduct or truthfulness exist in them.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.8 They say that the world is unreal, it has no basis, it is without a God. It is born of mutual union brought about by passion! What other (cause can there be)?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.9 Holding on to this view, (these people) who are of depraved character, of poor intellect, given to fearful actions and harmful, wax strong for the ruin of the world.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.10 Giving themselves up to insatiable passion, filled with vanity, pride and arrogance, adopting bad abjectives due to delusion, and having impure resolves, they engage in actions.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.11 Beset with innumerable cares which end (only) with death, holding that the enjoyment of desirable objects is the highest goal, feeling sure that this is all.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.12 Bound by hundreds of shackles in the form of hope, giving themselves wholly to passion and anger, they endeavour to amass wealth through foul means for the enjoyment of desirable objects.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.13 'This has been gained by me today; I shall acire this desired object. This is in hand; again, this wealth also will come to me.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.14 'That enemy has been killed by me, and I shall kill others as well. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am well-established, mighty and happy.'

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.15 'I am rich and high-born; who else is there similar to me? I shall perform sacrifices; I shall give, I shall rejoice,'-thus they are diversely deluded by non-discrimination.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.16 Bewildered by numerous thoughts, caught in the net of delusion, (and) engrossed in the enjoyment of desirable objects, they fall into a foul hell.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.17 Self-conceited, haughty, filled with pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices which are so in name only, with ostentation and regardless of the injunctions.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.18 Resorting to egotism, power, arrogance, passion and anger, hating Me in their own and others' bodies, (they become) [As the finite verb is missing in the verse, we have supplied 'they become'. S. adds the verb prabhavanti, wax strong, from verse 9, and constructs the last portion thus: '৷৷.the envious ones wax strond.' Following S. S., however, one may combine this verse with the preceding verse by taking 'perform sacrifices' as the finite verb.-Tr.'] envious by nature.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.19 I cast for ever those hateful, cruel, evil-doers in the worlds, the vilest of human beings, verily into the demoniacla classes.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.20 Being born among the demoniacal species in births after births, the foods, without ever reaching Me, O son of Kunti, attain conditions lower than that.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.21 This door of hell, which is the destroyer of the soul, is of three kinds-passion, anger and also greed. Therefore one should forsake these three.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.22 O son of Kunti, a person who is free from these three doors to darkness strives for the good of the soul. Thery he attains the highest Goal.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.23 Ignoring the precept of the scriptures, he who acts under the impulsion of passion,-he does not attain perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme Goal.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 16.24 Therefore, the scripture is your authority as regards the determination of what is to be done and what is not to be done. After understanding (your) duty as presented by scriptural injunction, you ought to perform (your duty) here.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.1 Arjuna said But, ['But' is used to present a standpoint distinct from the earlier ones understand from 16.23-4.-S.] O Krsna, what is the state [i.e., where do the rites undertaken by them end?] of those who, endued with faith, adore [Adore-perform sacrifices, distribute wealth etc. in honour of gods and others.] by ignoring the injunctions of the scriptures? Is it sattva, rajas or tamas?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.2 The Blessed Lord said That faith of the embodied beings, born of their own nature, is threefold-born of sattva, rajas and tamas. Hear about it.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.3 O scion of the Bharata dynasty, the faith of all beings is in accordance with their minds. This person is made up of faith as the dominant factor. He is verily what his faith is.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.4 Those having the sattva ality worship the gods; those having rajas, the demi-gods and ogres; and other people possessed of tamas worship ghosts and the hosts of spirits.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.5 Those persons who, given to ostentation and pride, and possessed of passion, attachment and strength, undertake severe austerities not sanctioned in the scriptures;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.6 (And who,) being non-discriminating, torture, all the organs in the body as also even Me who reside in the body,-know them as possessed of demoniacal conviction.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.7 Food also, which is dear to all, is of three kinds; and so also are sacrifices, austerity and charity. Listen to this classification of them.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.8 Foods that augment life, firmless of mind, strength, health, happiness and delight, and which are succulent, oleaginous, substantial and agreeable, are dear to one endowed with sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.9 Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and burning, and which production pain, sorrow and disease, are dear to one having rajas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.10 Food which is not properly cooked, lacking in essence, putrid and stale, and even ort and that which is unfit for sacrifice, is dear to one possessed of tamas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.11 That sacrifice which is in accordance with the injunctions, (and is) performed by persons who do not hanker after results, and with the mental conviction that it is surely obligatory, is done through sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.12 But that sacrifice which is performed having in veiw a result, as also for ostentation,-know that sacrifice to be done through rajas, O greatest among the descendants of Bharata.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.13 They declare that sacrifice as 'done through tamas' which is contrary to injunction, in which food is not distributed, in which mantras are not used, in which offerings are not made to priests, and which is devoid of faith.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.14 The worship of gods, twice-borns, venerable persons and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy and non-injury,-are said to be bodily austerity.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.15 That speech which causes no pain, which is true, agreeable and beneficial; as well as the practice of study of the scriptures,-is said to be austerity of speech.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.16 Tranillity of mind, gentleness, reticence, withdrawal of the mind, purity of heart,-these are what is called mental austerity.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.17 When that threefold austerity is undertaken with supreme faith by people who do not hanker after results and are self-controlled, they speak of it as born of sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.18 That austerity which is undertaken for earning a name, being honoured and worshipped, and also ostentatiously,-that is spoken of as born of rajas, belonging to this world, uncertain and transitory.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.19 That austerity which is undertaken with a foolish intent, by causing pain to oneself, or for the destruction of others-that is said to be born of tamas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.20 That gift is referred to as born of sattva which gift is given with the idea that it ought to be given, to one who will not serve in return, and at the (proper) place, (proper) time and to a (proper) person.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.21 But the gift which is given expecting reciprocation, or again, with a desire for its result, and which is given grudgingly,- that is considered to be born of rajas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.22 The gift which is made at an improper place and time, and to undeserving persons, without proper treatment and with disdain, is declared to be born of tamas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.23 'Om-tat-sat' ['Om, That, Existence': 'Om iti brahma, Om is Brahman' (Tai. 1.8.1); 'Tattvamasi, Thou art That' (Ch. 6.8.7); and 'Sadeva somya idamagra asit, This was Existence alone in the beginning, O amiable one' (Ch. 6.2.1)-in these texts Brahman is indicated by the words Om, tat, sat.]-this is considered to be the threefold designation of Brahman. The Brahmanas and Vedas and the sacrifices were ordanined by that in the days of yore.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.24 Therefore, acts of sacrifice, charity and austerity as prescribed through injunctions, of those who study and expound the Vedas, always commence after uttering the syllable Om.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.25 After (uttering) the word tat, acts of sacrifice and austerity as also the various acts of charity are performed without regard for results by persons aspiring for Liberation.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.26 This word sat is used with regard to (something) coming into being and with regard to (someone) becoming good. So also, O son of Prtha, the word sat is used with regard to an auspicious rite.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.27 And the steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and charity is spoken of as sat. And even the action meant for these is, verily, called as sat (good).

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 17.28 O son of Prtha, whatever is offered in sacrifice and given in charity, as also whatever austerity is undertakne or whatever is done without, faith, is said to be of on avail. And it is of no conseence after death, nor here.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.1 Arjuna said O mighty-armed Hrsikesa, O slayer of (the demon) Kesi, I want to know serverally the truth about sannyasa as also about tyaga.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.2 The Blessed Lord said The learned ones know sannyasa to be the giving up of actions done with a desire for reward. The adepts call the abandonment of the results of all works as tyaga.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.3 Some learned persons say that action, beset with evil (as it is), should be given up, and others (say) that the practice of sacrifice, charity and austertiy should not be given up.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.4 O the most excellent among the descendants of Bharata, hear from Me the firm conclusion regarding that tyaga. For, O greatest among men, tyaga has been clearly declared to be of three kinds.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.5 The practice of sacrifice, charity and austerity is not to be abandoned; it is surely to be undertaken. Sacrifice, charity and austerity are verily the purifiers of the wise.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.6 But even these actions have to be undertaken by renouncing attachment and (hankering for) results. This is My firm and best conclusion, O Parhta.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.7 The abandoning of daily obligatory acts (nityakamas) is not justifiable. Giving up that through delusion is declared to be based on tamas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.8 Whatever action one may relinish merely as being painful, from fear of physical suffering, he, having resorted to renunciation based on rajas, will surely not acire the fruits of renunciation.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.9 Whatever obligatory duty is performed just because it is a bounden duty, O Arjuna, by giving up attachment and the result as well,-that renunciation is considered to be based on sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.10 The man of renunciation who has become imbued with sattva, who is wise and freed from doubts, does not hate unbefitting action, nor does he become attached to befitting activity.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.11 Since it is not possible for one who holds on to a body to give up actions entirely, therefore he, on the other hand, who renounces results on actions is called a man of renunciation.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.12 The threefold results of actions-the undesirable, the desirable, and the mixed-accrues after death to those who do not resort to renunciation, but never to those who resort to monasticism.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.13 O mighty-armed one, learned from Me these [Another reading is etani.-Tr.] five factors for the accomplishment of all actions, which have been spoken of in the Vedanta in which actions terminate.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.14 The locus as also the agent, the different kinds of organs, the many and distinct activities, and, the divine is here the fifth.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.15 Whatever action a man performs with the body, speech and mind, be it just or its reverse, of it these five are the cuases.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.16 This being the case, anyone, who, owing to the imperfection of his intellect, perceives the absolute Self as the agent, that man does not perceive (properly), and has a perverted intellect.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.17 He who has not the feeling of egoism, whose intellect is not tainted, he does not kill, nor does he become bound-even by killing these creatures!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.18 Knowledge, the object the knowledge and the knower-this is the threefold inducement to action. The comprehension of actions comes under three heads-the instruments, the object and the subject.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.19 Knowledge, action and agent are stated in the teaching about the gunas to be only of three kinds according to the differences of the gunas. Hear about them also as they are.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.20 Know that knowledge to be originating from sattva through which one sees a single, undecaying, undivided Entity in all the diversified things.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.21 But know that knowledge to be originating from rajas which, amidst all things, apprehends the different entities of various kinds as distinct [As possessing distinct selves.].

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.22 But that (knowledge) is said to be born of tamas which is confined to one form as though it were all, which is irrational, not concern with truth and triivial.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.23 The daily obligatory action which is performed without attachment and without likes or dislikes by one who does not hanker for rewards, that is said to be born of sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.24 But that action is said to be born of rajas which is done by one desirous of results or by one who is egotistic, and which is highly strenuous.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.25 That action is said to be born of tamas which is undertaken out of delusion, (and) without consideration of its conseence, loss, harm and ability.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.26 [Ast. introduces this verse with 'Idanim kartrbhedah ucyate, Now is being stated the distinctions among the agents.'-Tr.] The agent who is free from attachment [Attachment to results or the idea of agentship.], not egotistic, endowed with fortitude and diligence, and unperturbed by success and failure is said to be possessed of sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.27 The agent who has attachment, who is desirous of the results of actions, covetous, cruel by nature, unclean and subject to joy and sorrow is declared to be possessed of rajas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.28 The agent who is unsteady, naive, unbending, deceitful, wicked, [A variant reading is naikrtikah.-Tr.] lazy, morose and procrastinating is said to be possessed of tamas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.29 O Dhananjaya, listen to the classification of the intellect as also of fortitude, which is threefold according to the gunas, while it is being stated elaborately and severally.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.30 O Partha, that intellect is born of sattva which understands action and withdrawal, duty and what is not duty, the sources of fear and fearlessness, and bondage and freedom.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.31 O Partha, that intellect is born of rajas with which one wrongly understands virtue and vice as also what ought to be done and ought not to be done.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.32 O Parhta, that intellect is born of tamas which, being covered by darkness, considers vice as virtue, and verily perceives all things contrary ot what they are.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.33 O Partha, the firmness that is unfailing through concentration, with which one restrains the functions of the mind, vital forces and the organs, that firmness is born of sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.34 But, O Partha, the firmness with which one holds on to righteousness, covetable things and wealth, being desirous of their fruits as the occasion for each arises, that firmness is born of rajas.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.35 That firmness is considered [Some editions read partha in place of mata (considered).-Tr.] to be born of tamas due to which a person with a corrupt intellect does not give up sleep, fear, sorrow, despondency as also sensuality.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.36 Now hear from Me, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, as regards the three kinds of joy: That in which one delights owing to habit, and certainly attains the cessation of sorrows; [S. and S.S. take the second line of this verse along with the next verse referring to sattvika happiness.-Tr.]

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.37 That which is like poison in the beginning, but comparable to nectar in the end, and which, arises from the purity of one's intellect-that joy is spoken of as born of sattva.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.38 That joy is referred to as born of rajas which, arising from the contact of the organs and (their) objects, is like nectar in the beginning, but like poison at the end.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.39 That joy is said to be born of tams which, both in the beginning and in the seel, is delusive to oneself and arises from sleep, laziness and inadvertence.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.40 There is no such entity in the world or, again, among the gods in heaven, which can be free from these three gunas born of Nature.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.41 O scorcher of enemies, the duties of the Brahmanas, the Ksatriyas and the Vaisyas, as also of the Sudras have been fully classified according to the gunas born from Nature.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.42 The natural duties of the Brahmanas are the control of the internal and external organs, austerity, purity, forgiveness, straightforwardness, knowledge as also wisdom [Knowledge refers to the understanding of subjects presented by the scriptures; wisdom means making them matters of one's own experience.] and faith.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.43 The natural duties of the Ksatriyas are heroism, boldness, fortitude, capability, and also not retreating from battle, generosity and lordliness.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.44 The natural duties of the Vaisyas are agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade. Of the Sudras, too, the natural duty is in the form of service.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 5.10 One who acts by dedicating actions to Brahman and by renouncing attachment, he does not become polluted by sin, just as a lotus leaf is not by water.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.46 A human being achieves success by adoring through his own duties Him from whom is the origin of creatures, and by whom is all this pervaded.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.47 One's own duty, (though) defective, is superior to another's duty well performed. By performing a duty as dictated by one's own nature, one does not incur sin.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.48 O son of Kunti, one should not give up the duty to which one is born, even though it be faulty. For all undertakings are surrounded with evil, as fire is with smoke.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.49 He whose intellect remains unattached to everything, who has conered his internal organs and is desireless, attains through monasticism the supreme perfection consisting in the state of one free from duties.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.50 Understand for certain from Me, in brief indeed, O son of Kunti, that process by which one who has achieved success attains Brahman, which is the supreme consummation of Knowledge.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.51 Being endowed with a pure intellect, and controlling oneself with fortitude, rejecting the objects-beginning from sound [Sound, touch, form and colour, taste and smell.-Tr.], and eliminating attachment and hatred;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.52 One who resorts to solitude, eats sparingly, has speech, body and mind under control, to whom meditation and concentration are ever the highest (duty), and who is possessed of dispassion;

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.53 (That person,) having discarded egotism, force, pride, desire, anger and superfluous possessions, free from the idea of possession, and serene, is fit for becoming Brahman.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.54 One who has become Brahman and has attained the blissful Self does not grieve or desire. Becoming the same towards all beings, he attains supreme devotion to Me.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.55 Through devotion he knows Me in reality, as to what and who I am. Then, having known Me in truth, he enters (into Me) immediately after that (Knowledge).

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.56 Ever engaging even in all actions, one to whom I am the refuge, attains the eternal, immutable State through My grace.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.57 Mentally surrendering all actions to Me and accepting Me as the supreme, have your mind ever fixed on Me by resorting to the concentration of your intellect.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.58 Having your mind fixed on Me, you will cross over all difficulties through My grace. If, on the other hand, you do not listen out of egotism, you will get destroyed.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.59 That you think 'I shall not fight', by relying on egotism,-vain is this determination of yours. (Your) nature impel you!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.60 Being bound by your own duty born of nature, O son of Kunti, you, being helpless, will verily do that which you do not wish to do owing to indiscrimination.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.61 O Arjuna, the Lord resides in the region of the heart of all creatures, revolving through Maya all the creatures (as though) mounted on a machine!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.62 Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, O scion of the Bharata dynasty. Through His grace you will attain the supreme Peace and the eternal Abode.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.63 To you has been imparted by Me this knowledge [Derived in the instrumental sense of 'means of knowledge'; i.e. the scripture Gita.] which is moe secret than any secret. Pondering over this as a whole, do as you like.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.64 Listen again to My highest utterance which is the profoundest of all. Since you are ever dear to Me, therefore I shall speak what is beneficial to you.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.65 Have your mind fixed on Me, be My devotee, be a sacrificer to Me and bow down to Me. (Thus) you will come to Me alone. (This) truth do I pormise to you. (For) you are dear to Me.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.66 Abandoning all forms of rites and duties, take refuge in Me alone. I sahll free you from all sins. (Therefore) do not grieve.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.67 This (that I have taught) you should not ever be taught to one who is devoid of austerities and to one who is not a devotee; also, neither to one who does not render service, nor as well to one who cavils at Me.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.68 He who, entertaining supreme devotion to Me, will speak of this highest secret, to My devotees will without doubt reach Me alone.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.69 And as compared with him, none else among human beings is the best accomplisher of what is dear to Me. Moreover, nor will there be anyone else in the world dearer to Me than he.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.70 And he who will study this sacred conversation between us two, which is conducive to virtue, by him I shall be adored through the Sacrifice in the form of Knowledge. This is My judgement.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.71 Any man who, being reverential and free from cavilling, might even hear (this), he too, becoming free, shall attain the blessed worlds of those who perform virtuous deeds.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.72 O Partha, has this been listened to by you with a one-pointed mind? O Dhananjaya, has your delusion caused by ignorance been destroyed?

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.73 Arjuna said O Acyuta, (my) delusion has been destroyed and memory has been regained by me through Your grace. I stand with my doubt removed; I shall follow Your instruction.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.74 Sanjaya said I thus heard this conversation of Vasudeva and of the great-souled Partha, which is unie and makes one's hair stand on end.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.75 Through the favour of Vyasa I heard this secret concerning the supreme Yoga from Krsna, the Lord of yogas, while He Himself was actually speaking!

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.76 And, O king, while repeatedly remembering this unie, sacred dialogue between Kesava and Arjuna, I rejoice every moment.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.77 O king, repeatedly recollecting that greatly extraordinary form of Hari, I am struck with wonder. And I rejoice again and again.

author: Swami Gambirananda
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content: 18.78 Where there is Krsna, the Lord of yogas, and where there is Partha, the wielder of the bow, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and unfailing prudence. Such is my conviction.

author: Rāmānuja
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
1.1 - 1.19 Dhrtarastra said - Sanjaya said Duryodhana, after viewing the forces of Pandavas protected by Bhima, and his own forces protected by Bhisma conveyed his views thus to Drona, his teacher, about the adeacy of Bhima's forces for conering the Kaurava forces and the inadeacy of his own forces for victory against the Pandava forces. He was grief-stricken within.
Observing his (Duryodhana's) despondecny, Bhisma, in order to cheer him, roared like a lion, and then blowing his conch, made his side sound their conchs and kettle-drums, which made an uproar as a sign of victory. Then, having heard that great tumult, Arjuna and Sri Krsna the Lord of all lords, who was acting as the charioteer of Arjuna, sitting in their great chariot which was powerful enough to coner the three worlds; blew their divine conchs Srimad Pancajanya and Devadatta. Then, both Yudhisthira and Bhima blew their respective conchs separately. That tumult rent asunder the hearts of your sons, led by Duryodhana. The sons of Dhrtarastra then thought, 'Our cause is almost lost now itself.' So said Sanjaya to Dhrtarastra who was longing for their victory.
Sanjaya said to Dhrtarastra: Then, seeing the Kauravas, who were ready for battle, Arjuna, who had Hanuman, noted for his exploit of burning Lanka, as the emblem on his flag on his chariot, directed his charioteer Sri Krsna, the Supreme Lord-who is overcome by parental love for those who take shelter in Him who is the treasure-house of knowledge, power, lordship, energy, potency and splendour, whose sportive delight brings about the origin, sustentation and dissolution of the entire cosmos at His will, who is the Lord of the senses, who controls in all ways the senses inner and outer of all, superior and inferior - by saying, 'Station my chariot in an appropriate place in order that I may see exactly my enemies who are eager for battle.'

content:
1.26 - 1.47 Arjuna said - Sanjaya said Sanjaya continued: The high-minded Arjuna, extremely kind, deeply friendly, and supremely righteous, having brothers like himself, though repeatedly deceived by the treacherous attempts of your people like burning in the lac-house etc., and therefore fit to be killed by him with the help of the Supreme Person, nevertheless said, 'I will not fight.'
He felt weak, overcome as he was by his love and extreme compassion for his relatives. He was also filled with fear, not knowing what was righteous and what unrighteous. His mind was tortured by grief, because of the thought of future separation from his relations. So he threw away his bow and arrow and sat on the chariot as if to fast to death.

author: Rāmānuja
alignmentStatus: first review verified (google/gemini-3.8-flash); second review pending
content:
2.9 - 2.10 Sanjaya said Thus, the Lord, the Supreme Person, introduced the Sastra regarding the self for the sake of Arjuna - whose natural courage was lost due to love and compassion in a misplaced situation, who thought war to be unrighteous even though it was the highest duty for warriors (Ksatriyas), and who took refuge in Sri Krsna to know what his right duty was -, thinking that Arjuna's delusion would not come to an end except by the knowledge of the real nature of the self, and that war was an ordained duty here which, when freed from attachment to fruits, is a means for self-knowledge. Thus, has it been said by Sri Yamunacarya: 'The introduction to the Sastra was begun for the sake of Arjuna, whose mind was agitated by misplaced love and compassion and by the delusion that righteousness was unrighteousness, and who took refuge in Sri Krsna.'
The Supreme Person spoke these words as if smiling, and looking at Arjuna, who was thus overcome by grief resulting from ignorance about the real nature of the body and the self, but was nevertheless speaking about duty as if he had an understanding that the self is distinct from the body, and while he (Arjuna), torn between contradictory ideas, had suddenly become inactive standing between the two armies that were getting ready to fight. Sri Krsna said, as if in ridicule, to Arjuna the words beginning with, 'There never was a time when I did not exist' (II. 12), and ending with 'I will release you from all sins; grieve not!' (XVIII. 66) - which have for their contents the real nature of the self, of the Supreme Self, and of the paths of work (Karma), knowledge (Jnana) and devotion (Bhakti) which constitute the means for attaining the highest spiritual fulfilment.
